'''Marcus Fraser''' (born 23 June 1994) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for {{Scottish football updater|StMirren}} club [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].

==Career==
===Celtic===
Raised in [[Bishopbriggs]],<ref name=foes>[https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/1568150/fraser-and-chalmers-to-be-friendly-foes-in-highland-derby/ Marcus Fraser and Joe Chalmers to be friendly foes in Highland derby] Press and Journal, 22 September 2018</ref> Fraser joined [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] when he was eight years old, progressing through the youth ranks signing a three-year professional contract in the summer of 2010.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.kirkintilloch-herald.co.uk/sport/football/marcus_is_a_rising_star_for_celtic_in_spain_1_1565551 | title=Marcus is a rising star for Celtic in Spain... | publisher=Kirkintilloch Herald | date=8 April 2011 | accessdate=3 November 2011}}</ref> Whilst a member of Celtic's under-19 squad,<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.celticfc.net/team_u19s | title=U19s *️⃣ The Players | publisher=[[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] | accessdate=3 November 2011 | url-status=dead | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110902004237/http://www.celticfc.net/team_u19s | archivedate=2 September 2011 | df=dmy-all }}</ref> he was called up to the first team for a friendly match against [[Athletic Bilbao]] on 26 March 2011.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.celticfc.net/matchstats.php?fid=179&date=2011-03-26 | title=Athletico Bilbao 0 v 0 Celtic | publisher=[[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] | date=26 March 2011 | accessdate=3 November 2011 | url-status=dead | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110423132354/http://www.celticfc.net/matchstats.php?fid=179&date=2011-03-26 | archivedate=23 April 2011 | df=dmy-all }}</ref> He made his debut the following season, on 3 November 2011, in a 3–1 win against [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Rennes]] in the [[UEFA Europa League]], coming on as a substitute at half time and playing in the centre of defence.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/15472980.stm | title=Celtic 3–1 Rennes | publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation | work=BBC Sport | date=3 November 2011 | access-date=3 November 2011}}</ref> Fraser made his first start for Celtic in a [[Scottish Premier League]] match against [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] on 9 February 2013.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21311327|title = Inverness CT 1-3 Celtic|work = BBC Sport}}</ref>

On 12 September 2014, Fraser joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Cowdenbeath F.C.|Cowdenbeath]] on loan.<ref>{{cite web|title=Marcus Fraser joins Cowdenbeath on loan|url=http://www.celticfc.net/news/6651|publisher=Celtic F.C.|last=Henderson|first=Mark|date=12 September 2014|accessdate=17 September 2014}}</ref> He was released by Celtic in January 2015.<ref name = "ross co">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30936407 |first=Martin |last=Dowden |title=Ross County sign defender Marcus Fraser |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=22 January 2015 |access-date=22 January 2015}}</ref>

===Ross County===
Fraser immediately signed for [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]].<ref name = "ross co"/> He made his debut for the Highland side on 24 January 2015, in a 1–0 defeat at home to Celtic.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ross County 0-1 Celtic: Hoops move three clear at top of Premiership |url=http://sport.stv.tv/football/clubs/celtic/307778-ross-county-0-1-celtic-hoops-move-three-clear-at-top-of-premiership/ |publisher=STV |work=STV Sport|date=24 January 2015|accessdate=17 March 2015}}</ref> On 17 March 2015, Fraser signed a new contract to keep him at Ross County until 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31920675 |title=Ross County: Marcus Fraser wins contract extension|publisher=BBC |work=BBC Sport|date=17 March 2015 |access-date=9 September 2015}}</ref>
A year later he signed a further two-year extension, keeping him under contract until summer 2019.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news/archive/marcus-fraser-signed/ |title=Signing News Marcus Fraser agrees 2 year contract extension|publisher=Ross County FC |work=Ross County FC Website|date=11 February 2016 |accessdate=25 January 2017}}</ref>

In June 2018, after [[Andrew Davies (footballer)|Andrew Davies]] left the club, Fraser became the new captain;<ref name=foes/> he went on to lift the [[2018-19 Scottish Championship|Scottish Championship]] and [[2019 Scottish Challenge Cup Final|Scottish Challenge Cup]]<ref name=scc18>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47622909|title=SCOTTISH CHALLENGE CUP - FINAL|access-date=27 October 2021|website=www.bbc.co.uk|date=23 March 2019|first=Eilidh|last=Davies}}</ref> as Ross County were promoted back to the [[Scottish Premiership]] after being relegated a year earlier.<ref name=champ19/>

On 5 June 2020, Fraser rejected a new contract at Ross County and left the club after five-and-a-half years and making 195 appearances.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/52934427|title=Ross County: Captain Marcus Fraser leaves after rejecting contract|publisher=Ross County FC |work=BBC Sport|date=5 June 2020 |accessdate=5 June 2020}}</ref>

===St Mirren===
On 28 July 2020, Fraser signed a one-year deal with [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53568061|title=Marcus Fraser: St Mirren sign former Ross County captain |work=BBC Sport |date=28 July 2020 |accessdate=28 July 2020}}</ref> In May 2021, he signed a two-year extension to remain at the club until the summer of 2023.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/3978-marcus-fraser-agrees-contract-extension|title=Marcus Fraser agrees contract extension |work=www.stmirren.com |date=7 May 2021 |accessdate=2 May 2022}}</ref>

Fraser opened the scoring after just two minutes in the [[2025 Scottish League Cup final]], as St Mirren ran out 3–1 winners against his former club Celtic.<ref name=SLCwin /> It was the club's first major trophy in 12 years.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/soccer/arid-41760014.html|title=Wilfried Nancy's nightmare start continues as St Mirren stun Celtic to land League Cup|first=Gavin|last=McCafferty|date=14 December 2025|website=Irish Examiner}}</ref>

===International===
Fraser represented Scotland at under-16, under-17, under-18, under-19 and under-21 levels.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=823&playerID=63726&CFID=2223824&CFTOKEN=22933570 | title=Marcus Fraser Scotland Profile | publisher=Scottish Football Association | accessdate=3 November 2011}}</ref>

'''Drey Jermaine Wright''' (born 30 April 1995) is an English professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[right-back]] or [[right winger]]. He plays for {{Scottish football updater|Dundee}} club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].

The son of former [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]] and [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] midfielder [[Jermaine Wright]], Wright progressed through the [[Colchester United F.C. Under-23s and Academy|Academy]] at [[Colchester United F.C.|Colchester United]] before he made his first-team debut in 2012. He made over 150 career appearances for Colchester before leaving to join [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] in May 2018. After two seasons with [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]], Wright returned to St Johnstone in 2022 for another three seasons.

==Career==
===Colchester United===
Born in [[Greenwich]], London,<ref name="FS"/> Wright is the son of former [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]] and [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] midfielder [[Jermaine Wright]], and brother to fellow footballer [[Diaz Wright]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Waldron |first1=Jonathan |date=25 July 2012 |title=Hot prospect Wright eager for more first-team action with U's |url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/sport/colchesterunited/9835541.Hot_prospect_Wright_eager_for_more_first_team_action_with_U_s/ |newspaper=Daily Gazette |location=Colchester |access-date=14 August 2012 }}</ref> A rapid winger who progressed through the [[Colchester United F.C. Under-23s and Academy|Academy]] at [[Colchester United F.C.|Colchester United]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cu-fc.com/team/player-profile/drey-wright/17 |title=Drey Wright |publisher=Colchester United FC |access-date=5 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150121191156/http://www.cu-fc.com/team/player-profile/drey-wright/17 |archive-date=21 January 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Wright featured for the Colchester first-team in the [[2011–12 Colchester United F.C. season|2011–12]] pre-season campaign, scoring in a 6–2 friendly win over [[Whitton United F.C.|Whitton United]] on 27 July 2011 for a youthful U's side.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Waldron |first1=Jonathan |date=27 July 2011 |title=Gilbey scores four in U's rout |url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/sport/colchesterunited/9163710.Gilbey_scores_four_in_U_s_rout/ |newspaper=Daily Gazette |location=Colchester |access-date=5 February 2015 }}</ref> He mostly featured for the youth and reserve sides throughout the season, alongside appearances in the [[Essex Senior Cup]]. He netted in their 4–0 semi-final win against [[Concord Rangers F.C.|Concord Rangers]] on 23 February 2012 to earn a place in the final.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Waldron |first1=Jonathan |date=23 February 2012 |title=Bond hat-trick helps U's book final place |url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/sport/colchesterunited/9548936.Bond_hat_trick_helps_U_s_book_final_place/ |newspaper=Daily Gazette |location=Colchester |access-date=5 February 2015 }}</ref> He featured in the final held against [[Canvey Island F.C.|Canvey Island]] on 17 April, a game in which Colchester were defeated 1–0.<ref>{{cite news |date=17 April 2012 |title=Rob is Gulls' King after late winner |url=http://www.gazette-news.co.uk/archive/2012/04/17/9653192.Rob_is_Gulls____King_after_late_winner/ |newspaper=Daily Gazette |location=Colchester |access-date=5 February 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20150210071750/http://www.gazette-news.co.uk/archive/2012/04/17/9653192.Rob_is_Gulls____King_after_late_winner/ |archive-date=10 February 2015  }}</ref> He then scored in the reserve side's penultimate game of the campaign on 24 April in a 2–1 win against [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Waldron |first1=Jonathan |date=24 April 2012 |title=U's reserves edge closer to the title |url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/sport/colchesterunited/9667270.U_s_reserves_edge_closer_to_the_title/ |newspaper=Daily Gazette |location=Colchester |access-date=5 February 2015 }}</ref> Despite a defeat to [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]] in the final game, he helped the side claim the last-ever [[The Football Combination|Football Combination North Division]] title on 1 May.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Waldron |first1=Jonathan |date=1 May 2012 |title=U's reserves win title despite Hatters defeat |url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/sport/colchesterunited/9680980.U_s_reserves_win_title_despite_Hatters_defeat/ |newspaper=Daily Gazette |location=Colchester |access-date=5 February 2015 }}</ref>

====2012–13 season====
In May 2012, after just one year of his apprenticeship and on the back of his success with the club's reserve side, Wright signed a two-year professional development contract with Colchester alongside fellow academy products [[Bradley Hamilton]], Ryan Melaugh, [[Tosin Olufemi]] and Shaun Phillips.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Waldron |first1=Jonathan |date=10 May 2012 |title=U's quartet sign new contracts |url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/sport/colchesterunited/9699364.U_s_quartet_sign_new_contracts/ |newspaper=Daily Gazette |location=Colchester |access-date=14 August 2012 }}</ref> Wright featured in the first-team preparations for the [[2012–13 Colchester United F.C. season|2012–13]] season, with Colchester manager [[John Ward (footballer, born 1951)|John Ward]] saying that "it doesn't really surprise me" that both Wright and teammate [[Alex Gilbey]] have made strides towards first-team football.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Waldron |first1=Jonathan |date=13 August 2012 |title=Ward not surprised by in-form Wright's progress |url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/sport/9870234.Ward_not_surprised_by_in_form_Wright_s_progress/ |newspaper=Daily Gazette |location=Colchester |access-date=5 February 2015 }}</ref> Ward then handed Wright his professional debut in the [[EFL Cup|League Cup]] tie against [[Yeovil Town F.C.|Yeovil Town]] on 14 August, the season's opening game. Wright started the match and played for 58 minutes before being replaced by [[Karl Duguid]] in the 3–0 defeat at [[Huish Park]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19159735 |title=Yeovil 3–0 Colchester |date=14 August 2012 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=14 August 2012 }}</ref> He was drafted into the squad at the last minute following [[Freddie Sears]]' withdrawal, but earned praise from his manager despite being forced to play first-team football prematurely.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Waldron |first1=Jonathan |date=15 August 2012 |title=Drey showed the Wright stuff |url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/sport/9875129.Drey_showed_the_Wright_stuff/ |newspaper=Daily Gazette |location=Colchester |access-date=5 February 2015 }}</ref> His father, [[Jermaine Wright|Jermaine]], said he was "proud to see my son out there playing" and that "he plays with a smile on his face and he loves playing with the first team".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Waldron |first1=Jonathan |date=16 February 2012 |title=Former Ipswich star Jermaine is proud of son Drey |url=http://www.gazette-news.co.uk/sport/9876817.Former_Ipswich_star_Jermaine_is_proud_of_son_Drey/ |newspaper=Daily Gazette |location=Colchester |access-date=5 February 2015 }}</ref> He then made his first [[EFL League One|League One]] appearance for the club, coming on as a 79th-minute substitute for [[Clinton Morrison]] in Colchester's 2–2 home draw with [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]] on 21 August.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19252494 |title=Colchester 2–2 Portsmouth |date=21 August 2012 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=5 February 2015 }}</ref>

On 28 August, Wright's cross for [[Freddie Ladapo]]'s goal in their [[Professional Development League]] Two match against [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]] was enough to hand Colchester their first-ever win in the newly established under-21 league format.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Waldron |first1=Jonathan |date=28 August 2012 |title=Ladapo strike gives U's first under-21 victory |url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/sport/9895888.Ladapo_strike_gives_U_s_first_under_21_victory/ |newspaper=Daily Gazette |location=Colchester |access-date=5 February 2015 }}</ref> He scored his first professional goal on his first league start on Boxing Day in a 3–1 home defeat to [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]], in which he played the full 90 minutes.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20779264 |title=Colchester 1–3 Brentford |date=26 December 2012 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=27 December 2012 }}</ref> Manager [[Joe Dunne]] enthused that "Drey Wright was outstanding" and "had an exceptional full debut and showed his strength".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Waldron |first1=Jonathan |date=27 December 2012 |title=Dunne hails U's young guns |url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/sport/10129854.Dunne_hails_U_s_young_guns/ |newspaper=Daily Gazette |location=Colchester |access-date=5 February 2015 }}</ref>

In March 2013, Wright was shortlisted for the League Football Education ' League One Apprentice of the Year' award, nominated alongside [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]]'s George Willis and eventual winner [[Luke James (footballer)|Luke James]] of [[Hartlepool United F.C.|Hartlepool United]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-league.co.uk/flawards/news/20130324/james-is-lfe-apprentice-of-the-year-for-league-1_2293338_3116282 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130928091637/http://www.football-league.co.uk/flawards/news/20130324/james-is-lfe-apprentice-of-the-year-for-league-1_2293338_3116282 |archive-date=28 September 2013 |title=James is LFE Apprentice of the Year for League 1 |publisher=The Football League |date=24 March 2013 |access-date=29 March 2013 }}</ref> Wright ended his first professional season with 23 first-team appearances, having scored three goals,<ref name="Games played by Drey Wright in 2012/2013">{{Soccerbase season|65501|2012|name=Drey Wright|accessdate=9 February 2015}}</ref> and was rewarded at the club's annual end of season awards evening on his 18th birthday, earning the Colchester United 'Young Player of the Year' accolade ahead of [[Sam Walker (footballer)|Sam Walker]] and [[Gavin Massey]].<ref name="YPOTY"/>

====2013–14 season====
With one year remaining on his contract, Wright signed a two-year extension on 26 July 2013 to keep him with the club until summer 2016.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Waldron |first1=Jonathan |date=26 July 2013 |title=Wright pens new U's deal |url=http://www.gazette-news.co.uk/sport/10576068.Wright_pens_new_U_s_deal/ |newspaper=Daily Gazette |location=Colchester |access-date=9 February 2015 }}</ref> He was brought on as a substitute in the season's opening game on 3 August in a 1–0 win at [[Gillingham F.C.|Gillingham]], setting up [[Andy Bond (footballer)|Andy Bond]] to score the 88th-minute winner.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Waldron |first1=Jonathan |date=3 August 2013 |title=Bond scores dramatic late winner to give U's opening day win |url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/sport/10591026.Bond_scores_dramatic_late_winner_to_give_U_s_opening_day_win/ |newspaper=Daily Gazette |location=Colchester |access-date=9 February 2015 }}</ref>

A calf strain left Wright out of action in early September,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Waldron |first1=Jonathan |date=4 September 2013 |title=U's facing injury crisis |url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/sport/10653703.U_s_facing_injury_crisis/ |newspaper=Daily Gazette |location=Colchester |access-date=9 February 2015 }}</ref> but he recovered in time to make his first start of the season in their 2–0 away defeat to [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]] on 8 September.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23918802 |title=Coventry 2–0 Colchester |date=8 September 2013 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=8 September 2013 }}</ref> Having undergone a knee operation in October 2013, Wright returned to light training with the squad in February 2014, having not featured since 14 September 2013 in the U's 2–2 draw with [[Bradford City A.F.C.|Bradford City]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Waldron |first1=Jonathan |date=4 February 2014 |title=Wright on the road to recovery |url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/sport/10986006.Wright_on_the_road_to_recovery/ |newspaper=Daily Gazette |location=Colchester |access-date=7 February 2014 }}</ref> He continued his comeback from injury on 6 March when he played for 60 minutes in Colchester's [[Essex Senior Cup]] semi-final defeat to [[Concord Rangers F.C.|Concord Rangers]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Waldron |first1=Jonathan |date=7 March 2014 |title=Young U's side beaten in Essex Senior Cup semi-final |url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/sport/11060699.Young_U_s_side_beaten_in_Essex_Senior_Cup_semi_final/ |newspaper=Daily Gazette |location=Colchester |access-date=9 February 2015 }}</ref> Manager Joe Dunne then announced that he was looking to loan Wright to another club to find first-team action elsewhere to aid his recovery process.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Waldron |first1=Jonathan |date=11 March 2014 |title=U's could allow Wright to leave on loan |url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/sport/11067786.U_s_could_allow_Wright_to_leave_on_loan/ |newspaper=Daily Gazette |location=Colchester |access-date=9 February 2015 }}</ref> However, Wright made his first appearance for the first-team in almost seven months as a substitute for [[David Wright (English footballer)|David Wright]] in the U's 2–0 away defeat to [[Peterborough United F.C.|Peterborough United]] on 2 April.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Waldron |first1=Jonathan |date=3 April 2015 |title=Drey's on the Wright track for U's |url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/sport/11125580.Drey_s_on_the_Wright_track_for_U_s/ |newspaper=Daily Gazette |location=Colchester |access-date=9 February 2015 }}</ref> Wright finished his injury-blighted campaign with 13 appearances.<ref name="Games played by Drey Wright in 2013/2014">{{Soccerbase season|65501|2013|name=Drey Wright|accessdate=9 February 2015}}</ref>

====2014–15 season====
After starting Colchester's first game of the season at home to [[Oldham Athletic A.F.C.|Oldham Athletic]] on 9 August 2014, Wright suffered a recurrence of his knee injury, which forced him out of much of last season. He was withdrawn after 64 minutes and replaced by [[Dominic Vose]] in the 2–2 draw.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28646626 |title=Colchester 2–2 Oldham |date=9 August 2014 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=9 February 2015 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Waldron |first1=Jonathan |date=12 August 2014 |title=U's reluctant to put timescale on Wright recovery |url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/sport/11403726.U_s_reluctant_to_put_timescale_on_Wright_recovery/ |newspaper=Daily Gazette |location=Colchester |access-date=9 February 2015 }}</ref> He returned to first-team action for the first time in six weeks, and for the first time under new manager [[Tony Humes]], on 20 September as an 84th-minute substitute for Gavin Massey in a 0–0 home draw with Bradford City.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Waldron |first1=Jonathan |date=20 September 2014 |title=U's play out goal-less draw with Bradford |url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/sport/11486636.U_s_play_out_goal_less_draw_with_Bradford/ |newspaper=Daily Gazette |location=Colchester |access-date=9 February 2015 }}</ref>

Wright announced his return to full fitness in late September following his return to the first-team,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Waldron |first1=Jonathan |date=24 September 2014 |title=Wright happy to be back in the fray for U's |url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/sport/11492065.Wright_happy_to_be_back_in_the_fray_for_U_s/ |newspaper=Daily Gazette |location=Colchester |access-date=9 February 2015 }}</ref> and then scored his first goal of the season, and his first for the club in 18 months, with the opener in Colchester's 3–3 [[EFL Trophy|Football League Trophy]] draw with [[Gillingham F.C.|Gillingham]] on 7 October.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Waldron |first1=Jonathan |date=7 October 2014 |title=U's knocked out of JPT on penalties |url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/sport/11520264.U_s_knocked_out_of_JPT_on_penalties/ |newspaper=Daily Gazette |location=Colchester |access-date=9 February 2015 }}</ref> Wright then limped out of the under-21 Development Squad's 5–0 defeat at home to [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]] on 14 October with another recurrence of his knee injury.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Waldron |first1=Jonathan |date=14 October 2014 |title=Injury worry over Wright as U's under-21s are beaten |url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/sport/11533130.Injury_worry_over_Wright_as_U_s_under_21s_are_beaten/ |newspaper=Daily Gazette |location=Colchester |access-date=9 February 2015 }}</ref> As a result of the injury, Wright was ruled out for the rest of the season with [[cruciate ligament]] damage.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Marston |first1=Carl |date=23 October 2014 |title=Colchester United winger Drey Wright ruled out for the season |url=http://www.greenun24.co.uk/colchester-united/colchester_united_winger_drey_wright_ruled_out_for_the_season_1_3818182 |newspaper=Green'Un |location=Ipswich |access-date=25 October 2014 }}</ref>

====2015–16 season====
Wright returned to first-team action on 11 August 2015 as a second-half substitute during Colchester's 1–0 League Cup defeat to [[Reading F.C.|Reading]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33769253 |title=Colchester United 0–1 Reading |date=11 August 2015 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=20 May 2016 }}</ref> He celebrated his 50th career appearance for Colchester during the season,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Waldron |first1=Jonathan |date=17 February 2016 |title=Colchester United winger Drey Wright showed "what a good prospect he is" according to Kevin Keen |url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/sport/14283290.Wright_display_earns_praise_from_Keen/ |newspaper=Daily Gazette |location=Colchester |access-date=20 May 2016 }}</ref> ending the campaign with 13 appearances.<ref name="Games played by Drey Wright in 2015/2016">{{Soccerbase season|65501|2015|name=Drey Wright|accessdate=8 July 2015}}</ref> He was offered a new deal at the end of the season following Colchester's relegation to [[EFL League Two|League Two]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cu-fc.com/news/article/colchester-united-2015-16-retained-list-3121083.aspx? |title=U's Retained List |last=Hudson |first=Matt |date=20 May 2016 |publisher=Colchester United FC |access-date=20 May 2016 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36347391 |title=Colchester United: Joe Edwards and Nicky Shorey among nine to depart |date=20 May 2016 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=20 May 2016 }}</ref> He signed a new one-year contract extension on 25 May 2016.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Waldron |first1=Jonathan |date=25 May 2016 |title=Winger Drey Wright commits his future to Colchester United |url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/sport/colchesterunited/14515641.Wright_agrees_new_one_year_deal_with_U_s/? |newspaper=Daily Gazette |location=Colchester |access-date=25 May 2016 }}</ref>

====2016–17 season====
Wright scored his first goal in almost two years on 24 September 2016 with the opening goal in Colchester's 2–1 home defeat to [[Accrington Stanley F.C.|Accrington Stanley]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/37393364 |title=Colchester United 1–2 Accrington Stanley |date=24 September 2016 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=25 September 2016 }}</ref> He made his 100th Colchester United appearance on 29 April 2017 in their 3–1 win at [[Leyton Orient F.C.|Leyton Orient]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39676226 |title=Leyton Orient 1–3 Colchester United |date=29 April 2017 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=30 April 2017 }}</ref> and made a total of 46 appearances in addition to scoring two goals across the season.<ref name="Games played by Drey Wright in 2016/2017">{{soccerbase season|65501|2016|accessdate=30 June 2016}}</ref>

====2017–18 season====
Following his most successful season to date for Colchester, Wright agreed a one-year contract extension with the club on 29 June 2017.<ref>{{cite news |last=Waldron |first=Jonathan |date=29 June 2017 |title=Drey Wright staying at Colchester United for at least another year after signing new deal |url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/sport/colchesterunited/15380068.Winger_Drey_Wright_agrees_Colchester_United_stay/ |newspaper=Daily Gazette |location=Colchester |access-date=29 June 2017 }}</ref> Manager [[John McGreal]] suggested he might pick Wright in a more central midfield and attacking role instead of his more frequent wing position for the new season after playing and scoring during pre-season.<ref>{{cite news |last=Waldron |first=Jonathan |date=20 July 2017 |title=Colchester United head coach John McGreal says Drey Wright is equipped to play as a centre forward |url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/sport/colchesterunited/15423017.Drey_can_be_Wright_man_for_central_role_at_Colchester_United/ |newspaper=Daily Gazette |location=Colchester |access-date=27 July 2017 }}</ref> He scored his first season goal on 27 January 2018 during Colchester's 2–2 draw with [[Port Vale F.C.|Port Vale]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42756557 |title=Port Vale 2–2 Colchester United |date=27 January 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=27 January 2018 }}</ref>

===St Johnstone===
After six years in the Colchester United first team and three goals in 47 appearances during 2017–18, Wright signed a pre-contract agreement to join [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] in a two-year deal in May 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44053663 |title=St Johnstone recruit midfielder Drey Wright from Colchester |date=9 May 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=25 May 2018 }}</ref> He made his competitive debut for the club on 16 July in a [[Scottish League Cup]] [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] win over [[East Fife F.C.|East Fife]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44846269 |title=St Johnstone 0–0 East Fife (5–4pens) |date=16 July 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=29 July 2018 }}</ref> Wright scored his first goal for the club on 18 August in St Johnstone's 4–2 [[Overtime (sports)|extra-time]] win over [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45189088 |title=Queen of the South 2–4 St Johnstone |date=18 August 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=27 October 2018 }}</ref> His first season at the club ended early when he suffered a knee injury in a match against [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] in November 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Drey Wright: St Johnstone winger to miss rest of season with knee injury|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46370233|publisher=BBC Sport|date=28 November 2018|access-date=28 July 2019}}</ref> In August 2019, he returned to playing after nine months out.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49495614|title=St Johnstone: Drey Wright on course for return after nine months out|date=28 August 2019|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=29 August 2019}}</ref> He rejected a new contract and left the Saints in June 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/52889159|title=Drey Wright: Winger to leave St Johnstone after rejecting new deal|website=BBC Sport|date=2 June 2020 |access-date=2 June 2020}}</ref>

===Hibernian===
On 10 July 2020, Wright signed for [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/10668|title=DREY WRIGHT SIGNS FOR HIBERNIAN|website=Hibernian FC|access-date=10 July 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53352032 |title=Hibernian sign Kevin Nisbet and Drey Wright |website=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=10 July 2020 |access-date=10 July 2020}}</ref>
On 20 September 2020, Wright scored his first goal for [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in a 2–2 draw against [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54135422|title=Hibernian 2–2 Rangers|website=bbc.co.uk|first=Jamie|last=Lyall|date=21 September 2020|access-date=23 August 2021}}</ref>
Wright made twenty-eight competitive appearances and scored one goal in his first season with [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]].<ref name="ReferenceA">{{soccerbase season|65501|2020|accessdate=1 August 2020}}</ref>

On 9 April 2022, Wright scored the opener in the [[Edinburgh derby]] for [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]], his second goal for the club, but the game ended in a 3–1 win for [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/60903115|title=Hearts 3–1 Hibernian|website=bbc.co.uk|first=Andrew|last=Southwick|date=9 April 2022|access-date=10 April 2022}}</ref> Hibs released Wright in June 2022, at the end of his contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61675106 |title=Hibernian: Scott Allan, Alex Gogic, Drey Wright and Jamie Murphy among six exits |website=BBC Sport |date=2 June 2022 |accessdate=2 June 2022}}</ref>

===St Johnstone return===
Wright returned to St Johnstone on 16 June 2022.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.stv.tv/sport/drey-wright-and-andy-considine-join-st-johnstone-on-free-transfers |title=Drey Wright and Andy Considine join St Johnstone on free transfers |website=STV Sport |date=16 June 2022 |accessdate=16 June 2022 |first=Andy |last=Coyle}}</ref>

=== Dundee ===
On 12 June 2025, Wright joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=12 June 2025 |title=The Wright Signing |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/wright-signs/ |access-date=12 June 2025 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> On 29 November, Wright scored his first goal for the ''Dark Blues'' in a home win over [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dundee vs St Mirren: Scottish Premiership radio updates, live text & match report|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c4g4xe7z2jdt|website=BBC Sport|access-date=30 November 2025|language=en-GB}}</ref> On 17 January 2026, Wright netted a late winner for Dundee away to [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] in the [[Scottish Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kilmarnock vs Dundee: Scottish Cup text & radio updates, match report |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cn0yg7x0kgzt |access-date=17 January 2026 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 22 August, Wright scored a stunner at [[Tannadice Park]] in a [[Dundee derby]] win.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Moffat |first=Live ReportingColin |title=Dundee United vs Dundee LIVE: Scottish Premiership radio, text updates, team news, reaction, stats & head-to-head |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c39w04vdkkllt |access-date=2026-08-22 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

'''Declan Christopher John''' (born 30 June 1995) is a Welsh professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[left wing-back]] for {{Scottish football updater|StMirren}} club [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]]. He also plays for the [[Wales national football team|Wales national team]].

==Club career==
===Cardiff City===
Born in [[Merthyr Tydfil]], John progressed through the academy at [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]]. His professional debut for Cardiff came on 14 August 2012, in a 2–1 home defeat to [[Northampton Town F.C.|Northampton Town]] in the first round of the [[Football League Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19159869|title=Northampton 1–2 Cardiff |website=BBC Sport |date=14 August 2012 |access-date=17 August 2012}}</ref> On 5 January 2013, he made his only other appearance of the season, a loss by the same margin at [[Macclesfield Town]] in the third round of the [[FA Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Hughes|first1=Dewi|title=Macclesfield 2–1 Cardiff|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20877003|access-date=19 December 2015|website=BBC Sport |date=3 January 2013}}</ref>

John made his league debut on 17 August 2013 in a 2–0 loss at [[West Ham United]], Cardiff's first game in the [[Premier League]]. He signed a long-term contract until 2018 in December.<ref>{{cite news |title=Cardiff City and Wales defender Declan John agrees with new contract |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25197093 |website=BBC Sport |date=3 December 2015 |access-date=3 December 2015}}</ref> He went on to make 20 appearances [[2013–14 Premier League|that season]], appearing more frequently in the second half of the campaign, as the Bluebirds were relegated.<ref name=barns/>

Under new manager, [[Russell Slade]], John fell down the pecking order and was subsequently loaned out to [[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]] for the remainder of the [[2014–15 Cardiff City F.C. season|season]].<ref name=barns>{{cite news|title=Barnsley sign Declan John on loan from Cardiff City|url=http://www.barnsleyfc.co.uk/news/article/barnsley-sign-declan-john-on-loan-from-cardiff-city-2318346.aspx|access-date=19 December 2015|publisher=Barnsley F.C.|date=6 March 2015}}</ref> He made nine appearances for the ''Tykes'' before returning to Cardiff at the end of the season.

After only making a single appearance for Cardiff during the [[2015–16 Cardiff City F.C. season|2015–16 season]], John signed for [[Football League One|League One]] side [[Chesterfield F.C.|Chesterfield]] on a month-loan deal in February,<ref>{{cite news |title=Jordan Slew and Declan John: Chesterfield sign duo |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35606193 |website=BBC Sport |date=18 February 2016 |access-date=18 February 2016}}</ref> where he impressed in six appearances before being recalled by Cardiff on 14 April.<ref>{{cite news |title=More to come from Declan John at Chesterfield, says Danny Wilson |url=http://www.derbyshiretimes.co.uk/sport/football/chesterfield-fc/more-to-come-from-declan-john-at-chesterfield-says-danny-wilson-1-7751133 |work=Derbyshire Times |date=25 February 2016 |access-date=25 February 2016 |archive-date=22 January 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170122153944/http://www.derbyshiretimes.co.uk/sport/football/chesterfield-fc/more-to-come-from-declan-john-at-chesterfield-says-danny-wilson-1-7751133 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Cardiff City recall Declan John as 'precaution' ahead of play-off run in |url=http://www.walesonline.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/cardiff-city-recall-declan-john-11185263 |work=Wales Online |date=14 April 2016 |access-date=14 April 2016}}</ref>

Upon his return to Cardiff, John impressed new manager, [[Paul Trollope]], during pre-season and went on to make his first league start for the club in over a year, where he put in a man of the match performance in a goalless draw against [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] on the opening day of the season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Birmingham City 0–0 Cardiff City |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36929866 |website=BBC Sport |date=6 August 2016 |access-date=6 August 2016}}</ref> Despite an impressive start to the season, John became a bit-part player under [[Neil Warnock]] and was told he could leave the club at the end of the season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Craig Noone and Declan John set to leave Cardiff City, says boss Neil Warnock |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40108932 |website=BBC Sport |date=1 June 2017 |access-date=1 June 2017}}</ref>

===Rangers===
John was loaned to [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] in August 2017,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41098437 |title=Rangers sign Cardiff left-back Declan John on loan |website=BBC Sport |date=31 August 2017 |access-date=31 August 2017}}</ref> and the move was made permanent in December.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42457549 |title=Declan John: Rangers left-back signs permanent deal |website=BBC Sport |date=22 December 2017 |access-date=22 December 2017}}</ref>

===Swansea City===
On 9 August 2018, John joined [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]] on a three-year contract.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45134690 Declan John: Swansea City sign Rangers defender on three year deal] BBC Sport. 9 August 2018. Retrieved 9 August 2018.</ref> He made his debut for Swansea on 28 August 2018 in the [[EFL Cup]] against [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://swansea.vitalfootball.co.uk/10500-2/|title = Line-Ups Confirmed: Potter Gives Debuts to 5 Against Crystal Palace|date = 28 August 2018}}</ref>

John signed for [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]] on a six-month loan on 31 January 2020.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51333781 |title=Declan John: Wales international joins Sunderland from Swansea on loan |website=BBC Sport |date=31 January 2020 |access-date=31 January 2020}}</ref> He played no matches, and returned to Swansea after the completion of his loan. On 7 January 2021, John joined [[EFL League Two|League Two]] side [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]] on loan for the remainder of the 2020–21 season.<ref>{{Cite news |url= https://www.bwfc.co.uk/news/2021/january/wanderers-welcome-welshman/ |title=Wanderers welcome Welshman |publisher=Bolton Wanderers FC |date=7 January 2021}}</ref>

===Bolton Wanderers===
On 11 June 2021, Bolton confirmed that John would be re-joining them on a permanent three year deal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bwfc.co.uk/news/2021/june/john-returns-on-three-year-deal|title=John Returns On Three-Year Deal | Bolton Wanderers FC|website=www.bwfc.co.uk}}</ref> John made his second debut for the club on 7 August in a 3–3 draw against [[Milton Keynes Dons F.C.|MK Dons]]<ref>{{cite news |title=Bolton Wanderers 3 - 3 Milton Keynes Dons |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58035993 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=16 August 2021 |date=7 August 2021}}</ref> On 2 April, he started in the [[2023 EFL Trophy Final]] which Bolton won 4–0 against [[Plymouth Argyle F.C.|Plymouth Argyle]].<ref name="EFLT23">{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65088981 |title=Bolton Wanderers 4–0 Plymouth Argyle |first=Brent |last=Pilnick |website=BBC Sport |date=2 April 2023 |access-date=3 April 2023}}</ref>

On 1 September 2023, John joined [[Salford City F.C.|Salford City]] on loan until January 2024.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66689905|title=Salford City sign defensive duo Declan John and Ethan Ingram on loan|date=1 September 2023|via=www.bbc.co.uk}}</ref> On 22 May 2024, the club confirmed that he would be leaving at the end of his contract on 30 June.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bwfc.co.uk/news/retained-list-confirmed |title=RETAINED LIST CONFIRMED |date=22 May 2024 |publisher=bwfc.co.uk|access-date=22 May 2024}}</ref>

===St Mirren===
In November 2024 John joined [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] on a short term deal, subsequently extended until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/czr30ez0rnvo| title=John pens St Mirren extension| publisher=BBC Sport| date=26 December 2024| access-date=8 April 2025}}</ref> On 28 March 2025, John signed a further two-year contract.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c33731vj160o| title=John extends stay with new two-year deal| publisher=BBC Sport| date=28 March 2025| access-date=8 April 2025}}</ref>

John supplied the assist for St Mirren’s third goal in their Scottish League Cup final win against Celtic on 14 December 2025.

==International career==
John was first called up to the [[Wales national football team|Wales]] squad for the [[2014 FIFA World Cup]] [[2014 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group A|qualifiers]] against [[Macedonia national football team|Macedonia]] and [[Serbia national football team|Serbia]], in September 2013.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23922411 |title=Bale wants to play for Wales in the World Cup qualifiers |date=2 September 2013 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=2 November 2013}}</ref> He was an unused substitute in both games.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23964942 |title=Macedonia 2–1 Wales |date=6 September 2013 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=2 November 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/24011041 |title=Wales 0–3 Serbia |date=10 September 2013 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=2 November 2013}}</ref> The following month, he retained his place in the squad for the qualifiers against Macedonia and [[Belgium national football team|Belgium]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/24381327 |title=Gareth Bale withdraws from Wales squad with thigh injury |date=3 October 2013 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=2 November 2013}}</ref> On 11 October, John made his debut, playing the whole 90 minutes in the 1–0 win against Macedonia at the [[Cardiff City Stadium]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/24393705 |title=Wales 1–0 Macedonia |date=11 October 2013 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=2 November 2013}}</ref>

'''Liam Francis Peadar Donnelly''' (born 7 March 1996) is a Northern Irish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|Kilmarno}} club [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].

Donnelly, who can also play as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]], has previously played for [[Dungannon Swifts F.C.|Dungannon Swifts]], [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]], [[Crawley Town F.C.|Crawley Town]], [[Hartlepool United F.C.|Hartlepool United]], [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell and Kilmarnock]]. He has also represented [[Northern Ireland national football team|Northern Ireland]] internationally.

==Club career==
===Fulham===
Donnelly signed for [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] as a youngster from [[IFA Premiership]] club [[Dungannon Swifts F.C.|Dungannon Swifts]]. Donnelly captained Fulham to the [[2013–14 FA Youth Cup#Final|2014 FA Youth Cup final]].<ref>[http://www.thefa.com/news/2014/may/05/chelsea-v-fulham-final-second-leg-report Chelsea seal Youth Cup glory after thriller at the Bridge], [[The Football Association]], 6 May 2014</ref>

On 31 July 2015, Donnelly signed for [[Crawley Town F.C.|Crawley Town]] on a one-month youth loan.<ref>{{cite web|title=Liam Donnelly: Crawley Town sign Fulham defender on loan|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33735029|publisher=BBC Sport|date=31 July 2015|access-date=24 July 2018}}</ref> The loan was then extended until January 2016,<ref>{{cite web|title=Liam Extends Crawley Loan|url=http://www.fulhamfc.com/news/2015/august/27/liam-extends-crawley-loan|publisher=Fulham F.C.|date=27 August 2015|access-date=24 July 2018}}</ref> however he was recalled early by Fulham in October.<ref>{{cite web|title=Liam Donnelly: Fulham recall defender from Crawley Town loan|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34651814|publisher=BBC Sport|date=27 October 2015|access-date=24 July 2018}}</ref>

===Hartlepool United===
On 19 August 2016, Donnelly signed for [[Hartlepool United F.C.|Hartlepool United]], following his release from Fulham.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.hartlepoolunited.co.uk/news/article/2016-17/hartlepool-united-liam-donnelly-signs-transfer-fulham-3259487.aspx|title=Former Fulham Defender Liam Donnelly Signs For Hartlepool United|work=Hartlepool United F.C.|date=19 August 2016|access-date=19 August 2016|archive-date=4 November 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161104210219/http://www.hartlepoolunited.co.uk/news/article/2016-17/hartlepool-united-liam-donnelly-signs-transfer-fulham-3259487.aspx|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Motherwell===
On 7 June 2018, [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] announced the signing of Donnelly on an initial two-year contract from Hartlepool United for an undisclosed fee.<ref name="Liam Donnelly is signing number two">{{cite web |title=Liam Donnelly is signing number two|url=http://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2018/06/07/liam-donnelly-is-signing-number-two/|website=motherwellfc.co.uk |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |access-date=7 June 2018 |date=7 June 2018}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club in a 3–2 victory against [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] on the final day of the [[2018–19 Motherwell F.C. season|season]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48236248|title=Turnbull double downs Livingston in thriller|work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

At the beginning of the [[2019–20 Motherwell F.C. season|2019–20 season]], Donnelly moved from defence into midfield,<ref>{{cite web|title=Liam Donnelly delighted to be back with Northern Ireland|url=https://www.irishnews.com/sport/footballsoccer/2019/09/04/news/liam-donnelly-delighted-to-be-back-with-northern-ireland-1702522/|publisher=The Irish News|last=Archer|first=Kenny|date=4 September 2019|access-date=4 October 2019}}</ref> and went on to score four goals in three games in the [[Scottish League Cup]] group stages, against [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Queen of the South 0–3 Motherwell: Steelmen win Betfred opener|url=https://www.motherwelltimes.co.uk/sport/football/queen-of-the-south-0-3-motherwell-steelmen-win-betfred-opener-1-4964505|publisher=Motherwell Times|last=Goldthorp|first=Craig|date=13 July 2019|access-date=4 October 2019}}</ref> [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Motherwell smash Morton as Dundee United ease past Cowdenbeath in Betfred Cup|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/motherwell-smash-morton-dundee-united-18367449|publisher=Daily Record|last=McDougall|first=Mark|date=19 July 2019|access-date=4 October 2019}}</ref> and [[Annan Athletic F.C.|Annan Athletic]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Motherwell 4, Annan Athletic 0: Stephen Robinson's new team looking good|url=https://www.eveningtimes.co.uk/sport/other_football/17799574.motherwell-4-annan-athletic-0-stephen-robinson-39-s-new-team-looking-good/|publisher=Evening Times|last=Cameron|first=Neil|date=28 F.C.|Hamilton Academical]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Hamilton Academical 1–3 Motherwell|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49378871|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Mullen|first=Scott|date=24 August 2019|access-date=4 October 2019}}</ref> and [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Motherwell 3–0 Hibernian|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49456516|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Sutherland|first=Jonathan|date=31 August 2019|access-date=4 October 2019}}</ref> In October 2019, Donnelly was rewarded for his early season form as he signed an extension to his contract at [[Fir Park]], to run until summer 2022.<ref>{{cite web|title=Liam Donnelly: Motherwell 'revelation' earns contract extension|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49914424|publisher=BBC Sport|date=2 October 2019|access-date=2 October 2019}}</ref>

In the opening game of the [[2020–21 Motherwell F.C. season|2020–21 season]], Donnelly missed a penalty as Motherwell lost 1–0 away to [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ross County 1–0 Motherwell|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53549282
|website=bbc.co.uk|last=Campbell|first=Andy|date=4 August 2020|access-date=24 July 2021}}</ref> Following that match he picked up a knee injury in training which was initially expected to keep him out for two months,<ref>{{cite web|title=LIAM DONNELLY SIDELINED WITH KNEE INJURY|url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2020/08/11/liam-donnelly-sidelined-with-knee-injury/|website=motherwellfc.co.uk|date=11 August 2020|access-date=24 July 2021}}</ref> however he then required surgery on the injury, ruling him out until after the new year.<ref>{{cite news|title=Motherwell dealt further Liam Donnelly injury blow|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/motherwell-dealt-further-liam-donnelly-22666237|newspaper=Daily Record|last=McGilvray|first=Andy|date=11 September 2020|access-date=24 July 2021}}</ref>

Donnelly made his return from injury on 14 July 2021, as a substitute in a 1–0 win away to [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] in a [[Scottish League Cup]] group stage match.<ref>{{cite web|title=QUEEN'S PARK 0-1 MOTHERWELL|url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2021/07/14/queens-park-0-1-motherwell/|website=motherwellfc.co.uk|date=14 July 2021|access-date=24 July 2021}}</ref> He was released by Motherwell at the end of the 2021–22 season.

===Kilmarnock===
On 5 July 2022, Donnelly signed a one-year contract with [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Liam Donnelly: Kilmarnock sign Northern Ireland midfielder after Motherwell exit |language=en-GB |website=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/62055012 |access-date=5 July 2022 |date=5 July 2022}}</ref> On 1 August 2023, he signed a new two-year contract with Kilmarnock.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/sport/football/scottish/northern-ireland-international-signs-two-year-contract-extension-at-kilmarnock/a64456401.html| title=Northern Ireland international signs two-year contract extension at Kilmarnock| publisher=Belfast Telegraph| date=1 August 2023| access-date=26 February 2025}}</ref>

===St Mirren===
Donnelly signed a two-year contract with [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] in June 2025.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c78nw9q64wno |title=St Mirren: Northern Ireland international Liam Donnelly joins from Kilmarnock |website=BBC Sport |date=23 June 2025 |accessdate=24 June 2025}}</ref>

==International career==
Donnelly made his senior [[Northern Ireland national football team|Northern Ireland]] debut on 4 June 2014 against [[Chile national football team|Chile]], coming on as a substitute in the 89th minute.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27383579|title=Late goals seal Chile win over Northern Ireland|publisher=BBC Sport|date=5 June 2014|access-date=4 July 2014}}</ref>

On 11 September 2018, Donnelly made his 22nd appearance for [[Northern Ireland national under-21 football team|Northern Ireland's under-21s]] in a 2–1 win away to [[Spain national under-21 football team|Spain]], a match in which he scored from a penalty, and in doing so became the nation's record cap holder at that level.<ref>{{cite web|title=Spain U21 1–2 Northern Ireland U21|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45409144|publisher=BBC Sport|date=11 September 2018|access-date=7 September 2019}}</ref> He eventually finished his time with the under-21 side with 24 caps.<ref>{{cite web|title=Captain Donnelly leaves Under-21s after record 24 appearances|url=https://www.irishfa.com/news/2018/october/watch-liam-donnelly-bids-emotional-farewell-to-under-21s|publisher=Northern Irish Football Association|date=17 October 2018|access-date=7 September 2019}}</ref>

Donnelly was recalled to the senior squad in August 2019, ahead of a friendly against [[Luxembourg national football team|Luxembourg]] and a [[UEFA Euro 2020 qualifying Group C|Euro 2020 qualifier]] against [[Germany national football team|Germany]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Liam Donnelly: Midfielder ready to grab Northern Ireland chance 'with both hands'|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49578912|publisher=BBC Sport|date=4 September 2019|access-date=7 September 2019}}</ref> He came on as a substitute against Luxembourg on 5 September, earning his second cap, five years after his first.<ref>{{cite web|title=Northern Ireland 1–0 Luxembourg|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49505624|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Sterling|first=Mark|date=5 September 2019|access-date=7 September 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=How Shayne Lavery and Liam Donnelly's Northern Ireland cameos provided optimism for big international futures|url=https://belfasttelegraph.co.uk/sport/football/international/how-shayne-lavery-and-liam-donnellys-northern-ireland-cameos-provided-optimism-for-big-international-futures-38472509.html|publisher=Belfast Telegraph|last=Hanna|first=Gareth|newspaper=Belfasttelegraph|date=6 September 2019|access-date=7 September 2019}}</ref>

'''Aaron Tshibola''' (born 2 January 1995) is a professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[defensive midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|Kilmarno}} club [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]]. Born in England, he represents the [[DR Congo national football team|DR Congo national team]].

Born in London, he came through the youth ranks at [[Reading F.C.|Reading]] before moving to [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] in 2016. He has had loan spells at English [[Football League]] sides [[Hartlepool United F.C.|Hartlepool United]], [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] and [[Milton Keynes Dons F.C.|Milton Keynes Dons]], as well as [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]]. He has also played in Belgium for [[Waasland Beveren]] and in Portugal for [[C.D. Aves|Aves]].

==Early life==
Tshibola was born in the [[London Borough of Newham]] in England.<ref name="ENFA">{{cite web |title=Player search |url=http://www.enfa.co.uk/ |publisher=English National Football Archive |accessdate=11 December 2014 |url-access=registration}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Reading===
Tshibola joined [[Reading F.C.|Reading]]'s academy at age thirteen<ref name="Reading profile">{{cite web |title=Aaron Tshibola |url=http://www.readingfc.co.uk/team/player-profile/aaron-tshibola/18 |publisher=Reading F.C |accessdate=23 August 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141008042010/http://www.readingfc.co.uk/team/player-profile/aaron-tshibola/18 |archive-date=8 October 2014 |url-status=dead}}</ref> and signed his first professional deal with the club in March 2011.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.readingfc.co.uk/page/NewsDetail/0,,10306~2304375,00.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110305235650/http://www.readingfc.co.uk/page/NewsDetail/0%2C%2C10306~2304375%2C00.html |archive-date=5 March 2011 |title=Tanner and Tshibola sign on |publisher=Reading F.C |accessdate=28 March 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref> While in the Reading Academy, Tshibola went on trial with [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]].<ref>{{cite news |title=MAN UTD TRIALS FOR READING ACADEMY PAIR |url=http://www.tribalfootball.com/articles/man-utd-trials-reading-academy-pair-3071991#.VRcYhPmsWSo |publisher=Tribal Football |accessdate=28 March 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161001202215/http://www.tribalfootball.com/articles/man-utd-trials-reading-academy-pair-3071991#.VRcYhPmsWSo |archive-date=1 October 2016 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Ahead of the 2014–15 season, Tshibola signed a new contract with [[Reading F.C.|Reading]], keeping him at the club until 2016.<ref>{{cite news |title=Transfer news: Reading midfielder Aaron Tshibola signs new two-year deal |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11756/9355885/transfer-news-reading-midfielder-aaron-tshibola-signs-new-two-year-deal |publisher=Sky Sports |date=20 June 2014 |accessdate=28 March 2015}}</ref> Then on 23 August 2014, he made his professional debut as an 86th-minute substitute in a [[Football League Championship|Championship]] fixture against [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Nottingham Forest 4–0 Reading |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/28815166 |publisher=BBC Sport |accessdate=5 October 2014}}</ref>

On 9 September 2015, Tshibola extended his contract with Reading until the summer of 2019.<ref name="Aaron Tshibola awarded new Royals contract">{{cite web |title=Aaron Tshibola awarded new Royals contract |url=http://www.readingfc.co.uk/news/article/aaron-tshibola-new-contract-reading-fc-2677572.aspx |website=readingfc.co.uk/ |publisher=Reading F.C. |accessdate=9 September 2015 |date=9 September 2015}}</ref>

news |title=Tshibola joins Hartlepool on loan |url=http://www.readingfc.co.uk/news/article/aaron-tshibola-hartlepool-united-reading-2177442.aspx |publisher=Reading F.C |date=2 January 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150105180532/http://www.readingfc.co.uk/news/article/aaron-tshibola-hartlepool-united-reading-2177442.aspx |archive-date=5 January 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref> before making his debut the next day in a 1–0 loss against [[Wycombe Wanderers F.C.|Wycombe Wanderers]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Wycombe Wanderers 1–0 Hartlepool United |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30609068 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=3 January 2015 |accessdate=28 March 2015}}</ref> His first four appearances at the club earned Tshibola a loan extension ===Aston Villa===
On 10 July 2016, Tshibola moved to [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] on a four-year contract, for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tshibola completes Villa Park move |url=http://www.readingfc.co.uk/news/article/2016-17/tshibola-departs-madejski-stadium-to-sign-for-aston-villa-3177097.aspx |website=readingfc.co.uk |publisher=Reading F.C. |accessdate=10 July 2016 |date=10 July 2016}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club in a 1–1 draw with [[Newcastle United]] on 24 September 2016.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/37392374 |title=Aston Villa 1–1 Newcastle |publisher=BBC |date=24 September 2016 |accessdate=27 September 2016}}</ref> On 30 January 2017, Tshibola moved to [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] on loan for the remainder of the [[2016–17 EFL Championship|2016–17]] season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tshibola joins The Reds |url=http://www.nottinghamforest.co.uk/news/article/2016-17/nottingham-forest-aston-villa-aaron-tshibola-3545100.aspx |website=nottinghamforest.co.uk |publisher=Nottingham Forest |accessdate=30 January 2017 |date=30 January 2017}}</ref>

On 27 July 2017, Tshibola joined [[EFL League One]] side [[Milton Keynes Dons F.C.|Milton Keynes Dons]] on a season-long loan deal.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Aston Villa midfielder joins League One side on season-long loan |url=http://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/aston-villa-midfielder-joins-league-13396962 |publisher=Birmingham Mail |date=27 July 2017 |accessdate=27 July 2017}}</ref> He scored his first goal for MK Dons in an [[EFL Trophy]] tie against [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C. Reserves and Academy|Brighton & Hove Albion Under-23s]] on 29 August 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.miltonkeynes.co.uk/sport/football/mk-dons/report-mk-dons-2-0-brighton-u21s-routine-win-in-checkatrade-trophy-1-8126085 |title=REPORT: MK Dons 2–0 Brighton U21s: Routine win in Checkatrade Trophy |publisher=miltonkeynes.co.uk |date=29 August 2017 |accessdate=30 August 2017|archive-date=30 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170830160912/http://www.miltonkeynes.co.uk/sport/football/mk-dons/report-mk-dons-2-0-brighton-u21s-routine-win-in-checkatrade-trophy-1-8126085|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 9 November 2017, he returned to Aston Villa following the mutual termination of his loan with Milton Keynes Dons.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41928507 |title=Aaron Tshibola: Aston Villa midfielder's loan with MK Dons is cancelled |publisher=BBC Sport |date=9 November 2017 |accessdate=14 November 2017}}</ref>

===Kilmarnock===
Tshibola was loaned to [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] in January 2018, working under his former [[Reading F.C.|Reading]] manager [[Steve Clarke]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42858245 |title=Aaron Tshibola: Kilmarnock sign Aston Villa midfielder on loan |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=29 January 2018 |accessdate=29 January 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/what-aston-villas-forgotten-man-15081512 |title=This is what Aston Villa's forgotten man is set to do now |date=28 August 2018}}</ref> He made his debut for Killie on 3 February 2018, as a 65th-minute substitute for [[Kris Boyd]] in the Ayrshire side's 1–0 win over [[Scottish Premiership]] Champions [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42842297 |title=Kilmarnock 1–0 Celtic |work=BBC Sport}}</ref> Tshibola scored his first Kilmarnock goal in the 4–0 [[Scottish Cup]] win over [[Brora Rangers F.C.|Brora Rangers]] the following week.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42927889 |title=Kilmarnock 4–0 Brora Rangers |work=BBC Sport}}</ref> After six months, he returned to Aston Villa, only to be loaned back out to Kilmarnock for another season on 29 August 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.avfc.co.uk/News/2018/08/29/tshibola-rejoins-kilmarnock-on-loan |title=Aaron Tshibola rejoins Kilmarnock on season-long loan |date=29 August 2018 |publisher=Aston Villa FC|access-date=29 August 2018}}</ref>

===Waasland Beveren===
On 29 August 2019, Tshibola signed for Belgian club [[Waasland Beveren]] for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite web |title=WELKOM, AARON TSHIBOLA! |date=29 August 2019 |url=https://www.waasland-beveren.be/2019/08/welkom-aaron-tshibola/ |publisher=[[Waasland Beveren]] |accessdate=29 August 2019 |archive-date=30 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190830042451/https://www.waasland-beveren.be/2019/08/welkom-aaron-tshibola/ |url-status=dead}}</ref> On 19 October 2019, he made his debut in a 2–0 defeat to [[K.A.A. Gent|Gent]].

===Aves===
On 31 January 2020, Tshibola signed for Portuguese side [[C.D. Aves|Aves]] on a one-and-a-half-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://cdaves.pt/contratacao-aaron-tshibola/ |title=CONTRATAÇÃO {{!}} AARON TSHIBOLA|date=31 January 2020|website=Clube Desportivo Das Aves|access-date=1 February 2020|archive-date=1 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200201091427/http://cdaves.pt/contratacao-aaron-tshibola/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 1 March 2020, he made his debut, coming on as substitute in a 3–1 defeat to [[F.C. Paços de Ferreira|Paços de Ferreira]]. He made one other appearance in a 2–0 defeat to [[Sporting CP]] before the league was suspended due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://ligaportugal.vsports.pt/mday/1732/liga/ |title=LIGA NOS Época 2019/2020 |date=8 March 2020 |website=Liga NOS Official Website|access-date=31 March 2020}}</ref>

On 13 July 2020, Tshibola announced on his [[Twitter]] account that due to financial difficulties at the club, he had left Aves and was a free agent once again.<ref>{{Cite web |date=13 July 2020 |title=Aaron Tshibola – Twitter |url=https://twitter.com/AaronTshibola/status/1282626837357760512|access-date=13 July 2020 |website=Twitter}}</ref>

===Kilmarnock===
On 31 July 2020, Tshibola returned for a third spell with [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]], signing a one-year contract.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kilmarnock sign Aaron Tshibola for third time after relegation double |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53613633 |date=31 July 2020 |accessdate=1 August 2020 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> He left Kilmarnock at the end of the 2020–21 season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/news/squad-update-following-2020-21-season/ |title=Squad update following 2020/21 season |date=25 May 2021}}</ref>

===Gençlerbirliği===
In July 2021, Tshibola signed for Turkish side [[Gençlerbirliği S.K.|Gençlerbirliği]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nottheoldfirm.com/news/aaron-tshibola-signs-for-genclerbirligi-sk-after-kilmarnock-exit/ |title=Aaron Tshibola signs for Gençlerbirliği SK after Kilmarnock exit |website=nottheoldfirm.com |date=11 July 2021|access-date=11 July 2021}}</ref> He made his debut playing 90 minutes of a 0–0 draw with [[Adanaspor]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adanaspor vs. Gençlerbirliği – 21 August 2021 |url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2021/08/21/turkey/1-lig/adanaspor-fk/genclerbirligi/3557621/|access-date=23 August 2021 |website=Soccerway}}</ref> On 19 December 2021, he scored his first goal in Turkish football, in a 5–0 victory over [[Menemenspor]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gençlerbirliği vs. Menemenspor – 19 December 2021 |url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2021/12/19/turkey/1-lig/genclerbirligi/yeni-menemen-belediyespor-izmir/3557764/|access-date=25 January 2022 |website=Soccerway}}</ref>

===AEL Limassol===
On 12 August 2022, [[Cypriot First Division]] club [[AEL Limassol]] announced that Tshibola had joined the club.<ref>{{Citation |title=Welcome Aaron Tshibola! Let's Go Lions 🔥🟡🔵 {{!}} By AEL Limassol FC {{!}} Facebook |url=https://ms-my.facebook.com/OfficialAELFC/videos/welcome-aaron-tshibola-lets-go-lions-/590784499417723/ |language=en |access-date=24 August 2022}}</ref> He made his debut of the club on 28 August 2022, in a 2–1 away defeat to local rivals [[Aris Limassol FC|Aris Limassol]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=28 August 2022 |title=Aris Limassol 2 : 1 AEL Limassol |url=https://www.whoscored.com/Matches/1662193/Show/Cyprus-First-Division-2022-2023-Aris-Limassol-AEL-Limassol |access-date=28 October 2022 |website=www.whoscored.com}}</ref> He scored his first goal in Cyprus on 28 October 2022, in a 3–0 victory over [[Akritas Chlorakas]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Akritas vs. AEL – 28 October 2022 |url=https://uk.soccerway.com/matches/2022/10/28/cyprus/1-division/akritas-chloraka/ael-limassol/3840456/ |access-date=28 October 2022 |website=Soccerway}}</ref>

===Hatta Club===
In August 2023, Tshibola joined newly promoted [[UAE Pro League]] team [[Hatta Club]] for a €150,000 fee.<ref>{{Cite web |date=11 August 2023 |title=Announcement |url=https://www.ael-fc.com/2023/08/tsimpola/ |access-date=11 August 2023 |website=www.ael-fc.com |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230812030144/https://www.ael-fc.com/2023/08/tsimpola/ |archive-date=12 August 2023 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

After half a season with [[PAS Lamia 1964|Lamia]], Tshibola joined [[Super League Greece|Greek Super League]] club [[Levadiakos F.C.|Levadiakos]] in June 2025.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.novasports.gr/sport/podosfairo/event/super-league-1/article/14256406/apo-ti-lamia-ston-levadeiako/ |title=Από τη Λαμία στον Λεβαδειακό |website=novasports.gr |date=19 June 2025 |accessdate=19 June 2025 |language=Greek}}</ref>

===Kilmarnock (fourth spell)===
On 2 February 2026, Tshibola returned to Scottish Premiership club Kilmarnock on a permanent deal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/news/aaron-tshibola-returns-to-kilmarnock-on-permanent-deal/ |title=Aaron Tshibola returns to Kilmanock on permanent deal |website=kilmarnockfc.co.uk |date=2 February 2026 |accessdate=2 February 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
Tshibola was called up by [[England national under-18 football team|England U18]] and made his debut, coming on as a substitute in the second half, in a 1–0 loss against [[Belgium national under-18 football team|Belgium]] on 5 March 2013.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.readingfc.co.uk/news/article/england-trio-play-tonight-695061.aspx |title=Trio make England bow |publisher=Reading F.C. |accessdate=28 March 2015 |date=6 March 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150328215222/http://www.readingfc.co.uk/news/article/england-trio-play-tonight-695061.aspx |archive-date=28 March 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

He is also eligible to represent [[DR Congo national football team|DR Congo national team]] due to his ancestry.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://thetilehurstend.sbnation.com/2013/8/6/4593404/the-aaron-tshibola-interview-reading-fc |title=The Aaron Tshibola Interview |date=6 August 2013 |publisher=SB Nation.com |accessdate=10 July 2016}}</ref> He was called up to the DR Congo national team for a friendly against [[Kenya national football team|Kenya]] on 26 March 2017, but did not make an appearance.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rdcongoleopardsfoot.com/amical-kenya-rd-congo-la-liste-des-24leopards/ |title=Amical Kenya-RD Congo: La liste des 24 Léopards |date=20 March 2017}}</ref> On 27 March 2018, he finally made his senior international debut for DR Congo, playing 45 minutes in a friendly against [[Tanzania national football team|Tanzania]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://uk.soccerway.com/matches/2018/03/27/world/friendlies/tanzania/congo-dr/2749056/?ICID=HP_MS_01_0 |title=TANZANIA VS. CONGO DR (Match report) |publisher=Soccerway |date=27 March 2018 |accessdate=27 March 2018}}</ref>

Tshibola was called up to the DR Congo squad for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]] on 20 May 2026, replacing the injured [[Rocky Bushiri]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-defender-rocky-bushiri-opens-up-on-world-cup-injury-heartache-and-makes-vow-8614513 |title=Hibs defender Rocky Bushiri opens up on World Cup injury heartache and makes vow |publisher=[[Edinburgh Evening News]] |first=Mark |last=Atkinson |date=May 21, 2026 |access-date=May 21, 2026 |url-status=live |archive-date=May 21, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260521161743/https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-defender-rocky-bushiri-opens-up-on-world-cup-injury-heartache-and-makes-vow-8614513}}</ref>
