'''Bradley Halliday''' (born 10 July 1995) is an English professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] or [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|Dundee}} club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].

He previously played for [[Fleetwood Town F.C.|Fleetwood Town]], [[Cambridge United F.C.|Cambridge United]], [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]] and [[Bradford City A.F.C.|Bradford City]], and had [[Loan (sports)|loan]] spells with [[York City F.C.|York City]], [[Hartlepool United F.C.|Hartlepool United]] and [[Accrington Stanley F.C.|Accrington Stanley]].

==Early and personal life==
Halliday was born and raised in [[Redcar]], North Yorkshire.
Halliday is engaged with two young children.<ref name=Hugman/><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.gazettelive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/former-middlesbrough-defender-brad-halliday-11972505 |title=Former Middlesbrough defender Brad Halliday set to face old club – Due to stoppage time dismissal |first=Philip |last=Tallentire |newspaper=The Gazette |location=Middlesbrough |date=3 October 2016 |accessdate=26 May 2018}}</ref> He attended [[Prior Pursglove College]] in [[Guisborough]], North Yorkshire.<ref name="Sport student gets talent spotted by Newcastle United"/>

==Career==
===Early career===
Halliday had been playing for [[Redcar Town F.C.|Redcar Town]]'s youth team for 10 years when joining the [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]] [[Middlesbrough F.C. Reserves and Academy|academy]] in 2010.<ref>{{cite web |first=Mike |last=Gettings |title=U15A 2009–10 review |url=https://sites.google.com/site/redcartownfc/about-the-team/reviews/2009-10-Review/u15a2009-10review |publisher=Redcar Town F.C. |date=21 February 2013 |accessdate=9 January 2018}}</ref> He later returned to Redcar although Middlesbrough continued to monitor his progress.<ref>{{cite web |title=Newton Aycliffe FC 2–4 Redcar Town Under 18s FC |url=http://clubwebsite.production.clubtest.co.uk/redcartownunder18/155626/SeasonArchive/match_report/3131837?archive_id=59619 |publisher=Redcar Town F.C. |date=23 July 2011 |accessdate=24 December 2014 |archive-date=24 December 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141224182437/http://clubwebsite.production.clubtest.co.uk/redcartownunder18/155626/SeasonArchive/match_report/3131837?archive_id=59619 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="Bradley Halliday">{{cite web |title=Bradley Halliday |url=http://www.mfc.co.uk.p.preprod.performgroup.com/page/squad/academy/0,,1~3445445,00.html |publisher=Middlesbrough F.C. |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141224145856/http://www.mfc.co.uk.p.preprod.performgroup.com/page/squad/academy/0%2C%2C1~3445445%2C00.html |archivedate=24 December 2014 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Halliday was spotted playing for Redcar by a [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] scout before joining the club's [[Newcastle United F.C. Reserves and Academy|academy]] in early 2013.<ref name="Sport student gets talent spotted by Newcastle United">{{cite web |title=Sport student gets talent spotted by Newcastle United |url=http://www.pursglove.ac.uk/news/bradley-halliday-newcastle-united |publisher=Prior Pursglove College |date=1 March 2013 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130515230238/http://www.pursglove.ac.uk/news/bradley-halliday-newcastle-united |archivedate=15 May 2013 |url-status=dead}}</ref> He rejoined Middlesbrough after impressing their manager Dave Parnaby during a trial, signing a professional contract with the club in August 2013.<ref name=YorkProfile>{{cite web |title=York City FC player profiles: Bradley Halliday |url=http://www.yorkcityfootballclub.co.uk/team/player-profile/bradley-halliday/17 |publisher=York City F.C. |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141214204350/http://www.yorkcityfootballclub.co.uk/team/player-profile/bradley-halliday/17 |archivedate=14 December 2014 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="Bradley Halliday"/><ref>{{cite news |title=Another year of excellent results |url=http://www.pursglove.ac.uk/news/a-level-results-2013 |publisher=Prior Pursglove College |date=15 August 2013 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141224175158/http://www.pursglove.ac.uk/news/a-level-results-2013 |archivedate=24 December 2014 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Having played regularly for Middlesbrough's under-21s in the [[2014–15 Middlesbrough F.C. season|2014–15 season]], Halliday joined [[EFL League Two|League Two]] club [[York City F.C.|York City]] on 14 November 2014 on a one-month youth [[Loan (sports)|loan]] to provide cover and competition for [[right back]] [[Marvin McCoy]].<ref name=YorkProfile/><ref>{{cite news |first=Dave |last=Flett |title=Update: Teenage Middlesbrough right-back Brad Halliday signs York City loan deal |url=http://www.yorkpress.co.uk/sport/11603618.UPDATED__Teenage_Middlesbrough_right_back_Brad_Halliday_signs_York_City_loan_deal/ |newspaper=The Press |location=York |date=14 November 2014 |accessdate=24 December 2014}}</ref> He made his first-team debut in York's 3–2 home defeat to [[AFC Wimbledon]] on 13 December 2014, and having been named [[man of the match]] his loan was extended until 17 January 2015 two days after the match.<ref>{{cite news |first=Dave |last=Flett |title=Middlesbrough teenager Brad Halliday extends his loan with York City |url=http://www.yorkpress.co.uk/sport/11668005.Middlesbrough_teenager_Brad_Halliday_extends_his_loan_with_York_City/ |newspaper=The Press |location=York |date=15 December 2014 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141215234448/http://www.yorkpress.co.uk/sport/11668005.Middlesbrough_teenager_Brad_Halliday_extends_his_loan_with_York_City/ |archivedate=15 December 2014}}</ref> He established himself in the team ahead of McCoy before receiving the first [[Red card (association football)|red card]] of his senior career for a two-footed tackle in York's 1–0 home win over [[Accrington Stanley F.C.|Accrington Stanley]] on 26 December 2014.<ref name="Brad Halliday signs on loan for York City until end of season – right back is winning race for starting place against Stevenage">{{cite news |first=Dave |last=Flett |title=Brad Halliday signs on loan for York City until end of season – Right back is winning race for starting place against Stevenage |url=http://www.yorkpress.co.uk/sport/11728242.UPDATED_WITH_VIDEO__Brad_Halliday_signs_on_loan_for_York_City_until_end_of_season/ |newspaper=The Press |location=York |date=15 January 2015 |accessdate=17 January 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |first=Dave |last=Flett |title=Ten-man York City beat Accrington 1–0 thanks to Keith Lowe goal |url=http://www.yorkpress.co.uk/sport/11689421.York_City_1__Accrington_Stanley_0/ |newspaper=The Press |location=York |date=27 December 2014 |accessdate=17 January 2015}}</ref> After serving a three-match suspension his loan at York was extended until the end of the season.<ref name="Brad Halliday signs on loan for York City until end of season – right back is winning race for starting place against Stevenage"/> Halliday scored his first career goal with an 85th-minute equaliser in a 1–1 draw away to [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]] on 2 May 2015 with a shot into the bottom right corner after capitalising on a slip from [[Dan Butler (English footballer)|Dan Butler]].<ref name=sb1415/><ref>{{cite news |title=Portsmouth 1–1 York City |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32460134 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=2 May 2015 |accessdate=9 January 2018}}</ref> He finished his loan at York with 24 appearances and 1 goal.<ref name=sb1415/>

Halliday joined League Two club [[Hartlepool United F.C.|Hartlepool United]] on a one-month loan on 10 September 2015, as cover for the injured [[Jordan Richards (footballer, born 1993)|Jordan Richards]] and [[Michael Duckworth]] and the suspended [[Carl Magnay]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Roy |last=Kelly |title=Hartlepool United sign Boro's ex-York defender Brad Halliday on loan |url=http://www.hartlepoolmail.co.uk/sport/football/hartlepool-united/hartlepool-united-sign-boro-s-ex-york-defender-brad-halliday-on-loan-1-7454555 |newspaper=Hartlepool Mail |date=10 September 2015 |accessdate=5 December 2016 |archive-date=19 October 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161019184131/http://www.hartlepoolmail.co.uk/sport/football/hartlepool-united/hartlepool-united-sign-boro-s-ex-york-defender-brad-halliday-on-loan-1-7454555 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He made his debut two days later in a 1–0 away loss to [[Exeter City F.C.|Exeter City]], and finished the loan spell with six appearances.<ref name=sb1516/> On 20 October 2015, he joined another League Two club, Accrington Stanley, on a one-month emergency loan,<ref>{{cite news |first=Tyrone |last=Marshall |title=Bradley Halliday: Accrington sign Middlesbrough defender on loan |url=http://www.lancashiretelegraph.co.uk/sport/13883362.Accrington_Stanley_sign_Middlesbrough_defender_on_emergency_loan_deal/ |newspaper=Lancashire Telegraph |location=Blackburn |date=20 October 2015 |accessdate=13 January 2016}}</ref> debuting the same day in a 4–3 home defeat to AFC Wimbledon.<ref name=sb1516/> Having made 11 appearances for Accrington, his loan was extended for the rest of [[2015–16 Accrington Stanley F.C. season|2015–16]] on 4 January 2016.<ref>{{cite news |first=Tyrone |last=Marshall |title=Accrington Stanley extend Brad Halliday loan until the end of the season |url=http://www.lancashiretelegraph.co.uk/sport/14180376.Accrington_Stanley_extend_Brad_Halliday_loan_until_the_end_of_the_season/ |newspaper=Lancashire Telegraph |location=Blackburn |date=4 January 2016 |accessdate=13 January 2016}}</ref>

===Cambridge United===
On 31 August 2016, Halliday signed for League Two club [[Cambridge United F.C.|Cambridge United]] on a long-term contract for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite news |title=Brad Halliday: Cambridge United sign defender from Middlesbrough |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/37226302 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=31 August 2016 |accessdate=2 September 2016}}</ref>

He was offered a new contract by Cambridge United at the end of the 2018–19 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48191973|title=David Forde: Cambridge United release former Millwall keeper|date=7 May 2019|accessdate=8 May 2019|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref>

===Doncaster Rovers===

On 24 May 2019, he signed for League One side [[Doncaster Rovers F.C.|Doncaster Rovers]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brad Halliday: Doncaster Rovers sign Cambridge defender on two-year deal|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48401193 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=24 May 2019 |accessdate=24 May 2019}}</ref>

===Fleetwood Town===

Halliday joined [[Fleetwood Town F.C.|Fleetwood Town]] on a two-year deal on 4 June 2021.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brad Halliday signs for the Cod Army|url=https://www.fleetwoodtownfc.com/news/2021/june/halliday-signs-for-the-cod-army/ |publisher=Fleetwood Town |date=4 June 2021 |accessdate=4 June 2021}}</ref>

=== Bradford City ===
Halliday joined [[Bradford City A.F.C.|Bradford City]] on his birthday – 10 July 2022 – on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |title=BRAD TO BRADFORD |url=https://www.bradfordcityfc.co.uk/news/2022/july/brad-to-bradford/ |access-date=10 July 2022 |website=www.bradfordcityfc.co.uk |language=en-gb }}{{Dead link|date=September 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thetelegraphandargus.co.uk/sport/sportlatest/20269084.bradford-city-sign-former-fleetwood-defender-halliday/|title=Right back Halliday becomes City's 13th summer signing|website=Bradford Telegraph and Argus}}</ref>

He made his 100th appearance for the club on 6 April 2024, scoring the only goal in a 1–0 home victory against Gillingham.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thetelegraphandargus.co.uk/sport/sportlatest/24236264.graham-alexander-praises-bantams-match-winner-brad-halliday/|title='Epitomy of consistency': Halliday deserved City winner says delighted boss|date=6 April 2024|website=Bradford Telegraph and Argus}}</ref> He was Bradford City's Player of the Year for the 2023–24 season.<ref name="POTY2324">{{cite news |url=https://www.thetelegraphandargus.co.uk/sport/sportlatest/24277094.brad-halliday-named-bradford-citys-player-year/?ref=rss |title=Brad Halliday named Bradford City's player of the year |first=Simon |last=Parker |website=Telegraph & Argus |date=25 April 2024 |access-date=25 April 2024}}</ref> At the end of the 2023–24 season, Bradford City triggered a contract extension.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bradfordcityfc.co.uk/news/2024/may/retained-list-202324/|title=RETAINED LIST: 2023/24|website=www.bradfordcityfc.co.uk}}{{Dead link|date=September 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thetelegraphandargus.co.uk/sport/sportlatest/24295712.brad-halliday-bobby-pointon-offered-new-deals-bantams/|title=Bantams make their move to keep Pointon and Halliday for long term|date=2 May 2024|website=Bradford Telegraph and Argus}}</ref>

At the start of the 2024–25 season, Halliday welcomed competition for the first-team with loan signing [[Jay Benn]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thetelegraphandargus.co.uk/sport/24672985.brad-halliday-welcomes-bantams-competition-jay-benn/?ref=rss|title=Halliday happy to help rival Benn in Bantams selection battle|date=24 October 2024|website=Bradford Telegraph and Argus}}</ref>

=== Dundee ===
On 14 January 2026, Halliday joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] on a two-and-a-half year deal after he had his contract with Bradford terminated by mutual consent.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-01-14 |title=Halliday Joins The Dee |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/hallidayjoinsdee/ |access-date=2026-01-14 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref><ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.bradfordcityafc.com/news/2026/january/14/halliday-leaves-city/|title=HALLIDAY LEAVES CITY|website=www.bradfordcityafc.com|date=14 January 2026|accessdate=14 January 2026}}</ref> On 31 January, Halliday made his debut for the ''Dark Blues'' in a league draw away to [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=St Mirren vs Dundee: Scottish Premiership updates & match report|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cgk8pyrrl5jt|website=BBC Sport|access-date=2026-02-01|language=en-GB}}</ref>

'''Simon Murray''' (born 22 March 1992) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|striker]] for {{Scottish football updater|Dundee}} club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].

After beginning his senior career with [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]], Murray played for several [[Scottish Junior Football Association|junior clubs]] before returning to senior football with [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] in 2014. He signed for [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] in January 2015, but initially remained with Arbroath on loan. After two seasons in the United first team, Murray moved to [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in 2017. He spent the latter part of the 2017–18 season on loan at [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], then moved to South African club [[Bidvest Wits F.C.|Bidvest Wits]] in July 2018. He returned to Scotland during 2020, when he signed for [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]], with whom he would lead the side in back-to-back promotions and a rise to the [[Scottish Championship]]. He signed for [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] in January 2023, whom he helped stay in the Premiership for two straight seasons, before returning to Dundee in 2024.

==Early life==
Murray was born in [[Dundee]]. His father [[Gary Murray]] was also a professional footballer, playing for [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]] and [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]].<ref name="Arbroath">{{cite news|last1=Stormont|first1=Brian|title=Murray can't wait to get going|url=http://www.arbroathherald.co.uk/sport/local-sport/murray-can-t-wait-to-get-going-1-3412438|accessdate=6 August 2015|work=Arbroath Herald|date=17 May 2014}}</ref><ref name = "plumber"/> After playing for a number of youth teams, including Dundee Celtic Boys Club, Dee Club and Dundee United Social Club, Murray joined Montrose as a youth player.<ref name=DUFC>{{cite web|title=First Team – Simon Murray|url=http://dufc.co/the-teams/first-team/8970/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150323040139/http://dufc.co/the-teams/first-team/8970/|url-status=usurped|archive-date=23 March 2015|website=Dundee United FC|accessdate=6 August 2015}}</ref>

==Playing career==
===Early career===
Murray began his professional career with Montrose. He made his only appearance for the first team as a substitute against [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] at [[Hampden Park|Hampden]] in May 2011. After a loan spell at Dundee-based junior club [[Downfield F.C.|Downfield]], Murray joined another junior club, [[Tayport F.C.|Tayport]], in February 2012.<ref>{{cite news|title=Murrray leaves Montrose for Tayport|url=http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/murrray-leaves-montrose-for-tayport/|accessdate=6 August 2015|work=Scottish Professional Football League|date=16 February 2012}}</ref>

After leaving Tayport, Murray spent almost a year living in Australia. On his return to Scotland, he briefly played junior football for [[Dundee Violet F.C.|Dundee Violet]] before signing for [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] in May 2014.<ref name=Arbroath /> Murray worked as a plumber while playing for Arbroath.<ref name = "plumber">{{cite news |url=http://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/gary-murray-we-knew-my-hibee-son-simon-would-make-it-1-4519707 |title=Gary Murray: We knew my Hibee son Simon would make it |first=David |last=Hardie |work=Edinburgh Evening News |date=2 August 2017 |accessdate=6 August 2017}}</ref> After scoring 18 goals in 28 matches for Arbroath, Murray was signed by [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] for a £50,000 fee in January 2015.<ref name = "united sign"/> He was immediately loaned back to Arbroath for the rest of the 2014–15 season.<ref name = "united sign">{{cite news|title=Dundee United sign Arbroath striker Simon Murray|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30669644|access-date=6 August 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=4 January 2015}}</ref>

===Dundee United===
Murray made his debut for Dundee United against [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] in August 2015.<ref>{{cite news|title=Dundee United open season with a loss|url=http://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/2015/08/03/dundee-united-open-season-with-a-loss/|accessdate=11 August 2015|work=Evening Telegraph|place=Dundee|date=3 August 2015}}</ref> He scored his first goal six days later, in his first away game for United, the second goal in a 2–0 win at [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Motherwell 0–2 Dundee Utd|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33744529|access-date=11 August 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=8 August 2015}}</ref> Murray scored seven goals for United in the 2015–16 season, as they were relegated to the [[Scottish Championship]].<ref name = "hibs">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40084907 |title=Simon Murray: Striker agrees move to Hibernian from Dundee United |first=Jane |last=Lewis |publisher=BBC Sport |date=29 May 2017 |accessdate=29 May 2017}}</ref>

Murray scored a hat-trick for United in their first home game of the 2016–17 season in a 6–1 win over [[Cowdenbeath F.C.|Cowdenbeath]] in the group stages of the [[2016–17 Scottish League Cup|League Cup]].<ref name="Hattrick">{{cite news|last1=McLauchlin|first1=Brian|title=Dundee United 6–1 Cowdenbeath|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36770667|accessdate=19 July 2016|publisher=BBC Sport|date=19 July 2016}}</ref> He scored 18 goals in all competitions for United in 2016–17.<ref name = "hibs"/> United won the [[2016–17 Scottish Challenge Cup]] and progressed to the Premiership play-off final, but lost 1–0 on aggregate to [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40079605 |title=Dundee United: Boss Ray McKinnon says his side ran out of steam in play-off final |first=Kenny |last=Crawford |publisher=BBC Sport |date=28 May 2017 |accessdate=29 May 2017}}</ref> Murray was sent off for two bookable offences in the first leg, but the second yellow card (and therefore the red) was appealed.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40053822 |title=Dundee Utd's Simon Murray free to face Hamilton after appeal against yellow card |publisher=BBC Sport |date=26 May 2017 |accessdate=29 May 2017}}</ref>

===Hibernian===
Soon after the play-off final defeat, Murray signed for [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]].<ref name = "hibs"/> He scored seven goals in his first four appearances for Hibs, in their [[2017–18 Scottish League Cup group stage|League Cup group]].<ref name = "plumber"/> He then scored on his league debut for Hibs, the third goal in a 3–1 win against [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40761235 |title=Hibernian 3–1 Partick Thistle |first=Jonathan |last=Sutherland |publisher=BBC Sport |date=5 August 2017 |accessdate=6 August 2017}}</ref>
On 24 October 2017, Murray scored the only goal in the [[Edinburgh Derby]] which saw [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] win 1–0 against [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41646985|title=Hibernian 1–0 Hearts|website=bbc.co.uk|first=Tom|last=English|date=24 October 2017|access-date=29 August 2021}}</ref>

==== Dundee (loan) ====
On 31 January 2018, Murray moved to [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] on loan for the remainder of the [[2017–18 Dundee F.C. season|2017–18 season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Hibernian sign Scott Allan, send Simon Murray to Dundee|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42898353|publisher=BBC Sport|date=1 February 2018|accessdate=1 February 2018}}</ref>

===Bidvest Wits===
Hibernian sold Murray to South African club [[Bidvest Wits F.C.|Bidvest Wits]] for an undisclosed fee in July 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/8985 |title=MURRAY COMPLETES MOVE TO BIDVEST WITS |publisher=Hibernian FC |date=23 July 2018 |accessdate=23 July 2018}}</ref> Murray suffered an injury to his [[anterior cruciate ligament]] in 2019, which prevented him from playing for several months.<ref name = return/> He intimated in February 2020 that he would like to return to Scotland.<ref name = return>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/simon-murray-former-hibs-striker-eyes-scotland-return-he-turns-down-extended-south-africa-stay-1556546 |title=Simon Murray: Former Hibs striker eyes Scotland return as he turns down extended South Africa stay |first=Patrick |last=McPartlin |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |date=13 February 2020 |accessdate=13 February 2020}}</ref>

===Queen's Park===
After returning to Scotland, Murray joined [[Scottish League Two|League Two]] club [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] in September 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Simon Murray Joins The Spiders |url=https://queensparkfc.co.uk/simon-murray-joins-the-spiders/ |accessdate=4 September 2020 |publisher=Queen's Park F.C. |date=4 September 2020}}</ref> He scored six goals in eleven appearances in his first season with the club as they were promoted as divisional champions.<ref name="ReferenceA">{{Soccerbase season|58241|2020|access-date=29 December 2020}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite news |date=2021-04-20 |title=Scottish League 2: Queen's Park are champions with four games to spare |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56823461#:~:text=Unbeaten%20Queen's%20Park%20have%20been,after%20a%20three-year%20wait. |access-date=2025-01-22 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 10 September 2021, Murray was awarded with the [[List of Scottish Professional Football League monthly award winners#2021–22 season|Scottish League One Player of the Month]] for August 2021, having scored four goals in five games in the league for that month.<ref name="MURRAY LANDS LEAGUE 1 AWARD">{{cite web|url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/murray-lands-league-1-award|title=MURRAY LANDS LEAGUE 1 AWARD|website=spfl.co.uk|date=10 September 2021|access-date=11 September 2021}}</ref> He was then unavailable for much of the next six months with injury and the team struggled to win matches in his absence, drawing half of the 36 fixtures to finish in fourth place and reach the [[2021–22 Scottish Championship#Championship play-offs|Scottish Championship play-offs]]. On 15 May 2022, fit-again Murray scored the winning goal from the penalty spot during extra time in the second leg of the play-off final to defeat [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] (who had finished runners-up in the regular season, 21 points ahead of Queen's Park); this secured back-to-back promotions for the ''Spiders'', meaning they would compete in the second tier of Scottish football for the first time in nearly forty years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61368166|title=Airdrieonians 1–2 Queen's Park|website= bbc.co.uk|first=Clive|last=Lindsay|date=15 May 2022|access-date=25 June 2022}}</ref>

On 16 June 2022, Murray signed a new one-year contract extension with Queen's Park.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://queensparkfc.co.uk/simon-back-for-another-season/|title=SIMON BACK FOR ANOTHER SEASON|website=queensparkfc.co.uk|date=16 June 2022|access-date=25 June 2022}}</ref> On 7 January 2023, Murray would net 4 goals in a single game against [[Cove Rangers F.C.|Cove Rangers]] in a 0–6 away win which would open up a 4-point gap at the top of the [[Scottish Championship]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Queen's Park thrash Cove to go four points clear |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64132744 |access-date=2023-01-07}}</ref>

===Ross County===
Murray signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] on 31 January 2023 for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64474406 |title=Ross County transfers: Simon Murray joins from Queen's Park |website=BBC Sport |date=31 January 2023 |access-date=31 January 2023}}</ref> The same day, he would make his debut for the ''Staggies'' as a substitute in a league draw at home draw against his former club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=County come from behind to draw with Hibs |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64382318 |access-date=2023-02-01}}</ref> Murray would score a key goal as well as netting in the [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] to help County come back against [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] in the [[2022–23 Scottish Premiership#Final|Premiership play-off final]] to keep them in the top flight.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Ross County stay up after epic play-off comeback |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65736747 |access-date=2023-06-04}}</ref>

Murray would get the [[2023–24 Ross County F.C. season|2023–24 season]] started in style with a hat-trick away from home against [[Stranraer F.C.|Stranraer]] in the [[Scottish League Cup]] group stage.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Stranraer v Ross County |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66148733 |access-date=2023-07-15}}</ref> Murray scored 23 goals in 46 appearances for the ''Staggies'' in a standout season, including 2 goals in the [[2023–24 Scottish Premiership#Premiership play-offs|Premiership play-off final]] against [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] to help keep County in the top tier.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Media |first=P. A. |date=2024-05-26 |title=Ross County breeze past Raith Rovers to seal Scottish Premiership survival |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/article/2024/may/26/ross-county-raith-scottish-premiership-playoff-match-report |access-date=2024-05-26 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-26 |title=Ross County ease past Raith Rovers to ensure Premiership survival |url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/24346853.ross-county-ease-past-raith-rovers-ensure-survival/ |access-date=2024-05-26 |website=The Herald |language=en}}</ref>

=== Return to Dundee ===
On 10 July 2024, Murray returned to his boyhood club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] for an undisclosed fee on a three-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-07-10 |title=Murray's home |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/murrays-home/ |access-date=2024-07-10 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> Murray made his second debut for the club on 16 July as a substitute in an away win over another one of his former clubs, [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]], in the [[Scottish League Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arbroath vs Dundee: League Cup |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c4ngzrxwpxzt |access-date=2024-07-16 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> He opened his scoring account for the ''Dark Blues'' the following week, netting a brace in a win over [[Annan Athletic F.C.|Annan Athletic]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dundee vs Annan Athletic: League Cup |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/ck5g3x3p7r9t |access-date=2024-07-23 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> He followed that up with a 30 minute [[hat-trick]] in a 6–0 demolishing of [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Premier Sports Cup Results {{!}} SPFL |url=https://spfl.co.uk/league/league-cup/results/2441546 |access-date=2024-07-27 |website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref> Murray scored his first league goal for the ''Dee'' on 24 August, netting a late equaliser away to his former club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hibernian vs Dundee: Scottish Premiership |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cp8nzk278ewt |access-date=2024-08-24 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 20 January 2025, Murray scored the only goal in a [[Scottish Cup]] win over [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] to give his boyhood team their first [[Dundee derby]] win since 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dundee vs Dundee United: Scottish Cup live commentary |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cjdenj593znt |access-date=2025-01-20 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Murray continued his derby success on 16 March, scoring a late penalty in Dundee's first win over United at [[Tannadice Park|Tannadice]] in over 20 years on the day after his birthday.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dundee United vs Dundee: Scottish Premiership LIVE - line ups, updates, radio, stats & head-to-head |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cr42d1wpe9vt |access-date=2025-03-16 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

In April 2025, Murray was named as one of four nominees for the 2024–25 [[PFA Scotland Players' Player of the Year]], alongside Celtic's [[Callum McGregor]], [[Nicolas Kühn]] and [[Daizen Maeda]].<ref name=":1">{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cg7245y77yxo|title=Celtic trio and Murray vie for player of the year|date=28 April 2025|publisher=BBC Sport|accessdate=1 May 2025}}</ref> He was also awarded as the [[List of Scottish Professional Football League monthly award winners#2024–25 season|Scottish Premiership Player of the Month]] for April 2025 on the back of a key stretch of goals, having scored 8 goals in 8 league games.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Murray voted Player of the Month {{!}} SPFL |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/murray-voted-player-of-the-month |access-date=2025-05-01 |website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref> The following month, Murray was nominated for the [[SFWA Footballer of the Year|Footballer of the Year]] award by the [[Scottish Football Writers' Association]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=2025-05-07 |title=Dundee striker Simon Murray nominated for SFWA player of the year |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cz797yx792eo |access-date=2025-05-07 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> At the end of the season, Murray also won the club's [[Dundee F.C.#Andrew De Vries Player of the Year|Andrew De Vries Player of the Year]] award and [[Dundee F.C.#Players' Player of the Year|Players' Player of the Year]] award.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |date=18 May 2025 |title=@DundeeFC on X: "The big award of the night! The Andrew De Vries Player of the Year award for 2024/25 goes to Simon Murray!" |url=https://x.com/DundeeFC/status/1924226919454629919 |access-date=18 May 2025 |website=x.com}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite web |date=18 May 2025 |title=@DundeeFC on X: "Simon Murray is the Player's Player of the Season for 2024/25!" |url=https://x.com/DundeeFC/status/1924215499916767582 |access-date=18 May 2025 |website=x.com}}</ref>

On 20 September 2025, Murray opened his account for the [[2025–26 Scottish Premiership|2025–26 league season]] in a home win over [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dundee 3-2 Born in England, he plays for the [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland national team]] at international level. == Club career == ===Urmston Town=== Born in Manchester, O'Hara began his career with local club Urmston Town,{{Cite web|url=http://www.evostikleague.co.uk/welcome-return-for-star-stopper-17088|title=Welcome return for star stopper – The Evo-Stik League Northern Premier|website=www.evostikleague.co.uk|access-date=15 March 2016|archive-date=2 February 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180202071455/http://www.evostikleague.co.uk/welcome-return-for-star-stopper-17088|url-status=dead}} while attending [[Ashton-on-Mersey School|Ashton-on-Mersey School and Sixth Form]].{{Cite web |last=Marshall |first=Adam |date=29 July 2014 |title=Keeper focus: Kieran O'Hara |url=http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Features/2014/Jul/manchester-united-goalkeeper-special-kieran-o-hara.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140804123757/http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Features/2014/Jul/manchester-united-goalkeeper-special-kieran-o-hara.aspx |archive-date=4 August 2014 |access-date=13 August 2022 |website=Manchester United}} ===Manchester United=== He then joined [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] on 1 July 2012, having represented the club at the [[Future Cup]] earlier in the year. Reaching the final before losing to [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] on penalties, the goalkeeper signed on to become an Under-17 Academy student, working with Under-18 coach [[Paul McGuinness (footballer)|Paul McGuinness]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.manutd.com/en/Players-And-Staff/Reserves/Kieran-O-Hara.aspx|title=Kieran O'Hara|website=ManUtd.com|access-date=15 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304085931/http://www.manutd.com/en/Players-And-Staff/Reserves/Kieran-O-Hara.aspx|archive-date=4 March 2016|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}} ====Loan moves==== His chances were limited in his first season with the youth team, and he was soon given a work-experience loan with [[Trafford F.C.|Trafford]] throughout the 2013–14 season. Upon his return, and having faced his first taste of senior football, O'Hara was promoted to the Under-21 squad. Despite his continued difficulty in breaking into the starting XI, with [[Joel Castro Pereira]] the preferred goalkeeper, O'Hara signed a professional deal with the Reds in the summer of 2014.{{Cite web|url=http://www.ibtimes.co.uk/manchester-united-loan-report-goalkeepers-kieran-ohara-dean-henderson-both-sent-elsewhere-1537711|title=Manchester United loan report: Goalkeepers Kieran O'Hara and Dean Henderson both sent elsewhere|website=International Business Times UK|date=13 January 2016|access-date=15 March 2016}} Making a single appearance for the Under-21s, he soon faced further loan spells in a bid to impress the coaching staff at [[Old Trafford]]. After a one-month loan with [[National League North|Conference North]] title-contenders [[A.F.C. Fylde|AFC Fylde]],{{Cite web|url=http://nonleague.pitchero.com/news/coasters-borrow-manchester-united-keeper-37097/|title=Coasters Borrow Manchester United Keeper|last=Whitney|first=Steve|website=Pitchero Non-League|date=31 January 2015|access-date=15 March 2016}} O'Hara was given his first opportunity for United in the final game of the [[Professional Development League|Under-21 Premier League]] season. Following 15 games as an unused substitute, he completed 90 minutes in a 3–1 defeat to [[Manchester City F.C. Reserves and Academy|Manchester City]], with his side already crowned league champions.{{Cite web|url=http://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/manchester-united-transfer-news-kieran-10505535|title=Manchester United goalkeeper leaves on loan|last=Luckhurst|first=Samuel|work=Manchester Evening News|date=26 November 2015|publisher=MEN Media|access-date=15 March 2016}} O'Hara opted for senior football once more during the 2015–16 season, and completed a deadline day move to [[Football League Two|League Two]] club [[Morecambe F.C.|Morecambe]] on a one-month loan in the summer.{{Cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/12956/9975553/manchester-united-goalkeeper-kieran-ohara-joins-morecambe-on-loan|title=Manchester United goalkeeper Kieran O'Hara joins Morecambe on loan|website=Sky Sports|access-date=15 March 2016}} He later faced a one-month loan spell with [[National League North]] club [[Stockport County F.C.|Stockport County]] in November, before returning to [[Morecambe F.C.|Morecambe]] for the remainder of the season on 12 January.{{Cite web|url=http://www.manutd.com/en/Players-And-Staff/Reserves/Reserves-News/2016/Jan/loan-moves-agreed-for-manchester-united-goalkeepers-kieran-o%27hara-and-dean-henderson.aspx|title=Loan moves agreed 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160316013428/http://www.manutd.com/en/Players-And-Staff/Reserves/Reserves-News/2016/Jan/loan-moves-agreed-for-manchester-united-goalkeepers-kieran-o%27hara-and-dean-henderson.aspx|archive-date=16 March 2016|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}} Having failed to make a competitive appearance in his first spell with the Shrimps, O'Hara made his professional debut in a 3–1 defeat to league leaders [[Northampton Town F.C.|Northampton Town]] on 23 January 2016.{{Cite web |date=23 January 2016 |title=Northampton Town 3-1 Morecambe |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35330871 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160130014432/http://www.bbc.com/sport/football/35330871 |archive-date=30 January 2016 |access-date=13 August 2022 |website=BBC}} On 15 August 2018, O'Hara joined League Two side [[Macclesfield Town F.C.|Macclesfield Town]] on loan for the 2018–19 season.{{Cite web|url=https://www.mtfc.co.uk/news/2018/august/15.08.18-silkmen-sign-united-stopper|title=Silkmen Sign Manchester United Stopper|publisher=Macclesfield Town FC|date=15 August 2018|access-date=16 August 2018}} O'Hara was Macclesfield's first-choice goalkeeper for the 2018–19 season, making 37 appearances in the league, as well as a further five in cup competitions, including Macclesfield's 8–0 loss to [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] in the third round of the [[2018–19 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]].{{cite news |title=West Ham 8-0 Macclesfield: Hammers thrash Macclesfield to reach fourth round |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45569334 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=26 September 2018 |access-date=8 July 2019 }} A draw with [[Cambridge United F.C.|Cambridge United]] saw Macclesfield remain in the Football League, helped greatly by O'Hara's performances in goal; his form over the course of the season saw him named as Macclesfield's Player of the Year, Players' Player of the Year and Young Player of the Year.{{cite news |first=Adam |last=Marshall |title=O'Hara ends the season on a real high '''Alan James Forrest''' (born 9 September 1996) is a [[Scottish people|Scottish]] [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as an [[attacking midfielder]] or [[right midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|Dundee}} club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Scotland - A. Forrest - Profile with news, career statistics and history - Soccerway |url=https://uk.soccerway.com/players/alan-forrest/303505/ |access-date=2024-07-15 |website=uk.soccerway.com}}</ref>

Born in [[Prestwick]], he began his career with [[Ayr United]], coming through their academy and making 245 appearances for the ''Honest Men''. Forrest then spent two seasons with Scottish Premiership side [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]], before joining [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]], where he made over 140 appearances in four seasons.

He is the younger brother of [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] and [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] winger [[James Forrest (footballer, born 1991)|James Forrest]];<ref name="Alan Forrest Ayr United Player Profile"/> their sister Lisa is also a footballer.<ref>[https://glasgowcityfc.co.uk/blogs/latest/lisa-forrest-signs-first-city-professional-contract Lisa Forrest signs first City professional contract], Glasgow City FC, 18 January 2023</ref><ref>[https://www.pressreader.com/uk/sunday-mail-uk/20230611/282978224404454 Brother's advice has given me new Lisa life], Alison McConnell, ''Sunday Mail'', 11 June 2023, via [[PressReader]]</ref>

==Club career==

=== Ayr United ===
Forrest made his debut for [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] in a [[Scottish Challenge Cup]] match against [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]]. He came off the bench to score an 89th-minute winner at [[Hampden Park]]. With this goal Forrest became Ayr's youngest ever goalscorer aged 16 years, 321 days.<ref name="Alan Forrest Ayr United Player Profile">{{cite web | url=http://www.ayrunitedfc.co.uk/player/alan-forrest/ | title=Alan Forrest Ayr United Player Profile | work=Ayr United | access-date=10 July 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161008230349/http://www.ayrunitedfc.co.uk/player/alan-forrest/|archive-date=8 October 2016}}</ref>

During the [[2019–20 Scottish Championship]] season, Forrest was awarded the [[List of Scottish Professional Football League monthly award winners|Scottish Championship Player of the Month]] for September after scoring five goals in three league games.<ref name="Alan Forrest wins award">{{cite web |url=https://ayrunitedfc.co.uk/alan-forrest-wins-award/ |title=Alan Forrest wins award  |publisher=Ayr United FC |date=4 October 2019 |access-date=10 November 2019}}</ref>

=== Livingston ===
Forrest signed a pre-contract deal with [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] on 10 April 2020, making the jump from the [[Scottish Championship]] to the [[Scottish Premiership]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Alan Forrest: Pre-Contract Agreement |url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/alan-forrest-pre-contract-agreement/ |website=Livingston FC |access-date=25 June 2021 |date=2020-04-10}}</ref> Forrest made his debut for Livingston on the opening day of the [[2020–21 Scottish Premiership]] season in a 1–0 loss against [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] at [[St Mirren Park]]. He scored his first goal for Livingston in a 2–2 draw against [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] on 12 August 2020, at [[Fir Park]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/motherwell-vs-livingston/425579 |title=Motherwell 2-2 Livingston - Match Report & Highlights |work=[[Sky Sports]] |publisher=Sky Sports |date=12 August 2020 |access-date=30 September 2020}}</ref>

=== Heart of Midlothian ===
On 1 June 2022, it was announced that Forrest would join [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] on a two-year deal, following the expiry of his Livingston contract on 10 June.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/alan-forrest-hearts-confirm-signing-of-winger-from-livingston-on-2-year-deal-3717380|title=Hearts confirm signing of winger from Livingston on 2-year deal|date=2022-06-01|access-date=2022-06-04|language=en-GB| publisher=[[The Scotsman]] | work=scotsman.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/news/article/alan-forrest-is-our-first-summer-recruit|title=Alan Forrest Is Our First Summer Recruit|date=2022-06-01|access-date=2022-06-04|language=en-GB| publisher=[[Heart of Midlothian F.C.]] | work=heartsfc.co.uk}}</ref> In an [[Edinburgh derby]] match on 7 October 2023, Forrest scored a stunning long-range goal which later won the club's goal of the season award.<ref>{{cite news |last=McPheat |first=Nick |date=7 October 2023 |title=Hearts 2-2 Hibernian: 'Total madness' as quickfire Elie Youan double earns visitors unlikely draw |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66969131 |work=BBC Scotland |location=Glasgow, Scotland |publisher=BBC |access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/player-of-the-year-2023-24 | title= Player of the Year - 2023/24 | publisher = HMFC | date=29 April 2024 | access-date=11 May 2024}}</ref> On 19 January 2024, he signed a two-year extension to his contract until 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Forrest signs new contract – Hearts |url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/forrest-signs-new-contract |access-date=2024-07-15 |website=www.heartsfc.co.uk |language=en}}</ref> 

After four years and 147 appearances with the club, Forrest departed at the end of his contract in July 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Four players leaving Tynecastle
|url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/three-players-leaving-tynecastle |access-date=8 July 2026 |website=Heart of Midlothian F.C.}}</ref>

=== Dundee ===
On 13 July 2026, Forrest joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] on a two-year deal with the option of a third.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-07-13 |title=Alan Forrest joins Dundee FC |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/alan-forrest-joins-dundee-fc/ |access-date=2026-07-13 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> He made his debut on 21 July as a substitute in a [[Scottish League Cup]] group stage match away to [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Text |first=Live |title=Ross County vs Dundee: Scottish League Cup updates & report |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c4gvlv1pe3nt |access-date=2026-07-22 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> In their next game, Forrest scored his first goal for the ''Dee'' at home to [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Text |first=Live |title=Dundee 4-0 Clyde: Four second-half goals take hosts through in League Cup |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/ce8lnne93xet |access-date=2026-07-25 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

== International career ==
In 2016, Forrest made his debut for the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21]] team in a friendly against [[Slovakia national under-21 football team|Slovakia]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/37930204 |title=International friendly: Slovakia U21 4–0 Scotland U21 |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=9 November 2016 |access-date=9 November 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fitbastats.com/scotlandu21/player.php?playerid=620 |title=Scotland U21 profile |publisher=Fitbastats.com|access-date=19 June 2017}}</ref>

Born in England, he represents the [[Kenya national football team|Kenya national team]]. ==Club career== ===Early career=== Ayunga started his career at Bridport Youth in 2007 and was in the squad for the Dorset County under-16s representative team.{{cite news|title=Siblings in selection for Dorset|url=http://www.dorsetecho.co.uk/news/9989143.Siblings_in_selection_for_Dorset/|publisher=Dorset Echo|date=17 October 2012|accessdate=4 November 2017}} In July 2015, Ayunga went on a trial at [[Dorchester Town F.C.|Dorchester Town]] and impressed the side in the pre-season.{{cite news|title=Magies: Heath hails ace Ayunga|url=http://www.dorsetecho.co.uk/sport/13439214.Magies__Heath_hails_ace_Ayunga/|publisher=Dorset Echo|date=16 July 2015|accessdate=4 November 2017}} As a result, Ayunga was signed by Dorchester Town, signing a 12-month contract on 19 July 2015.{{cite news|title=Magpies: Ace Ayunga pens Avenue deal and Nicholls is poised to return|url=http://www.dorsetecho.co.uk/sport/13464067.Magpies__Ace_Ayunga_pens_Avenue_deal_and_Nicholls_is_poised_to_return/|publisher=Dorset Echo|date=19 July 2015|accessdate=4 November 2017}} He made his Dorchester Town debut in the opening game of the season, scoring in a 3–0 win over [[Histon F.C.|Histon]], followed up by scoring in a 4–2 win over [[Cirencester Town F.C.|Cirencester Town]].{{cite news|title=Magpies: Perfect start to season for Dorchester Town|url=http://www.dorsetecho.co.uk/sport/13583537.Magpies__Perfect_start_to_season_for_Dorchester_Town/|publisher=Dorset Echo|date=9 August 2015|accessdate=4 November 2017}}
{{cite news|title=Magpies: Late penalty seals Dorchester Town's fate in thriller|url=http://www.dorsetecho.co.uk/sport/13588576.Magpies__Late_penalty_seals_Dorchester_s_fate_in_thriller/|publisher=Dorset Echo|date=11 August 2015|accessdate=4 November 2017}} By the time of his departure, Ayunga made 31 appearances, scoring seven times during his spell at the club. Dorchester manager, [[Mark Jermyn]] described him as "an exciting young talent" and a "strong and powerful center forward".{{cite news|title=Magpies: Dorchester Town ace Jonah hailed as a top talent by boss Jermyn|url=http://www.dorsetecho.co.uk/sport/14217759.Magpies__Ace_Jonah_hailed_as_a_top_talent_by_boss_Jermyn/|publisher=Dorset Echo|date=21 February 2016|accessdate=4 November 2017}} ===Brighton & Hove Albion=== It was agreed that Ayunga agreed a move to [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]] on 31 January 2016.{{cite web|url=http://dorchestertownfc.co.uk/2016/01/31/statement-jonah-agrees-terms-with-brighton-and-hove-albion/|title=STATEMENT: Jonah agrees terms with Brighton and Hove Albion|publisher=Dorchester Town F.C.|date=31 January 2016|accessdate=4 November 2017|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20171104172320/http://dorchestertownfc.co.uk/2016/01/31/statement-jonah-agrees-terms-with-brighton-and-hove-albion/|archivedate=4 November 2017|url-status=live|df=dmy-all}} The move was confirmed on 1 February 2016 for £40,000, with the transfer fee being touted as "the biggest receipt in the history of Dorchester Town FC".{{cite web|url=http://dorchestertownfc.co.uk/2016/02/01/jonah-ayunga-seals-move-to-brighton-and-hove-albion/|title=Jonah Ayunga seals move to Brighton and Hove Albion|publisher=Dorchester Town F.C.|date=1 February 2016|accessdate=4 November 2017|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20171104172335/http://dorchestertownfc.co.uk/2016/02/01/jonah-ayunga-seals-move-to-brighton-and-hove-albion/|archivedate=4 November 2017|url-status=live|df=dmy-all}} He made his debut in a 4–1 friendly defeat to [[Arsenal F.C. Reserves|Arsenal U21]], his coach at Brighton described him as a "good player and natural goal scorer".{{cite web|url=https://www.brightonandhovealbion.com/news/2016/february/under-21s-face-arsenal-today/|title=UNDER-21S FACE ARSENAL TODAY|publisher=Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|date=5 February 2016|accessdate=4 November 2017|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20171104192257/https://www.brightonandhovealbion.com/news/2016/february/under-21s-face-arsenal-today/|archivedate=4 November 2017|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}
{{cite web|url=https://www.brightonandhovealbion.com/news/2016/february/u21-report-arsenal-4-albion-1/|title=U21 REPORT: ARSENAL 4 ALBION 1|publisher=Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|date=5 February 2016|accessdate=4 November 2017|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20171104192306/https://www.brightonandhovealbion.com/news/2016/february/u21-report-arsenal-4-albion-1/|archivedate=4 November 2017|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}} It wasn't until on 11 April 2016 when he scored his first Brighton & Hove Albion U23, in a 4–1 win over [[Newcastle United F.C. Reserves and Academy|Newcastle United U23]].{{cite web|url=https://www.brightonandhovealbion.com/news/2016/april/u21-report-newcastle-1-albion-4/|title=U21 REPORT: NEWCASTLE 1 ALBION 4|publisher=Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|date=11 April 2016|accessdate=4 November 2017|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20171104192550/https://www.brightonandhovealbion.com/news/2016/april/u21-report-newcastle-1-albion-4/|archivedate=4 November 2017|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}} In the summer pre-season tour of 2016, Ayunga played against his former club, Dorchester Town, which saw Brighton & Hove Albion U21 won 7–0 in July 2016.{{cite news|title=Magpies: Top night for Jonah on return to the Avenue|url=http://www.dorsetecho.co.uk/sport/14636564.Magpies__Top_night_for_Jonah_on_return_to_the_Avenue/|publisher=Dorset Echo|date=22 July 2016|accessdate=4 November 2017}} On 24 October 2016, Jonah was sent on a month long loan to English 7th tier side Burgess Hill Town,{{cite web|last1=Korir|first1=Patrick|title=English side Brighton loans out Kenyan striker|url=http://www.soka.co.ke/news/item/english-side-brighton-loans-out-kenyan-striker}} he scored his first goal at Burgess in a 5-1 thumping of Beaconsfield SYCOB{{cite web|last1=Korir|first1=Patrick|title=Ayunga opens account at Burgess Hill|url=http://www.soka.co.ke/stars-abroad/item/ayunga-opens-account-at-burgess-hill}} After making 10 appearances, Ayunga's loan spell at [[Burgess Hill Town F.C.|Burgess Hill Town]] came to an end. On 23 January 2017, Ayunga joined Irish side [[Sligo Rovers F.C.|Sligo Rovers]] on loan for the [[2017 League of Ireland Premier Division|2017]] campaign.{{Cite news|title=Jonah Ayunga signs!|url=http://www.sligorovers.com/news/17/jan/jonah-ayunga-signs|publisher=Sligo Rovers Official Site|date=23 January 2017|accessdate=23 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202034124/http://www.sligorovers.com/news/17/jan/jonah-ayunga-signs|archive-date=2 February 2017|url-status=dead}} He made his Sligo Rovers debut in the opening game of the season, in a 5–1 loss against [[Limerick F.C.|Limerick]].{{cite news|title=League Report: Limerick 5 - 1 Sligo Rovers|url=http://www.extratime.ie/articles/18404/league-report-limerick-5---1-sligo-rovers/|publisher=Extra Time Irish|date=24 February 2017|accessdate=4 November 2017}} However, in a follow-up match against [[Dundalk F.C.|Dundalk]] on 4 March 2017, he was sent-off for a second bookable offence, in a 4–0 loss.{{cite news|title=Dundalk inflict Sligo's second thrashing in two games|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/soccer/national-league/dundalk-inflict-sligo-s-second-thrashing-in-two-games-1.2998360|publisher=The Irish Times|date=4 March 2017|accessdate=4 November 2017}} After returning from suspension, Ayunga then scored his first goal for the club, in a 2–0 win over [[Bohemian F.C.|Bohemians]] on 8 April 2017.{{cite news|title=Sligo secure all three points against Bohs|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/soccer/national-league/sligo-secure-all-three-points-against-bohs-1.3042423|publisher=The Irish Times|date=8 April 2017|accessdate=4 November 2017}} He went on to score two more goals against [[Drogheda United F.C.|Drogheda United]] and Limerick.{{cite news|title=Ayunga rescues point for Rovers|url=https://www.independent.ie/regionals/sligochampion/sport/soccer/ayunga-rescues-point-for-rovers-35670214.html|publisher=The Irish Independent|date=6 May 2017|accessdate=4 November 2017}} He went on to make 22 appearances and scoring 4 times in all competitions before his loan has terminated on the 31 July 2017.{{cite news|title=Sligo Rovers to ramp up efforts to land former Celtic star Paddy McCourt|url=http://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/soccer/soccer-news/sligo-rovers-ramp-up-efforts-10884523|publisher=The Irish Mirror|date=28 July 2017|accessdate=4 November 2017}} On 31 July 2017, Ayunga joined Irish side [[Galway United F.C.|Galway United]] on loan for the remainder of the [[2017 League of Ireland Premier Division|2017]] campaign.{{cite news|title=Galway United striker Jonah Ayunga on loan from Brighton & Hove Albion|url=http://www.extratime.ie/articles/19491/galway-united-striker-jonah-ayunga-on-loan-from-brighton-hove-albion/|publisher=Extra Times Irish|date=31 July 2017|accessdate=4 November 2017}} He made his Galway United debut on 4 August 2017, in a 2–1 win over [[Finn Harps F.C.|Finn Harps]].,{{cite news|title=Galway boost survival chances against 10-man Finn Harps|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/soccer/2017/0804/895364-galway-united/|publisher=RTE Sport|date=4 August 2017|accessdate=4 November 2017}} Ayunga's loan with [[Galway United F.C.|Galway United]] was cut short after just four games through injury.{{cite news|title=Broken leg cuts short Jonah Ayunga's loan spell with Galway United|url=http://www.extratime.ie/articles/19681/broken-leg-cuts-short-jonah-ayungas-loan-spell-galway-united/|publisher=Extra Time Irish|date=1 September 2017|accessdate=4 November 2017}} ===Sutton United=== Ayunga signed for Sutton United in the summer of 2018, following his release by Brighton.{{Cite news|url=https://www.suttonunited.net/player/jonah-ayunga/|title=Jonah Ayunga - Sutton United Football Club|work=Sutton United Football Club|access-date=2018-11-01|language=en-GB}} On 4 September 2018, he made his debut during a 1–0 victory over [[Maidstone United F.C.|Maidstone United]], featuring for 65 minutes before being replaced by Tommy Wright.{{Cite news |title=Maidstone United vs. Sutton United |url=https://uk.soccerway.com/matches/2018/09/04/england/conference-national/maidstone-united-fc/sutton-united-fc/2817474/ |publisher=Soccerway |date=4 September 2018 |accessdate=16 May 2019}} Just United |url=https://uk.soccerway.com/matches/2018/09/29/england/conference-national/leyton-orient-fc/sutton-united-fc/2817532/ |publisher=Soccerway |date=29 September 2018 |accessdate=16 May 2019}} On 24 November 2018, Ayunga made the switch to fellow [[National League (division)|National League]] side, [[Havant & Waterlooville F.C.|Havant & Waterlooville]] on a three-month loan.{{Cite news |title=Jonah Ayunga joins the Hawks on loan |url=https://www.havantandwaterloovillefc.co.uk/articles/2018/11/24/jonah-ayunga-joins-the-hawks-on-loan.html |publisher=[[Havant & Waterlooville F.C.]] |date=24 November 2018 |accessdate=16 May 2019}} On the same day, Ayunga went onto net on his debut during a 5–2 victory over Maidstone United, netting Havant's second in the 35th minute.{{Cite news |title=Havant & Waterlooville vs. Maidstone United |url=https://uk.soccerway.com/matches/2018/11/24/england/conference-national/havant-and-waterlooville-fc/maidstone-united-fc/2817616/ |publisher=Soccerway |date=24 November 2018 |accessdate=16 May 2019}} Three days later, he continued his good form, netting a late consolation goal in Havant's 3–1 defeat against [[Dagenham & Redbridge F.C.|Dagenham & Redbridge]].{{Cite news |title=Dagenham & Redbridge vs. Havant & Waterlooville |url=https://uk.soccerway.com/matches/2018/11/27/england/conference-national/dagenham--redbridge-fc/havant-and-waterlooville-fc/2817624/ |publisher=Soccerway |date=27 November 2018 |accessdate=16 May 2019}} Following his impressive form, Ayunga returned to Sutton prematurely and went onto feature seventeen more times, scoring twice before leaving at the end of the campaign. ===Havant & Waterlooville=== On 14 May 2019, Ayunga agreed to return to Havant, following their relegation to the [[National League South]].{{Cite news |title=Jonah Ayunga joins the Hawks permanently |url=https://www.havantandwaterloovillefc.co.uk/articles/jonah-ayunga-joins-the-hawks-permanently.html |publisher=[[Havant & Waterlooville F.C.]] |date=14 May 2019 |accessdate=16 May 2019}} Before the early conclusion of the season, Ayunga had scored seventeen goals in the league, seeing him win the Golden Boot award in a three-way tie along with [[Darren McQueen|McQueen]] of [[Dartford F.C.|Dartford]] and [[Joe Iaciofano|Iaciofano]] of [[St Albans City F.C.|St Albans City]].{{cite web|url= https://www.havantandwaterloovillefc.co.uk/jonah-ayunga-shares-golden-boot/|title=Jonah Ayunga Shares Golden Boot|website=www.havantandwaterloovillefc.co.uk|date=27 July 2020}} The season ultimately ended in disappointment for Ayunga and Havant as they were defeated 2–1 in the play off semi-final by Dartford after Ayunga had given his side the lead.{{cite web|url= https://www.havantandwaterloovillefc.co.uk/match/havant-and-waterlooville-play-off-semi-final/#hwfc_match_report|title=Havant and Waterlooville play-off semi final|website=www.havantandwaterloovillefc.co.uk|date=25 July 2020|accessdate=29 July 2020}} ===Bristol Rovers=== On 29 July 2020, Ayunga signed for [[EFL League One|League One]] side [[Bristol Rovers F.C.|Bristol Rovers]] for an undisclosed fee, signing a two-year deal.{{cite web|url=https://www.bristolrovers.co.uk/news/2020/july/jonah-ayunga-joins|title=Jonah Ayunga Joins the Gas!|website=www.bristolrovers.co.uk|date=29 July 2020|accessdate=29 July 2020|archive-date=29 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200729085828/https://www.bristolrovers.co.uk/news/2020/july/jonah-ayunga-joins|url-status=dead}} He made his debut for the club on 5 September 2020, in a 3–0 [[EFL Cup|League Cup]] defeat to [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]], replacing [[Cameron Hargreaves]] from the bench at half time.{{cite web|url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53955732|title=Ipswich Town 3-0 Bristol Rovers|publisher=BBC Sport|date=5 September 2020}} He made his first start for the club the following Tuesday in a 2–2 draw contract.{{cite web|url=https://www.morecambefc.com/news/2021/july/signing--jonah-ayunga/|title=SIGNING : Jonah Ayunga|website=www.morecambefc.com|date=26 July 2021}} After surviving relegation in web|url=https://www.morecambefc.com/news/2022/may/retained-list-announced/|title=Retained List announced|website=www.morecambefc.com|date=2 May 2022|accessdate=5 May 2022}} ===St Mirren=== Ayunga web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cgrnp913714o|title=Ayunga commits to Saints until 2025|publisher=BBC Sport|date=14 September 2023}} Ayunga scored twice against Celtic in the [[2025 '''Thomas Richard Lowery''' (born 31 December 1997) is a Welsh professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].

==Club career==
===Crewe Alexandra===
[[File:Tommy Lowery.jpg|thumb|left|Tom Lowery at Crawley Town (2018)]]
A graduate of the [[Crewe Alexandra F.C.|Crewe Alexandra]] [[Crewe Alexandra F.C. Academy|Academy]], Lowery signed his first professional contract with the club in May 2016.<ref name="Chron06052016">{{cite news|last1=Morse|first1=Peter|title=Tom Lowery signs first pro deal with Crewe Alex|url=http://www.crewechronicle.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/tom-lowery-signs-first-pro-11296813|accessdate=9 October 2016|work=Crewe Chronicle|date=6 May 2016}}</ref> He made his Crewe debut on 4 October 2016, coming on as a second-half substitute in an [[EFL Trophy]] tie against [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers U23s]] at Gresty Road.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|title=Tom Lowery|url=http://www.soccerbase.com/players/player.sd?player_id=97009|website=Soccerbase|accessdate=9 October 2016}}</ref>

The diminutive midfielder made what was regarded as a "sparkling" league debut four days later,<ref name="Morse-09Oct2016">{{cite news |last1=Morse |first1=Peter |title=OPINION: Crewe Alex's 'Miniesta' is one for the future |url=https://www.crewechronicle.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/opinion-crewe-alexs-miniesta-one-11998679 |access-date=28 April 2022 |work=Crewe Chronicle |date=9 October 2016}}</ref> coming on at half-time against [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]] at Kenilworth Road on 8 October 2016.<ref name="Chron09/10/2016">{{cite news|last1=Morse|first1=Peter|title=Luton Town 1 Crewe Alex 1|url=http://www.crewechronicle.co.uk/sport/football/match-reports/match-luton-town-1-crewe-11994300|accessdate=9 October 2016|work=Crewe Chronicle|date=8 October 2016}}</ref> Nicknamed 'Miniesta', Lowery was described as "hungry for the ball and composed and inventive with it at his feet".<ref name="Morse-09Oct2016"/> A week later, he was in Crewe's starting line-up at [[Notts County F.C.|Notts County]].

In January 2018, Lowery signed a new three-and-a-half-year contract at Crewe.<ref name="CAnet-15Jan2018">{{cite web|title=Contract: Tommy Lowery Pens New Long-Term Deal|url=https://www.crewealex.net/news/2018/january/contract-tommy-lowery-pens-new-long-term-deal/|website=CreweAlex.net|accessdate=19 January 2018}}</ref> He scored his first goal for Crewe in a 2–0 defeat of [[Yeovil Town F.C.|Yeovil Town]] at Gresty Road on 19 April 2019,<ref name="BBC-19Apr2019">{{cite news |title=Crewe Alexandra 2-0 Yeovil Town |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47904337 |accessdate=20 April 2019 |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=19 April 2019}}</ref> in his 50th League appearance.

In January 2020, after 36 Crewe appearances during the season, Lowery suffered a pelvic injury which ruled him out of several games.<ref name="Morse-10Mar2020">{{cite news |last1=Morse |first1=Peter |title=Crewe Alex playing it safe with Tom Lowery after two failed comebacks |url=https://www.cheshire-live.co.uk/sport/football/crewe-alex-playing-safe-tom-17896957 |accessdate=10 March 2020 |work=Cheshire Live |date=10 March 2020}}</ref> In October 2020, Lowery signed a new two-year contract.<ref name="Johnson-14Oct2020">{{cite news |last1=Johnson |first1=Steve |title=Lowery Signs Contract Extension |url=https://www.crewealex.net/news/2020/october/lowery-signs-new-deal/#:~:text=We're%20delighted%20to%20announce,a%20professional%20contract%20in%202016. |accessdate=19 October 2020 |work=Vital Football |date=14 October 2020}}</ref>

He played no part in Crewe's July 2021 pre-season games after negotiations over a new contract stalled.<ref name="CAFC-21Jul2021">{{cite news |title=Boss Makes Stance Over Lowery's Decision Not To Sign New Deal |url=https://www.crewealex.net/news/2021/july/sign-no-deal-tom/ |access-date=23 July 2021 |work=CreweAlex.net |date=21 July 2021}}</ref> As the contract impasse continued into August,<ref name="CAFC-05Aug2021">{{cite web |title=No Movement On Lowery Contract |url=https://www.crewealex.net/news/2021/august/no-movement-on-lowery-contract/ |website=Crewe Alexandra F.C. |access-date=26 August 2021}}</ref> Lowery only played an under-23s game on 16 August 2021 due to a shortage of players caused by a sickness bug; he did not otherwise feature for Crewe during the first weeks of the season.<ref name="CAFC-17Aug2021">{{cite web |title=Boss: "Tommy Played For Under-23s But Don't Read Anything Into It" |url=https://www.crewealex.net/news/2021/august/artell-lowery-and-under-23s/ |website=Crewe Alexandra F.C. |access-date=26 August 2021}}</ref> He eventually made his season debut on 31 August in a 1–0 victory at [[Shrewsbury Town F.C.|Shrewsbury Town]] in an EFL Trophy group tie,<ref name="CAFC-31Aug2021">{{cite news |title=Shrewsbury 0-1 Crewe |url=https://www.crewealex.net/news/2021/august/shrewsbury-0-1-crewe/ |access-date=1 September 2021 |work=CreweAlex.net |date=31 August 2021}}</ref> as manager [[David Artell]] looked to conclude further talks with Lowery and his agent,<ref name="CAFCTom-01Sep2021">{{cite news |title="The Truth Is I Don't Want Tom Not To Be Playing Football" |url=https://www.crewealex.net/news/2021/september/truth-is-i-dont-want-tom-not-playing/ |access-date=1 September 2021 |work=CreweAlex.net |date=1 September 2021}}</ref> but the talks stalled again in early September.<ref name="CAFC-07Sep2021">{{cite news |title=Back To Square One Over Lowery Contract Dispute |url=https://www.crewealex.net/news/2021/september/back-to-square-one-over-lowery/ |access-date=8 September 2021 |work=CreweAlex.net |date=7 September 2021}}</ref> He eventually resumed league appearances, coming on as a second-half substitute and scoring Crewe's goal in a 2–1 defeat at [[Wycombe Wanderers F.C.|Wycombe Wanderers]] on 23 October 2021.<ref name="BBC-23Oct2021">{{cite news |title=Wycombe Wanderers 2-1 Crewe Alexandra |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58936109 |access-date=23 October 2021 |work=BBC Sport |date=23 October 2021}}</ref> He scored three further goals as Crewe were relegated from League One; manager [[Alex Morris (footballer)|Alex Morris]], who had replaced Artell, did not expect Lowery to extend his Crewe career beyond the end of the season.<ref name="BBC-26Apr2022">{{cite news |title=Alex Morris: Crewe interim boss says managerial uncertainty will not affect response to relegation |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61227841 |access-date=27 April 2022 |work=BBC Sport |date=26 April 2022}}</ref>

===Portsmouth===
On 5 August 2022, Lowery joined League One [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]] on a three-year contract,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.portsmouthfc.co.uk/news/2022/august/pompey-sign-lowery/|title=Pompey Sign Lowery|website=www.portsmouthfc.co.uk|date=5 August 2022|accessdate=6 August 2022}}</ref> making his Pompey debut as a second-half substitute in a 3–0 [[EFL League Cup]] first round win at [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]] on 9 August 2022.<ref name="BBC-09Aug2022">{{cite news |title=Cardiff City 0-3 Portsmouth |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/62387893 |access-date=11 August 2022 |work=BBC Sport |date=9 August 2022}}</ref> During his 10th appearance, on 17 September 2022 against [[Plymouth Argyle F.C.|Plymouth Argyle]], Lowery suffered a hamstring injury which ruled him out of League action until March 2023.<ref name="Lacey-07Mar2023">{{cite news |last1=Lacey |first1=Pepe |title=Tom Lowery details Portsmouth injury nightmare - and promise to Fratton faithful after completing long-awaited comeback |url=https://www.portsmouth.co.uk/sport/football/portsmouth-fc/tom-lowery-details-portsmouth-injury-nightmare-and-promise-to-fratton-faithful-after-completing-long-awaited-comeback-4051351 |access-date=8 March 2023 |work=The News (Portsmouth) |date=7 March 2023}}</ref> In the opening game of the 2023–2024 season on 5 August 2023, Lowery suffered a torn [[Meniscus (anatomy)|meniscus]] in his knee, requiring surgery and a lengthy recovery period,<ref name="Cross-16Aug2023">{{cite news |last1=Cross |first1=Jordan |title=Portsmouth boss outlines transfer plan after midfielder's hit with lengthy injury |url=https://www.portsmouth.co.uk/sport/football/portsmouth-fc/latest-portsmouth-boss-outlines-transfer-plan-after-midfielders-hit-with-lengthy-injury-4257287 |access-date=29 November 2023 |work=The News |date=16 August 2023}}</ref><ref name="Cross-29Nov2023">{{cite news |last1=Cross |first1=Jordan |title=Portsmouth boss responds to 'injury prone' jibes as midfielder closes in on return |url=https://www.portsmouth.co.uk/sport/football/portsmouth-fc/pompey-portsmouth-league-one-tom-lowery-4427258 |access-date=29 November 2023 |work=The News |date=29 November 2023}}</ref> eventually returning to the first team in January 2024.

====Crewe Alexandra (loan)====
On 30 January 2025, Lowery returned to Crewe Alexandra on loan for the remainder of the 2024–25 season,<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.crewealex.net/news/2025/january/30/lowery-returns-on-loan/|title=Lowery returns on loan|website=www.crewealex.net|date=30 January 2025|accessdate=30 January 2025}}</ref> making his first appearance in Crewe's 1–1 draw at [[Harrogate Town F.C.|Harrogate Town]] on 1 February 2025,<ref>{{cite news |title=Harrogate Town 1-1 Crewe Alexandra |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cn01xy8yv0jt#Line-ups |access-date=1 February 2025 |work=BBC Sport |date=1 February 2025}}</ref> and scoring a penalty in a 3–0 victory over [[Barrow F.C.|Barrow]] at Gresty Road on 22 February 2024.<ref>{{cite news |title=Crewe Alexandra 3-0 Barrow |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cn4m4kzwdn0t |access-date=22 February 2025 |work=BBC Sport |date=22 February 2025}}</ref>

He was released by Portsmouth upon the expiration of his contract at the end of the [[2024–25 Portsmouth F.C. season|2024–25 season]].<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.portsmouthfc.co.uk/news/2025/may/13/pompey-retained-list--summer-2025/|title=Pompey Retained List: Summer 2025|website=www.portsmouthfc.co.uk|date=13 May 2025|accessdate=13 May 2025}}</ref>

===Kilmarnock===
On 7 July 2025, Lowery joined [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].<ref name="7 July 2025">{{cite news |title=Killie add 'quality' striker Daniels and 'technical' midfielder Lowrey |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/teams/kilmarnock |access-date=7 July 2025 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club on 12 May 2026, in a 3–1 win over [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] that secured the club's Premiership survival.<ref>{{cite news |title=Hugill’s late double secures Kilmarnock's Premiership survival |url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/26101392.hugills-late-double-secures-kilmarnocks-premiership-survival/ |access-date=21 May 2026 |work=The Herald |date=12 May 2026}}</ref>

==International career==

In May 2021, Lowery was called up to train with the [[Wales national football team|Wales national squad]] ahead of the [[UEFA Euro 2020]] tournament.<ref name="YClwb">{{cite news |last1=Jones |first1=Jordan |title=Crewe Alexandra's Tom Lowery training with Wales ahead of Euros |url=https://clwbpeldroed.org/2021/05/21/crewe-alexandra-tom-lowery-wales/ |access-date=21 May 2021 |work=Y Clwb Pel-Droed |date=21 May 2021}}</ref><ref name="Baggaley-28May2021">{{cite news |last1=Baggaley |first1=Michael |title=Crewe manager's verdict on Tom Lowery's Wales call-up and training with Stoke midfielder |url=https://www.cheshire-live.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/tommy-lowery-crewe-alex-wales-20701109 |access-date=25 June 2021 |work=Cheshire Live |date=28 May 2021}}</ref>
