'''Keanu Kole Baccus''' (born 7 June 1998) is a professional footballer who plays as a [[defensive midfielder]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]]. Born in [[South Africa]], he is an international with the [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australia national team]], where he made his full international debut in September 2022.

==Early life==
Baccus was born in [[Durban]], [[South Africa]] but moved to [[Australia]] before his first birthday where his family settled in western [[Sydney]].<ref>{{Cite web|title="It's Keanu, not Keano!" — why St Mirren's new general is putting his foot down|url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/scotland/article/its-keanu-not-keano-why-st-mirrens-new-general-is-putting-his-foot-down-hvlt0597p|date=9 April 2022|website=[[The Times]]|access-date=11 November 2022|archive-date=11 November 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221111140826/https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/its-keanu-not-keano-why-st-mirrens-new-general-is-putting-his-foot-down-hvlt0597p|url-status=live}}</ref> Baccus attended Kings Langley Public School where he was inspired by Socceroo Mark Schwarzer  to participate in the sport.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Home - Crestwood High School|url=https://kingslangl-p.schools.nsw.gov.au/|access-date=27 July 2021|website=kingslangl-p.schools.nsw.gov.au|language=en-AU|archive-date=27 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210727070059/https://kingslangl-p.schools.nsw.gov.au/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Mark Schwarzer Profile, News & Stats {{!}} Premier League|url=https://www.premierleague.com/players/1218/Mark-Schwarzer/overview|access-date=27 July 2021|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en|archive-date=28 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180928203738/https://www.premierleague.com/players/1218/Mark-Schwarzer/overview|url-status=live}}</ref> He is the younger brother of [[Kearyn Baccus]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.snl24.com/kickoff/sanews/sa-players-abroad/durban-born-keanu-baccus-joins-st-mirren-20220630|title=Durban-born Keanu Baccus joins St. Mirren|author=Staff reporter|website=Kickoff|date=30 June 2022 |access-date=23 September 2022|archive-date=27 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220927213355/https://www.snl24.com/kickoff/sanews/sa-players-abroad/durban-born-keanu-baccus-joins-st-mirren-20220630|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Western Sydney Wanderers===
After rising from the Wanderers Academy to serve as co-captain of the youth team, Baccus signed a two-year senior contract in May 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wswanderersfc.com.au/article/keanu-baccus-earns-first-team-contract/kr6tv9l19mxh11adwfidoxffd|title=Keanu Baccus earns first team contract|publisher=[[Western Sydney Wanderers FC|Western Sydney Wanderers]]|date=5 May 2017|access-date=8 May 2017|archive-date=19 May 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170519171442/http://www.wswanderersfc.com.au/article/keanu-baccus-earns-first-team-contract/kr6tv9l19mxh11adwfidoxffd|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===St Mirren===
In April 2022, [[St Mirren F.C.|St. Mirren]] boss [[Stephen Robinson (footballer)|Stephen Robinson]] announced that Baccus was joining the [[Scottish Premiership]] club following the conclusion of the 2022 A League campaign.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Burns |first=Scott |date=25 April 2022 |title=Western Sydney Wanderers star Keanu Baccus agrees St Mirren pre contract |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/keanu-baccus-pens-st-mirren-26795812 |access-date=5 May 2022 |website=Daily Record |language=en |archive-date=22 November 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221122142046/https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/keanu-baccus-pens-st-mirren-26795812 |url-status=live }}</ref> A few months later, the signing was confirmed by the club as a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/4478-keanu-baccus-agrees-two-year-deal|title=Keanu Baccus agrees two-year deal|website=[[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]]|date=27 June 2022|access-date=27 June 2022|archive-date=27 June 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220627110737/https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/4478-keanu-baccus-agrees-two-year-deal|url-status=live}}</ref> At the end of his contract, after 64 games and 3 goals for [[St Mirren F.C.|St. Mirren]], Keanu decided his future lay elsewhere and decided not to sign a new contract.

===Mansfield Town===
On 22 May 2024 it was announced that he had joined [[Mansfield Town F.C.|Mansfield Town]] on a free transfer.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c28873zz1ewo|website=BBC|date=22 May 2024|title=Australia's Baccus joins Mansfield from St Mirren|access-date=22 May 2024}}</ref> The Stags had just been promoted from [[EFL League Two]] into [[EFL League One]] by finishing in an automatic promotion position in the [[2023–24 EFL League Two|2023–24 season]].

===Return to St Mirren===
On 7 August 2025, Baccus returned to St Mirren on a two-year deal with the option for a further year.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/5965-keanu-baccus-returns-to-saints-on-permanent-deal|title=Keanu Baccus returns to Saints on permanent deal|website=www.stmirren.com|date=7 August 2025|accessdate=8 August 2025}}</ref>

==International career==
Baccus qualified for the [[2020 Summer Olympics|Tokyo 2020 Olympics]] as part of the [[Australia men's national under-23 soccer team|Australia under-23]] team. The team beat Argentina in their first group match but were unable to win another match. They were therefore not in medal contention.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Australian Olympic Team for Tokyo 2021|url=https://www.theroar.com.au/olympics/australian-olympic-team/|access-date=25 February 2022|website=The Roar|language=en-US|archive-date=15 March 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220315191131/https://www.theroar.com.au/olympics/australian-olympic-team/|url-status=live}}</ref>

In September 2022, Baccus debuted for the [[Australia men's national soccer team|senior national team]] as a second-half substitute in a friendly against [[New Zealand men's national football team|New Zealand]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=22 June 2022 |title=New Zealand vs Australia, International Friendlies, Round 1, 25th Sep 2022 |url=https://www.socceroos.com.au/match/new-zealand-v-australia-friendlies-25-09-2022/2289966 |access-date=25 September 2022 |website=Socceroos |language=en |archive-date=25 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220925065521/https://www.socceroos.com.au/match/new-zealand-v-australia-friendlies-25-09-2022/2289966 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 8 November 2022, he was named in Australia's [[FIFA World Cup|World Cup]] squad for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]] in Qatar.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Socceroos Squad Announced for FIFA 2022 World Cup|url=https://www.socceroos.com.au/news/socceroos-squad-announced-fifa-world-cup-qatar-2022tm|accessdate=8 November 2022|date=8 November 2022|archive-date=8 November 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221108050206/https://www.socceroos.com.au/news/socceroos-squad-announced-fifa-world-cup-qatar-2022tm|url-status=live}}</ref> Baccus was used as a substitute in Australia's first three games in the tournament, before making his first senior international start in Australia's loss in the round of sixteen to [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.socceroos.com.au/news/dream-come-true-baccus-over-moon-after-socceroos-starting-debut|website=[[Socceroos]]|first=Euan|last=James|date=7 December 2022|access-date=7 December 2022|title='Dream come true': Baccus over the moon after Socceroos starting debut|archive-date=7 December 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221207103257/https://www.socceroos.com.au/news/dream-come-true-baccus-over-moon-after-socceroos-starting-debut|url-status=live}}</ref>

'''Alexandros Gogić''' ({{langx|el|Αλέξανδρος Γκόγκιτς}}; {{lang-sr-Cyrl|Александрос Гогић}}; born 13 April 1994) is a Cypriot professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] and [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|StMirren}} club [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] and the [[Cyprus national football team|Cyprus national team]]. He has also previously played for Scottish clubs [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]], and [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]].

==Early and personal life==
Gogić is the son of Serbian-born Cypriot international footballer [[Siniša Gogić]].<ref name = "Accies"/>

==Club career==
Gogić played youth football for Greek club [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]] and Welsh club [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.swanseacity.com/news/article/promising-youngsters-sign-890838.aspx|title=Swans sign Zabret and Gogic|date=2 July 2013|access-date=11 March 2017|publisher=Swansea City A.F.C.}}{{Dead link|date=June 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> He signed for Scottish club [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] in February 2017.<ref name = "Accies">{{cite web|url=http://www.hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/gogic-signs/|title=Gogic Signs|date=25 February 2017|access-date=11 March 2017|publisher=Hamilton Academical F.C.|archive-date=30 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170330012242/http://www.hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/gogic-signs/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In March 2017, Gogić signed a contract extension with Hamilton until May 2018,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39428853|title=Hamilton Accies: Alex Gogic and Jordan McGregor sign contract extensions|date=29 March 2017|access-date=29 March 2017|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> before signing a further extension, until 2020, in December 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42409133|title=Hamilton Accies' Dougie Imrie and Alex Gogic sign contract extensions|date=19 December 2017|access-date=19 January 2018|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 3 June 2020 he announced that he had left the club.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/52889605|title=Hamilton: George Oakley & Alex Gogic follow Aaron McGowan in announcing exit|work=BBC Sport|date=3 June 2020}}</ref>

On 10 July 2020, Gogić signed a two-year contract with [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53352032 |title=Hibernian sign Kevin Nisbet, Drey Wright & Alex Gogic |website=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=10 July 2020 |access-date=10 July 2020}}</ref>

On 31 January 2022, Gogić joined [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]], on loan for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/article/alex-gogic-joins-st-mirren-on-loan |title=Alex Gogic joins St Mirren on loan |website=hibernianfc.co.uk |date=31 January 2022|access-date=31 January 2022}}</ref> He scored on his debut for St Mirren, a 1–1 draw with [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] on 1 February.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/60121363 |title=St Mirren 1–1 Motherwell |first=Andrew |last=Southwick |website=BBC Sport |date=1 February 2022 |accessdate=5 February 2022}}</ref> He was released by Hibs in June 2022, at the end of his contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61675106 |title=Hibernian: Scott Allan, Alex Gogic, Drey Wright and Jamie Murphy among six exits |website=BBC Sport |date=2 June 2022 |accessdate=2 June 2022}}</ref> In August 2022 he signed a two-year contract with St Mirren.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/62609954 |title=Alex Gogic: Cyprus midfielder returns to St Mirren on two-year deal |website=BBC Sport |date=19 August 2022 |accessdate=19 August 2022}}</ref> In May 2024 Gogić  signed a three–year extension to his contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/ckv7pp78n2do |title=Defender Gogic signs new deal with St Mirren |website=BBC Sport |date=7 May 2024 |accessdate=8 May 2024}}</ref>

==International career==
He has represented Cyprus at [[Cyprus national under-19 football team|under-19]] and [[Cyprus national under-21 football team|under-21]] youth levels.<ref name = "Accies"/> He was first selected for the senior [[Cyprus national football team|Cyprus national team]] in September 2020,<ref>{{cite tweet |number=1299297164829614080 |user=HibernianFC |date=28 August 2020 |accessdate=28 August 2020 |title=Congratulations to @Gogic13 on a first call-up to the senior @CyprusFA squad! The powerhouse midfielder has hit the ground running since moving to Hibernian in the summer.}}</ref> but had to withdraw when he tested positive for [[COVID-19]].<ref name = covid/> Further tests were negative, but he still had to enter a 10-day period of self-isolation that prevented him from playing.<ref name = covid>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53965079 |title=Alex Gogic: Hibs midfielder confirms false positive Covid test |website=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=30 August 2020 |access-date=30 August 2020}}</ref> He made his senior debut with Cyprus a month later, in a 2–1 friendly loss to the [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech Republic]] on 7 October.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://uk.soccerway.com/matches/2020/10/07/world/friendlies/cyprus/czech-republic/3297854/|title = Cyprus vs. Czech Republic – 7 October 2020 – Soccerway}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |first=Craig |last=Fowler |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-star-alex-gogic-makes-international-debut-cyprus-2996846 |title=Hibs star Alex Gogic makes international debut for Cyprus |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |date=8 October 2020 |access-date=9 October 2020}}</ref>

'''Luke Gerald Michael Thomas''' (born 19 February 1999) is an English professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as winger for {{Scottish football updater|StMirren}} club [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].

Thomas began his career with [[Cheltenham Town F.C.|Cheltenham Town]], before later playing for [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]] and [[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]]. He has also featured on loan for [[Gloucester City A.F.C.|Gloucester City]], [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]] and [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]].

==Club career==
Thomas began his career with [[National League (division)|National League]] club [[Cheltenham Town F.C.|Cheltenham Town]], making his only first team appearance against [[Chelmsford City F.C.|Chelmsford City]] in the [[FA Trophy]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Palmer|first1=Jon|title=Cheltenham Town to net five figure sum as Luke Thomas makes debut|url=http://www.gloucestershirelive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/cheltenham-town-net-five-figure-812972|accessdate=26 January 2018|work=Gloucestershire Live|date=21 November 2017}}</ref> He had a trial with Portuguese club [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] in 2015. He joined [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]] in January 2016 for an undisclosed transfer fee, signing a two-and-a-half-year professional contract.<ref>{{cite news|title=Derby County: Rams sign Cheltenham teenager Thomas|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35365905|accessdate=26 January 2018|work=BBC Sport|date=20 January 2016}}</ref> He had a loan spell with [[National League North]] club [[Gloucester City F.C.|Gloucester City]] during the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Who is Derby County forward Luke Thomas?|url=http://www.derbytelegraph.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/who-derby-county-forward-luke-709632|publisher=Derby Telegraph|accessdate=17 December 2017}}</ref>

Thomas was nominated for the [[Premier League 2]] Player of the Month award in September 2017 as a result of his performances for [[Derby County F.C. Reserves and Academy|Derby County's under-23 team]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Watson|first1=Chris|title=Derby County youngster nominated for Premier League Two award|url=http://www.derbytelegraph.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/derby-county-youngster-nominated-premier-587011|accessdate=26 January 2018|work=Derby Telegraph|date=6 October 2017}}</ref> He signed a new three-year contract with Derby in October 2017.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Wakefield|first1=Mark|title=Derby County forward signs new three-year contract|url=http://www.derbytelegraph.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/derby-county-forward-luke-thomas-624593|accessdate=26 January 2018|work=Derby Telegraph|date=13 October 2017}}</ref> He was first named in a first team matchday squad on 31 October 2017 against [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]],<ref name="Leeds United 1-2 Derby County">{{cite web|title=Leeds United 1–2 Derby County|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41730395|publisher=BBC Sport|accessdate=17 December 2017}}</ref> and made his league debut on 21 November 2017, coming on as an 89th-minute substitute for [[Tom Lawrence]] in a 2–0 win over [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]].<ref name="Derby County 2-0 Queens Park Rangers">{{cite web|title=Derby County 2–0 Queens Park Rangers|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41978137|publisher=BBC Sport|accessdate=17 December 2017}}</ref>

Thomas signed a new four-year contract with Derby in August 2018.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Watson |first1=Chris |title=Derby County starlet signs new contract with Rams |url=https://www.derbytelegraph.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/luke-thomas-derby-county-contract-1867413 |accessdate=17 February 2019 |work=Derbyshire Live |date=6 August 2018}}</ref> Later that month, he joined [[EFL League One|League One]] [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]] on a half-season loan until the start of 2019.<ref name="Coventry Loan">{{cite news|title=Derby County: Coventry City sign winger Luke Thomas on half-season loan|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45213054|publisher=BBC Sport|accessdate=16 August 2017}}</ref> In January 2019, the loan was extended for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Luke Thomas: Derby County winger to stay at Coventry City for rest of season |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46749197 |accessdate=17 February 2019 |work=BBC Sport |date=3 January 2019}}</ref>

===Barnsley===
In June 2019, he joined [[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]] for an undisclosed fee.<ref name="Barnsley Move">{{cite web |title=Thomas Makes Barnsley Switch|url=https://www.dcfc.co.uk/news/2019/06/thomas-makes-barnsley-switch |publisher=[[Derby County F.C.]] |accessdate=13 June 2019}}</ref> On his debut he scored the winning goal for Barnsley in a 1–0 win against [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49135734 |title=Barnsley 1–0 Fulham |date=3 August 2019 |publisher=BBC|accessdate=15 August 2019}}</ref>

In January 2021, Thomas joined [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]] on loan for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{Cite web | url = https://www.yorkshirepost.co.uk/sport/football/barnsley-fc-winger-luke-thomas-seals-loan-move-ipswich-town-3105649 | work = [[Yorkshire Post]] | title = Barnsley FC winger Luke Thomas seals loan move to Ipswich Town| first= Leon | last= Wobschall| accessdate = 19 January 2021 | date = 19 January 2021}}</ref> On 8 April 2021, Thomas announced on social media that he had cut his loan move with Ipswich short for personal reasons and he returned to Barnsley.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.itfc.co.uk/news/2021/april/luke-thomas-returns-to-barnsley/|title = Luke Absent for Personal Reasons}}</ref>

====Bristol Rovers (loan)====
On 10 July 2021, Thomas joined [[EFL League Two|League Two]] side [[Bristol Rovers F.C.|Bristol Rovers]] on a season-long loan deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bristolrovers.co.uk/news/2021/july/Luke-thomas-loan-deal-bristol-rovers/|title=Luke Thomas joins the Gas on Loan!|website=www.bristolrovers.co.uk|date=10 July 2021}}</ref> On 13 October, he scored his first goal for the club when he opened the scoring in a 2–1 [[EFL Trophy]] defeat to [[Chelsea F.C. Under-23s and Academy|Chelsea U21s]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bristolrovers.co.uk/news/2021/october/match-report-rovers-chelsea-u21s/|title=Match Report - Rovers 1–2 Chelsea U21s|website=www.bristolrovers.co.uk|date=13 October 2021}}</ref> On 23 November 2021, Thomas came off the bench in a 1–1 draw against nine-men [[Salford City F.C.|Salford City]], missing a great chance to put Rovers two ahead before the home side eventually equalised.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/59300902|title=Salford City 1–1 Bristol Rovers|publisher=BBC Sport|date=23 November 2021|accessdate=24 November 2021}}</ref> After the match, Thomas' manager [[Joey Barton]] criticised Thomas claiming that he "thinks the world owes him a favour" and that "if he doesn't get his finger out, this opportunity at Rovers is going to pass him by".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bristolpost.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/bristol-rovers-boss-joey-barton-6251316|title=Bristol Rovers boss Joey Barton launches scathing criticism of ex-Derby County man Luke Thomas|publisher=Bristol Post|last1=Frost|first1=Sam|date=24 November 2021}}</ref> Barton continued with his criticism of Thomas the following day, claiming that the club had tried to terminate his loan in the summer, the same window in which Thomas had been signed after the player had stormed out of training a number of times in frustration.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bristolpost.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/bristol-rovers-boss-joey-barton-6261467|title=Bristol Rovers boss Joey Barton doubles down on Luke Thomas criticism in astonishing detail|publisher=Bristol Post|last1=Frost|first1=Sam|date=25 November 2021}}</ref> In January 2022, Thomas admitted that he deserved the criticism and had let people down.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bristolpost.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/luke-thomas-i-people-down-6464238|title=Luke Thomas: 'I let people down at Bristol Rovers and deserved rocket from Joey Barton'|publisher=Bristol Post|last1=Frost|first1=Sam|date=9 January 2022|accessdate=13 January 2022}}</ref> The season ended with Rovers getting promoted on the final day of the season, moving into the automatic promotion spots on goals scored.<ref name="21/22 promotion"/>

===Return to Barnsley===
After speculation surrounding Thomas and a permanent return to Bristol Rovers,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bristolpost.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/bristol-rovers-pushing-permanent-deal-7332392|title=Bristol Rovers pushing for permanent deal for Barnsley winger Luke Thomas|publisher=Bristol Post|last1=Palmer|first1=Jon|last2=Frost|first2=Sam|date=14 July 2022|accessdate=9 October 2022}}</ref> he found himself in the first team picture under new manager [[Michael Duff (footballer)|Michael Duff]] and scored the only goal in the second match of the season as Duff was given his first win in charge over Thomas' former club Cheltenham Town.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/62357572|title=Barnsley 1–0 Cheltenham Town|publisher=BBC Sport|date=6 August 2022|accessdate=9 October 2022}}</ref> On 8 October 2022, it was confirmed that Thomas had suffered a broken leg in training that would see the winger out of action for at least four months.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.yorkshirepost.co.uk/sport/football/key-barnsley-midfielder-suffers-broken-leg-and-will-be-out-for-at-least-four-months-3872666|title=Key Barnsley midfielder suffers broken leg and will be out for at least four months|publisher=Yorkshire Post|last1=McKenna|first1=Ben|date=8 October 2022|accessdate=9 October 2022}}</ref> Following defeat in the play-off final, he was offered a new contract at the end of the [[2022–23 Barnsley F.C. season|2022–23 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.barnsleyfc.co.uk/news/20232/june/retained/|title=REDS SUBMIT RETAINED LIST|website=www.barnsleyfc.co.uk|date=24 June 2023|accessdate=25 June 2023}}</ref>

===Bristol Rovers===
On 24 June 2023, Thomas' return to Bristol Rovers was confirmed, signing a three-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bristolrovers.co.uk/news/2023/june/luke-thomas-returns/|title=Thomas Returns to Rovers|website=www.bristolrovers.co.uk|date=24 June 2023|accessdate=25 June 2023}}</ref> He scored his first league goal for the club on his second debut, an opening day draw with [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66345552|title=Portsmouth 1–1 Bristol Rovers|publisher=BBC Sport|date=5 August 2023|accessdate=6 August 2023}}</ref> On 30 September 2023, Thomas suffered a tight hamstring during half-time of a 2–0 defeat to [[Peterborough United F.C.|Peterborough United]], failing to tell the club's medical staff until the end of the half-time break, with the opposition going on to score early in to the second period. Following the match, manager Joey Barton launched an angry tirade toward the player, blaming him for the second goal and criticising his character, demanding that the player should be fined by the club and threatening his future at the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.peterboroughtoday.co.uk/sport/football/peterborough-united/bristol-rovers-boss-joey-barton-launches-an-astonishing-outburst-at-his-own-player-after-inferior-peterborough-united-beat-his-team-4355019|title=Bristol Rovers boss Joey Barton launches an astonishing outburst at his own player after 'inferior' Peterborough United beat his team|publisher=Peterborough Telegraph|last1=Swann|first1=Alan|date=30 September 2023|accessdate=2 October 2023}}</ref> It was later revealed that he would miss a number of weeks with a hamstring injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bristolpost.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/luke-thomas-injury-acts-double-8798764|title=Luke Thomas' injury acts as double-whammy for Bristol Rovers after Joey Barton's criticism|publisher=Bristol Post|last1=Hargraves|first1=Daniel|date=2 October 2023|accessdate=2 October 2023}}</ref> Following the appointment of new manager [[Matt Taylor (footballer, born 1982)|Matt Taylor]] in December 2023, Thomas saw himself switched to a more unfamiliar [[Defender (association football)#Wing-back|right wing-back]] position. He impressed from this new role, considered as one of his side's best players over the busy Christmas period, notably scoring a last-minute winner against leaders [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]] on Boxing Day.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bristolpost.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/bristol-rovers-player-who-represents-9010433|title=The Bristol Rovers player who represents Matt Taylor's biggest success story at the Gas so far|publisher=Bristol Post|last1=Hargraves|first1=Daniel|date=3 January 2024|accessdate=11 January 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/67756989|title=Bristol Rovers 2–1 Portsmouth|publisher=BBC Sport|date=26 December 2023|accessdate=11 January 2024}}</ref>

During his second season back at the club permanently, Thomas once again found himself out of favour with manager Matt Taylor, struggling for minutes ahead of summer signing [[Shaq Forde]].<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.bristolpost.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/matt-taylor-addresses-reasons-luke-9734125|title=Matt Taylor addresses reasons for Luke Thomas' recent exclusions from Bristol Rovers line ups|publisher=Bristol Post|last=Hargraves|first=Daniel|date=21 November 2024|accessdate=19 December 2024}}</ref>

He departed the club upon the expiry of his contract at the end of the [[2025–26 Bristol Rovers F.C. season|2025–26 season]].<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.bristolrovers.co.uk/news/bristol-rovers-issue-202526-retained-list|title=Bristol Rovers issue 2025/26 retained list|website=www.bristolrovers.co.uk|date=5 May 2026|accessdate=5 May 2026}}</ref>

===St Mirren===
On 1 August 2026, Thomas joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] on an initial two-year deal, with the club holding the option for a further year.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.stmirren.com/news/luke-thomas-signs-for-saints|title=Luke Thomas becomes eighth summer signing|website=www.stmirren.com|date=1 August 2026|accessdate=1 August 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
Thomas made his youth international debut on 6 September 2019 with [[England national under-20 football team|England U20]], coming on as an 80th minute substitute for [[Luke Bolton]] in a 0–0 draw against [[Netherlands national under-20 football team|Netherlands U20]] at [[New Meadow]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.barnsleyfc.co.uk/news/2019/september/luke-england-interview/|title=Thomas: "It's a very proud moment for me."|work=Barnsley Football Club|date=6 September 2019|accessdate=8 September 2019}}</ref>

'''Nico Mantl''' (born 6 February 2000) is a German professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for {{Scottish football updater|Kilmarno}} club [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].

==Club career==
After nearly two seasons as [[SpVgg Unterhaching]]'s first choice goalkeeper, Mantl completed a move to [[Austrian Bundesliga]] side [[FC Red Bull Salzburg|Red Bull Salzburg]] in January 2021, signing a four-and-a-half-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.redbullsalzburg.at/en/fc-red-bull-salzburg/news/saison_2020_21/new-keeper-signs.html|title=NEW KEEPER SIGNS|publisher=[[FC Red Bull Salzburg]]|date=28 January 2021|accessdate=28 January 2021}}</ref> At the end of December 2022, Mantl signed loan deal for the rest of the season with [[Danish Superliga]] club [[AaB Fodbold|AaB]].<ref>[https://aabsport.dk/nyheder/2022/december/aab-henter-tysk-u21-landsholdsmaalmand-paa-leje/ AaB henter tysk U/21-landsholdsmålmand på leje], aabsport.dk, 30 December 2022</ref>

Mantl returned to Salzburg ahead of the 2023–24 season, sitting on the bench for a number of games in his first six months back at the club, while also getting a full game in the league against [[FC Blau-Weiß Linz|Blau-Weiß Linz]] in September 2023. In search of more playing time, Mantl returned to Denmark in January 2024; this time to [[Viborg FF]], where Mantl signed a loan deal until the end of the season.<ref>[https://vff.dk/nyhed/sport/14135-vff-lejer-nico-mantl-resten-af-saesonen VFF lejer Nico Mantl resten af sæsonen], vff.dk, 7 January 2024</ref>

On 19 June 2024, it was announced that Mantl would join Portuguese side [[F.C. Arouca|Arouca]] on a permanent deal on 1 July.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Trindade |first=Tiago |date=19 June 2024 |title=Oficial: Nico Mantl reforça a baliza do Arouca |url=https://www.abola.pt/futebol/noticias/oficial-nico-mantl-reforca-a-baliza-do-arouca-2024061917125965813 |access-date=23 June 2024 |website=A Bola |language=pt}}</ref> On 27 January 2026, Arouca sent Mantl on loan to Austrian Bundesliga club Blau-Weiß Linz until the end of the [[2025–26 Austrian Football Bundesliga|2025–26 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=27 January 2026 |title=Nico Mantl regressa à Áustria por empréstimo do Arouca |trans-title=Nico Mantl returns to Austria on loan from Arouca |url=https://sapo.pt/artigo/nico-mantl-regressa-a-austria-por-emprestimo-do-arouca-69790d1b05baa009b0eceb61 |access-date=28 January 2026 |website=SAPO |language=pt}}</ref>

On 16 October 2026, Mantl joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] on a short-term deal until the end of the [[2026–27 Kilmarnock F.C. season|2026–27 season]].<ref> {{cite web|url=https://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/news/nico-mantl-joins-killie/|title=Nico Mantl joins Killie|website=kilmarnockfc.co.uk|date=16 October 2026|accessdate=16 October 2026}}</ref>

'''Calum Ferrie''' (born 19 June 1998) is an English professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for {{Scottish football updater|Kilmarno}} club [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].

A former [[Youth system|youth team]] player at [[Port Vale F.C.|Port Vale]], he played on [[Loan (sports)|loan]] at [[Gresley F.C.|Gresley]] in 2015 before he turned professional at [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] the following year. He made his first-team debut for Dundee in April 2018. He joined [[Stirling Albion F.C.|Stirling Albion]] on loan in June 2018 and became named the club's Player of the Year for the 2018–19 season. He joined [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] on loan in January 2020. Ferrie returned to Dundee the following season before leaving the club in 2021. He subsequently signed with Queen's Park and helped the club to win [[Promotion and relegation|promotion]] out of [[Scottish League One]] via the play-offs in 2022, before being named on the [[PFA Scotland Team of the Year|PFA Scotland Scottish Championship Team of the Year]] for both 2022–23 and 2023–24. He played in the 2025 [[Scottish Challenge Cup]] final. In 2026, Ferrie moved to [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].

==Career==
===Port Vale===
Ferrie was a [[Youth system|youth team]] player at [[Port Vale F.C.|Port Vale]] when he moved on [[Loan (sports)|loan]] to [[Northern Premier League]] Division One South side [[Gresley F.C.|Gresley]] in October 2015.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vale 'keeper goes out on loan|url=https://www.port-vale.co.uk/news/2015/october/vale-keeper-goes-out-on-loan/|date=28 October 2015|accessdate=9 May 2018|publisher=Port Vale F.C.}}</ref> He made his debut for Gresley in an [[FA Trophy]] qualification match at [[Matlock Town F.C.|Matlock Town]] on 31 October. He featured in three further games for the club, his final appearance coming against [[Market Drayton Town F.C.|Market Drayton Town]] on 28 November.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gresleyfc.com/players/?id=2070|title=Profile|accessdate=9 May 2018|publisher=Gresley F.C.}}</ref>

===Dundee===
After leaving Port Vale, Ferrie signed for [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] in 2016.<ref name = "ET"/> He made his senior debut in the [[Scottish Premiership]] in a 4–0 defeat away to [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] on 7 April 2018.<ref name = "2017-18"/> He appeared as a [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] for the injured [[Elliot Parish]], and was praised by [[Manager (association football)|manager]] [[Neil McCann]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/633070/dundee-boss-praises-young-keeper-calum-ferrie/|title=Dundee boss praises young keeper Calum Ferrie|date=10 April 2018|accessdate=9 May 2018|publisher=The Courier}}</ref> After the match, Ferrie described himself as being "numb", and said that he wished to play more first-team games.<ref name = "ET">{{cite web|url=https://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/fp/calum-ferrie-numb-as-he-achieves-childhood-dream-and-makes-dundee-debut/|title=Calum Ferrie 'numb' as he achieves childhood dream and makes Dundee debut|date=18 April 2018|accessdate=9 May 2018|author=George Cran|newspaper=The Evening Telegraph}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/637636/dundee-first-team-is-the-priority-for-young-keeper-calum-ferrie/|title=Dundee first team is the priority for young keeper Calum Ferrie|date=18 April 2018|accessdate=9 May 2018|publisher=The Courier}}</ref>

Ferrie was loaned to [[Scottish League Two]] club [[Stirling Albion F.C.|Stirling Albion]] in June 2018.<ref>{{cite news |title=Dundee keeper Calum Ferrie heading to Stirling Albion - The Courier |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/679686/dundee-keeper-calum-ferrie-heading-to-stirling-albion/ |accessdate=30 June 2018 |work=The Courier |date=30 June 2018}}</ref> He made 28 appearances for the Binos during the [[2018–19 Scottish League Two|2018–19]] season. His efforts for the club were rewarded by being named Stirling's Young Player of the Year and Player of the Year.<ref name="poty">{{Cite web|url=https://twitter.com/Stirling_Albion/status/1124775394308239366|title=Stirling Albion FC Official Twitter|date=4 May 2019|website=Twitter}}</ref>

Ferrie signed a one-year extension with Dundee on 15 May 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/893042/dundee-hand-new-one-year-contract-to-goalkeeper-calum-ferrie/|title=Dundee hand new one-year contract to goalkeeper Calum Ferrie|last=Roache|first=Ian|date=15 May 2019|website=The Courier|access-date=19 May 2019}}</ref> He was sent out on loan to [[Scottish League One]] side [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] on 31 January 2020, after signing another one-year extension with the "Dark Blues".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/calum-signs-new-deal-and-joins-falkirk-on-loan/|title=Calum signs new deal and joins Falkirk on loan|last=|first=|date=31 January 2020|website=Dundee FC|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200131160102/https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/calum-signs-new-deal-and-joins-falkirk-on-loan/ |archive-date=31 January 2020 |access-date=31 January 2020}}</ref>

Ferrie earned his first league start for Dundee in three seasons on 24 October 2020, earning his first win and [[Shutout|clean sheet]] for the club in a 1–0 win over [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] at [[Dens Park]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=24 October 2020|title=Dundee v Greenock Morton|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54580541|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201030194414/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54580541 |archive-date=30 October 2020 |access-date=25 October 2020|website=BBC}}</ref> However, [[Adam Legzdins]] was signed the following month, whilst number one [[Jack Hamilton (footballer, born 1994)|Jack Hamilton]] returned to fitness, and Ferrie made just two further appearances in the [[2020–21 Dundee F.C. season|2020–21]] campaign.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=13 November 2020|title=Adam signs|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/adam-signs/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201113113159/https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/adam-signs/ |archive-date=13 November 2020 |access-date=13 November 2020|website=dundeefc.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Cran |first1=George |title=Dundee goalkeeper Jack Hamilton has to prove he can hold on to No 1 jersey says boss James McPake |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/1800157/dundee-goalkeeper-jack-hamilton-has-to-prove-he-can-hold-on-to-no-1-jersey-says-boss-james-mcpake/ |access-date=25 May 2021 |work=The Courier |date=10 December 2020}}</ref><ref name="2020 - 21"/> He was on the bench for the [[2020–21 Scottish Premiership#Premiership play-offs|play-off final]] win over [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] as Dundee secured [[Promotion and relegation|promotion]] back into the Premiership,<ref name="pof1">{{cite news |last1=Campbell |first1=Andy |title=Dundee see off Kilmarnock in play-off |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57139366 |access-date=25 May 2021 |work=BBC Sport |date=24 May 2021}}</ref> and was released upon the expiry of his [[Association football contracts|contract]] in June.<ref>{{Cite web|date=3 June 2021|title=Player departures|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/player-departures-8/|url-status=live|access-date=3 June 2021|website=dundeefc.co.uk|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210603125402/https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/player-departures-8/ |archive-date=3 June 2021 }}</ref>

=== Queen's Park ===
In July 2021, Ferrie signed for Scottish League One side [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] as [[head coach]] [[Laurie Ellis]] looked to provide competition to established number one Willie Muir.<ref>{{Cite web|date=3 July 2021|title=Calum Ferrie joins the Spiders|url=https://queensparkfc.co.uk/calum-ferrie-joins-the-spiders/|url-status=live|access-date=3 July 2021|website=queenspark.co.uk|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210703090628/https://queensparkfc.co.uk/calum-ferrie-joins-the-spiders/ |archive-date=3 July 2021 }}</ref> Ferrie would become the club's starting goalkeeper midway through the [[2021–22 Queen's Park F.C. season|2021–22]] season under new manager [[Owen Coyle]], and would enjoy his second-successive promotion as Queen's Park won the [[2021–22 Scottish Championship#Championship play-offs|Championship play-offs]] in May 2022 by beating [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] 3–2 on [[aggregate score|aggregate]] after [[Overtime (sports)|extra time]].<ref name="pof2">{{cite news |last1=Lindsay |first1=Clive |title=Queen's Park beat Airdrie to reach Championship |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61368166 |access-date=22 May 2022 |work=BBC Sport |date=15 May 2022}}</ref> At the end of a successful debut season, Ferrie would agree to extend his contract with the club until 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 June 2022 |title=Calum Ferrie Extends Contract |url=https://queensparkfc.co.uk/calum-ferrie-extends-contract/ |access-date=8 June 2022 |website=Queen's Park Football Club |language=en-US}}</ref>

Ferrie would have a stand out [[2022–23 Queen's Park F.C. season|2022–23 season]] with Queen's Park, starting every game for the side and being a key factor in the club's unexpected title challenge, and was named to [[PFA Scotland]]'s [[PFA Scotland Team of the Year#Championship 9|Scottish Championship Team of the Year]] at the end of the league season.<ref name=":0">{{cite tweet|number=1655898923506999298|user=PFAScotland|title=Your PFA Scotland Championship Team of the Year - as voted for by the players|date=9 May 2023|access-date=9 May 2023}}</ref> Ferrie marked his 100th appearance for the club with a clean sheet against [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] on 17 February 2024.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Resolute Queen's Park hold in-form Morton |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68144697 |access-date=17 February 2024 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> A couple days later, Ferrie signed a new three-year contract with Queen's Park, keeping him at the club until June 2027.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cairns |first=Ian |date=19 February 2024 |title=Calum Ferrie signs on until June 2027 |url=https://queensparkfc.co.uk/calum-ferrie-signs-on-until-june-2027/ |access-date=19 February 2024 |website=Queen's Park Football Club |language=en-US}}</ref> At the end of the [[2023–24 Queen's Park F.C. season|2023–24]] campaign, he was named on the Scottish Championship Team of the Year for the second successive season.<ref name=yee>{{cite tweet |number=1781374755003645954 |title=PFA Scotland on X: "🏆 PFA Scotland Championship Team of the Year. As voted by the players, the nominated team is… Callum Ferrie Jack McMillan Kevin Holt Scott McMann Josh Edwards Adam Frizzell Craig Sibbald Sam Stanton Louis Moult Brian Graham Ruari Paton #PFASAwards |user=PFAScotland |date=19 April 2024 |access-date=19 April 2024}}</ref>

On 9 February 2025, Ferrie earned plaudits in an upset [[Scottish Cup]] victory over [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]], including a late [[Penalty kick|penalty]] save to clinch a quarter-final berth.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rangers vs Queen's Park: Scottish Cup stats & head-to-head |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/crm71jddmp7t |access-date=9 February 2025 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Murray |first=Ewan |date=9 February 2025 |title=Calum Ferrie the hero as Queen's Park shock Rangers with win at Ibrox |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/feb/09/rangers-queens-park-scottish-cup-fifth-round-match-report |access-date=9 February 2025 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> He played in the 2025 final of the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]] at [[Falkirk Stadium]], which ended in a 5–0 defeat to [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].<ref name=scc25>{{cite news |title=Queen's Park vs Livingston: SPFL Trust Trophy final stats & head-to-head |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cz03vzdrgmpt |access-date=14 April 2025 |work=BBC Sport |date=30 March 2025}}</ref> He played a total of 44 games in the [[2024–25 Queen's Park F.C. season|2024–25]] campaign.<ref name=":04"/> He was linked with a move to Northern Irish club [[Coleraine F.C.|Coleraine]] in May 2025, where manager [[Ruaidhrí Higgins]] was reportedly tabling a bid and Queen's Park were said to be open to offers.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hutchinson |first1=Luke |title=Coleraine show interest in Queens Park 'keeper |url=https://www.colerainechronicle.co.uk/football/2025/05/14/news/coleraine-show-interest-in-queens-park-keeper-57451/ |access-date=30 December 2025 |work=Coleraine Chronicle |date=14 May 2025 |language=en}}</ref> He was named on the SPFL Team of the Week on 21 April 2026 after saving 11 shots to keep a clean sheet against [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Team of the Week |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/team-of-the-week-51180 |access-date=4 May 2026 |work=spfl.co.uk |date=21 April 2026}}</ref> He made 43 appearances across the [[2025–26 Queen's Park F.C. season|2025–26]] campaign.<ref name="25/26"/>

=== Kilmarnock ===
On 19 June 2026, Ferrie left Queen's Park to join [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] on a two-year deal for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Paton |first=Ewan |date=19 June 2026 |title=Calum Ferrie arrives at Killie |url=https://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/news/calum-ferrie-arrives-at-killie/ |access-date=12 July 2026 |website=Kilmarnock FC |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Oliver |first=David |date=19 June 2026 |title=Calum Ferrie Joins Kilmarnock |url=https://queensparkfc.co.uk/calum-ferrie-joins-kilmarnock/ |access-date=12 July 2026 |website=Queen's Park Football Club |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Christopher Robert Mochrie''' (born 7 April 2003)<ref>{{cite news |title=Chris Mochrie |url=https://www.arabarchive.co.uk/player.php?id=1953 |accessdate=29 May 2019 |work=Arab Archive}}</ref> is a Scottish footballer who plays as an [[Midfielder#Attacking midfielder|attacking midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|StMirren}} club [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]]. He holds the record as the youngest player to appear for the [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] first team after making his debut in 2019.

==Playing career==
===Club===
Born in [[Dundee]], Mochrie played for Logie Harp Boys Club before joining the Dundee United Academy.<ref>{{cite news |title=Thirteen Academy graduates sign professional contracts |url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/6065/THIRTEEN-ACADEMY-GRADUATES-SIGN-PROFESSIONAL-CONTRACTS.html |accessdate=8 April 2020 |publisher=Dundee United F.C. |date=10 May 2019}}</ref> He also attended the [[Scottish Football Association]] Performance School programme based at [[St John's Roman Catholic High School]].<ref>{{cite news |title=SFA Performance Football: S4 Profiles |url=http://stjohnshigh.ea.dundeecity.sch.uk/dept-template/profiles/s1-profiles-2 |accessdate=29 May 2019 |publisher=St John's RC High School}}</ref> He became Dundee United's youngest ever first team player when making his debut as a substitute against [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] in May 2019, aged 16 years and 27 days.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Cran |first1=George |title=Boss Robbie says defeat can be jolt Dundee United need |url=https://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/fp/boss-robbie-says-defeat-can-be-jolt-dundee-united-need/ |accessdate=29 May 2019 |work=Evening Telegraph |date=7 May 2019 |location=Dundee}}</ref><ref name="DUFC">{{cite news |title=Mochrie becomes youngest ever first team player |url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/6057/MOCHRIE-BECOMES-YOUNGEST-EVER-FIRST-TEAM-PLAYER.html |accessdate=29 May 2019 |publisher=Dundee United F.C. |date=4 May 2019}}</ref>{{refn|group=nb|The previous record of 16 years and 99 days had been set by [[John Souttar]] in 2013.<ref name="DUFC" />}}

In October 2020, Mochrie joined [[Scottish League One]] side [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]] on loan.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=16 October 2020|title=Chris Mochrie joins Montrose on loan|url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/6627/CHRIS-MOCHRIE-JOINS-MONTROSE-ON-LOAN.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201019033816/https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/6627/CHRIS-MOCHRIE-JOINS-MONTROSE-ON-LOAN.html |archive-date=19 October 2020 |access-date=18 October 2020|website=dundeeunitedfc.co.uk}}</ref> He was recalled by United when lower league football was suspended in January 2021, but returned to Montrose when the suspension was lifted in March.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://montrosefc.co.uk/33-featured/2419-mochrie-returns-on-new-loan-deal|title = Montrose FC Online - MOCHRIE RETURNS ON NEW LOAN DEAL}}</ref>

Mochrie scored his first goal for Dundee United on 14 July 2021, in a 6–1 win over [[Elgin City F.C.|Elgin City]] in the [[Scottish League Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Kieran Freeman and Chris Mochrie score their first goals for Dundee United |url=https://www.bt.com/sport/news/2021/july/kieran-freeman-and-chris-mochrie-score-their-first-goals-for-dundee-united |access-date=18 July 2021 |work=BT Sport |date=14 July 2021}}</ref> He made his [[Scottish Premiership]] debut and first league start against [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] the following month.<ref name="Call-up">{{cite news |last1=Smith |first1=Ewan |title=Thomas Courts hails 'exceptional' Chris Mochrie as Dundee United teenager marks Scottish Premiership debut with international call-up |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/2493154/thomas-courts-hails-exceptional-chris-mochrie-as-dundee-united-teenager-marks-scottish-premiership-debut-with-international-call-up/ |access-date=29 August 2021 |work=The Courier |date=29 August 2021 |location=Dundee}}</ref>

In August 2022 Mochrie joined [[Dunfermline Athletic]] on a season long loan,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/3565540/dundee-united-chris-mochrie-dunfermline-pars-league-one/ | title=EXCLUSIVE: Dundee United kid Chris Mochrie set for Dunfermline deal as Pars fight off competition from League One rivals | date=5 August 2022 }}</ref> helping the Pars win the [[Scottish League One|League One]] title.

Mochrie made 30 appearances for Dundee United in the 2023/2024 season, scoring three goals. This included the winning goal against [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] on 20 April 2024 to "all but [seal] promotion" back to the top flight of Scottish football.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/68791774 | title=Dundee United 1-0 Ayr United: Mochrie winner all but seals promotion | work=BBC Sport | date=10 April 2024 }}</ref>

Mochrie signed with [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] in July 2024 after being released by Dundee United.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2024-07-09|title=Chris Mochrie joins Airdrie after Dundee United exit|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/c0w4egd7lelo|access-date=2024-07-13|website=BBC Sport|language=en-GB}}</ref>

Mochrie signed with [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren FC]] in July 2026 on a 2 year deal <ref>{{Cite web |title=Chris Mochrie joins St Mirren |url=https://www.stmirren.com/news/chris-mochrie-joins-st-mirren |access-date=2026-07-17 |website=St.Mirren FC |language=en}}</ref>

===International===
Mochrie was called up to the [[Scotland national under-16 football team|Scotland under-16]] squad in August 2018.<ref>{{cite news |title=Dundee United kids earn Scotland call-up to face England and Turkey |url=https://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/fp/dundee-united-kids-earn-scotland-call-up-to-face-england-and-turkey/ |accessdate=29 May 2019 |work=Evening Telegraph |date=8 August 2018 |location=Dundee}}</ref> He scored Scotland's goal in a 1–1 draw against [[Northern Ireland national under-16 football team|Northern Ireland]] in the [[Victory Shield]] in November 2018.<ref>{{cite news |title=Billy Gilmour double hands Scotland U19 Euro Championship qualifier win in Wales |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/billy-gilmour-double-hands-scotland-13591075 |accessdate=29 May 2019 |work=Daily Record |date=14 November 2018 |location=Glasgow}}</ref> After being involved in a training camp in August 2019,<ref>{{cite news |title=Chris Mochrie called up for Scotland under-17s camp |url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/6187/CHRIS-MOCHRIE-CALLED-UP-FOR-SCOTLAND-UNDER-17S-CAMP.html |accessdate=27 October 2019 |publisher=Dundee United F.C. |date=21 August 2019}}</ref> he made a scoring debut for [[Scotland national under-17 football team|Scotland under-17s]] in a 2–0 win against [[Armenia national under-17 football team|Armenia]] in October 2019.<ref>{{cite news |title=Under-17s start qualification with win over Armenia |url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/under-17s-start-qualification-with-win-over-armenia/ |accessdate=27 October 2019 |publisher=Scottish Football Association |date=22 October 2019}}</ref> He was called up to the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21 squad]] for the first time in August 2021.<ref name="Call-up" />

'''Finlay Robertson''' (born 12 November 2002) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a midfielder for {{Scottish football updater|Dundee}} club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].<ref>{{soccerbase|120207|accessdate=19 August 2019}}</ref>

==Club career==
Robertson began his career at his local Sunday League team Fairmuir Boys Club before joining the youth team of his boyhood club Dundee when he was 11. Finlay continued to progress through the age groups earning his first professional contract with the club on his sixteenth birthday.<ref>{{cite web|title=Finlay and Josh sign pro contracts|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/finlay-and-josh-sign-pro-contracts/|publisher=Dundee F.C.|date=12 November 2018|accessdate=15 September 2019}}</ref> He made his first team debut for Dundee in the final game of the [[2018–19 Scottish Premiership]] season against [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].<ref>{{cite web|title=What Dundee debutants were doing one hour after facing St Mirren|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/what-dundee-debutants-were-doing-16166374|publisher=Daily Record|last=McDougall|first=Mark|date=18 May 2019|accessdate=15 September 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Dundee 2–3 St Mirren|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48236247|publisher=BBC Sport|last=McLauchlin|first=Brian|date=18 May 2019|accessdate=15 September 2019}}</ref> New manager [[James McPake]] introduced Robertson into the first team squad for the 2019–20 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49500516|title=Finlay Robertson: Dundee 16-year-old 'will handle' city derby - James McPake|last=Smith|first=Tyrone|work=BBC Sport |date=28 August 2019}}</ref>

Robertson received consistent praise regarding his performances while being such a young age, becoming a first-team regular for the Dee and earning several Man of the Match and SPFL Team of the Week nominations. Despite his first senior season finishing early due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], Finlay was named as Dundee's Isobel Sneddon Young Player of the Year.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Finlay wins Isobel Sneddon Young Player of the Year|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/finlay-wins-isobel-sneddon-young-player-of-the-year/|last=|first=|date=1 May 2020|website=Dundee FC|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=1 May 2020}}</ref> In September 2020, Finlay signed a three-year extension with Dundee, keeping him at the club until 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=22 September 2020|title=Finlay signs new deal|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/finlay-sign-new-deal/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=22 September 2020|website=[[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]]}}</ref> In March 2021, it was announced that Robertson would miss the rest of the season with an ankle injury sustained in training.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Cran|first=George|date=22 March 2021|title=Fin Robertson: Highly-rated Dundee youngster ruled out for the rest of the season|url=https://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/fp/highly-rated-dundee-youngster-fin-robertson-ruled-out-for-the-rest-of-the-season/|access-date=23 March 2021|website=eveningtelegraph.co.uk}}</ref>

On 24 September 2021, Robertson joined [[Scottish League One]] side [[Cove Rangers F.C.|Cove Rangers]] on loan until January 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-09-24|title=Robertson Joins On Loan|url=https://coverangersfc.com/2021/09/24/robertson-joins-on-loan/|access-date=2021-09-24|website=Cove Rangers FC|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/cove-rangers/3493781/cove-rangers-paul-hartley-finlay-robertson/ |title=Cove Rangers: Fin Robertson will bring midfield quality, says Paul Hartley |first=Jamie |last=Durent |newspaper=Press & Journal |date=25 September 2021 |accessdate=25 September 2021}}</ref> Robertson returned to Dens in January, having made 10 appearances for Cove Rangers.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-01-17|title=Players return from loan|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/players-return-from-loan/|access-date=2022-01-17|website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-01-17|title=Robertson Returns to Parent Club Dundee|url=https://coverangersfc.com/2022/01/17/robertson-returns-to-dundee/|access-date=2022-01-17|website=Cove Rangers FC|language=en}}</ref>

On 26 November 2022, Robertson scored his first senior goal for Dundee, in a 6–2 [[Scottish Cup]] win over [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Dundee v Airdrieonians |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63685926 |access-date=2022-11-26}}</ref> It would take just two games later for Finlay to notch his second, in a [[Scottish Challenge Cup|Challenge Cup]] win away to [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dundee reach quarter-finals {{!}} SPFL |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/dundee-reach-quarter-finals |access-date=2022-12-08 |website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref> Robertson would win the [[Scottish Championship]] with Dundee at the end of the season.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |title=Dundee back in Premiership after eight-goal epic |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65420805 |access-date=2023-05-05}}</ref>

On 12 June 2023, Dundee announced that Robertson had signed a new two-year deal, keeping him at the club until the summer of 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-06-12 |title=New deal for Robertson |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/new-deal-for-robertson/ |access-date=2023-06-12 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> Over the next couple of seasons with new manager [[Tony Docherty]], Robertson would play a more diverse role for the ''Dee'' largely due to his [[Ambidexterity|ambidextrous]] feet, including regularly playing at [[Wing back (association football)|left wing back]] and taking corners from both sides with different feet, which saw him get more playing time than with previous managers.

On 4 February 2025, Dundee announced that Robertson had signed a new two-and-a-half year deal which would keep him at the club until the summer of 2027.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-02-04 |title=New deal for Robertson |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/new-deal-for-fin-robertson/ |access-date=2025-02-04 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> During the summer and between football seasons in Scotland, Robertson travelled to [[Mexico]] to train with Dundee's partner club [[C.F. Monterrey]] for a fortnight alongside players such as [[Sergio Ramos]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cran |first=George |date=2025-06-05 |title=Watch as Dundee ace joins superstar Sergio Ramos at Monterrey training in Mexico |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/5260813/video-dundee-sergio-ramos-monterrey-training-mexico/ |access-date=2025-06-05 |website=The Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref> After his return, Robertson was given the number 10 jersey after the departure of [[Lyall Cameron]] to [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=4 July 2025 |title=@DundeeFC on X |url=https://x.com/DundeeFC/status/1941195433906151597 |access-date=4 July 2025 |website=x.com}}</ref>

On 5 June 2026, Robertson signed a contract extension with Dundee which would last until 2028.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-06-05 |title=FIN ROBERTSON {{!}} DARK BLUE TILL 2028 |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/finrobertson2028/ |access-date=2026-06-05 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> On 6 September 2026, Robertson suffered an [[ACL injuries|ACL injury]] which ended his 2026–27 season prematurely.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-09-09 |title=Dundee: 'Devastating' ACL injury ends Finlay Robertson's season |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cy0zqdzxereo |access-date=2026-09-19 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

== International career ==
After an impressive start to his rookie season with Dundee, Robertson earned a call-up to the [[Scotland national under-19 football team|Scotland U19]] squad for two matches against [[Japan national under-20 football team|Japan]] in September 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=6 September 2019|title=Josh and Fin on international duty|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/josh-and-fin-on-international-duty/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=7 September 2019|website=Dundee FC}}</ref>

On 12 October 2023, Robertson was called up to the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland U21]] squad for the [[2025 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification Group B|2025 UEFA U21 Euros qualification group]] games against [[Hungary national under-21 football team|Hungary]] and [[Malta national under-21 football team|Malta]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-10-12 |title=Robertson joins Scotland Under 21's squad |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/finr-s21/ |access-date=2023-10-12 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-10-12 |title=Robertson links up with Scotland U21s |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/c2j970mgr2jo |access-date=2023-10-12 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> He made his debut off the bench in November, in an away victory over [[Belgium national under-21 football team|Belgium]] in the [[2025 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification Group B|UEFA Euro U21 qualifiers]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Scotland U21s go second with victory in Belgium |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67416721 |access-date=2023-11-18}}</ref>

'''Jayden De'Chante Richardson''' (born 4 September 2000) is an English professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|right back]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].

==Career==
===Nottingham Forest===
After impressing as part of the [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] academy, Richardson signed his first professional contract with the club in April 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nottinghampost.com/sport/football/football-news/nottingham-forest-youngster-announces-signed-2719325|title=Forest youngster announces he has signed professional deal|first=Nottinghamshire|last=Live|date=4 April 2019|website=nottinghampost}}</ref> He was named as part of the first team squad ahead of the [[2019–20 Nottingham Forest F.C. season|2019–20 season]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nottinghamforest.co.uk/news/2019/august/squad-numbers-confirmed-for-2019-20-season/|title=Squad numbers confirmed|website=www.nottinghamforest.co.uk}}</ref>

====Loan to Exeter City====
On 16 August 2019, Richardson joined [[EFL League Two|League Two]] side [[Exeter City F.C.|Exeter City]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nottinghamforest.co.uk/news/2019/august/richardson-joins-exeter-on-loan/|title=Richardson joins Exeter on loan|website=www.nottinghamforest.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.exetercityfc.co.uk/news/2019/august/jayden-richardson/|title=✍️ Jayden Richardson joins Exeter City on season-long loan|website=www.exetercityfc.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49374616|title=Jayden Richardson: Exeter City sign Nottingham Forest youngster on loan|date=16 August 2019|website=www.bbc.co.uk}}</ref> He made his professional debut on 20 August 2019, starting a 0–0 draw against [[Oldham Athletic A.F.C.|Oldham Athletic]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49326988|title=Oldham Athletic v Exeter City|date=20 August 2019|website=www.bbc.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.exetercityfc.co.uk/news/2019/august/MatchreportOldham/|title=📝 Match report: Oldham Athletic 0 Exeter City 0|website=www.exetercityfc.co.uk}}</ref> He scored his first professional goal against the same club, the first goal in a 5–1 win for Exeter.

====Loan to Forest Green Rovers====
On 23 September 2020, Richardson signed for [[EFL League Two|League Two]] club [[Forest Green Rovers F.C.|Forest Green Rovers]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fgr.co.uk/news/september-2020/signing-wing-back-richardson-joins-on-loan|title=SIGNING {{!}} Wing-back Richardson joins on loan|website=www.fgr.co.uk|access-date=23 September 2020|archive-date=13 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201013091023/https://www.fgr.co.uk/news/september-2020/signing-wing-back-richardson-joins-on-loan|url-status=dead}}</ref>

====Loan to Notts County====
On 7 December 2021, Richardson joined [[National League (division)|National League]] side [[Notts County F.C.|Notts County]] on a one-month loan deal.<ref>{{Cite web |url= https://www.nottscountyfc.co.uk/news/2021/december/richardson-signing-071221/ |title=Richardson joins on loan |publisher=Notts County FC |date=7 December 2021 |accessdate=7 December 2021}}</ref>
His loan was extended in January 2022 until the end of season.

===Aberdeen===
On 20 June 2022, Richardson signed with [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.afc.co.uk/2022/06/20/highly-rated-young-defender-joins-dons/ | title=Highly Rated Young Defender Joins Dons | date=20 June 2022 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nottinghamforest.co.uk/news/2022/june/20/richardson-departs/ | title=Richardson departs }}</ref>

On 26 July 2023, Richardson joined [[EFL League Two|League Two]] side [[Stockport County F.C.|Stockport County]] on a season-long loan deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stockportcounty.com/richardson-joins-on-loan/|title=Richardson joins on loan|publisher=[[Stockport County F.C.]]|date=26 July 2023|accessdate=26 July 2023}}</ref> However, the deal was cut short in January 2024 and he was loaned again to fellow League Two side [[Colchester United F.C.|Colchester United]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/67960868 |title=Jayden Richardson: Colchester United sign Aberdeen full-back on loan|publisher=BBC Sport|date=12 January 2024|accessdate=2 February 2024}}</ref>

===Boreham Wood===
On 20 September 2024, Richardson joined [[National League South]] club [[Boreham Wood F.C.|Boreham Wood]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.borehamwoodfootballclub.co.uk/uncategorized/welcome-to-meadow-park-jayden-richardson/|title=WELCOME TO MEADOW PARK, JAYDEN RICHARDSON!|website=www.borehamwoodfootballclub.co.uk|date=20 September 2024|accessdate=20 September 2024}}</ref>

===St Mirren===
Richardson returned to Scottish football in June 2025, signing a two-year contract with [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c62dmgn6k3no |title='All attributes are there' for Jayden Richardson to succeed at St Mirren, says Stephen Robinson |website=BBC Sport |date=18 June 2025 |accessdate=19 June 2025}}</ref>

'''George William Stanger''' (born 15 August 2000) is a professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]]. Born in Scotland, Stanger represents the [[New Zealand men's national football team|New Zealand national team]].

==Early and personal life==
Stanger's father is former [[Scotland national rugby union team|Scottish International]] [[rugby union]] player [[Tony Stanger]], and his mother Bid is from [[Auckland]], New Zealand.<ref name="auto"/> George was born in [[Melrose, Scottish Borders|Melrose]] in the [[Scottish Borders]]; the family eventually settled in [[Dunblane]].<ref name="auto"/><ref name=hero>{{cite web |url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/rugby-union/scotland/interview-scotland-rugby-hero-tony-stanger-on-why-he-loves-football-1-4831226 |title=Interview: Scotland rugby hero Tony Stanger on why he loves football |author=Aiden Smith |work=The Scotsman |date=17 November 2018 |access-date=24 August 2019}}</ref><ref name=starlet>{{cite web |url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/scotland-could-miss-out-on-hamilton-starlet-starring-at-fifa-u20-world-cup-and-son-of-scottish-rugby-royalty-1-4936134/amp |title=Scotland could miss out on Hamilton starlet starring at Fifa U20 World Cup – and son of Scottish rugby royalty |author=Joel Sked |work=The Scotsman |date=28 May 2019 |access-date=24 August 2019}}</ref>

==Club career==
Stanger began his career with [[Stirling Albion F.C.|Stirling Albion]], joining [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] in January 2018 before being loaned back to Stirling Albion for the rest of the season, making his senior debut in [[Scottish League Two]].<ref name=starlet/><ref name=hero/><ref>{{soccerbase|108893}}</ref><ref name=sway/> During the 2018–19 campaign he played for Hamilton's [[Hamilton Academical F.C. Reserves and Academy|youth teams]], including in the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]] and the [[UEFA Youth League]].<ref name=fcb22>{{cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-match-reports/hamilton-accies-uefa-youth-league-13475206|title=Hamilton Accies UEFA Youth League adventure continues after dramatic penalty victory over Basel|work=Daily Record|date=24 October 2018|access-date=24 August 2019}}</ref><ref name=starlet/><ref name=sway/>

In the summer 2019 transfer window, he was linked with a move away from Hamilton.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eveningtimes.co.uk/sport/17846337.hamilton-youngster-george-stanger-set-loan-move-amid-leeds-united-interest/|title=Hamilton youngster George Stanger set for loan move amid Leeds United interest|website=Evening Times|date=19 August 2019}}</ref> He made his first professional-level start for the club in the [[Scottish Premiership]] on 24 August, a 3–1 home defeat to [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] in the [[Lanarkshire derby]].<ref name=sway/><ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49378871 Hamilton Academical 1–3 Motherwell: Visitors claim first league victory], BBC Sport, 24 August 2019</ref>

In September 2019 he moved on loan to [[East Kilbride F.C.|East Kilbride]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/george-stanger-goes-on-loan-to-east-kilbride/|title=George Stanger Goes On Loan To East Kilbride|date=3 September 2019|website=Hamilton Academical Website|access-date=6 September 2019|archive-date=6 September 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190906083223/https://www.hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/george-stanger-goes-on-loan-to-east-kilbride/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In January 2020 he moved on loan to [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar Athletic]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/scottish-league-1/1069790/forfar-boss-stuart-malcom-signs-defender-george-stanger-on-loan-from-hamilton/|title=Forfar boss Stuart Malcolm signs defender George Stanger on loan from Hamilton|first=Ian|last=Roache|date=9 January 2020 }}</ref>

He was released by Hamilton in October 2021<ref>{{cite tweet|number=1445072035701534720|user=acciesfc|title=Defender George Stanger, 21, has been released by the club. After representing New Zealand in the Olympics in July…|date=4 October 2021}}</ref> and joined [[University of Stirling F.C.|University of Stirling]] in the [[Lowland Football League]], before signing for [[Scottish League One]] side [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] on loan in February 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dumbarton Football Club – GEORGE STANGER ARRIVES ON LOAN|url=https://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=5253|access-date=18 February 2022|website=www.dumbartonfootballclub.com}}</ref> He scored his first goal in senior football for the Sons in a 3–2 defeat to [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] in April 2022<ref>{{Cite news |title=Airdrieonians v Dumbarton |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60903665 |access-date=16 April 2022}}</ref> but turned down a new deal following the club's relegation to [[Scottish League Two]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dumbarton Football Club – GEORGE MOVES ON |url=https://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=5364 |access-date=2 June 2022 |website=www.dumbartonfootballclub.com}}</ref>

'''Jake Alan Young''' (born 22 July 2001) is an English professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for Scottish club [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].

Young joined [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]] from [[Guiseley A.F.C.|Guiseley]] in 2019, though moved on to [[Forest Green Rovers F.C.|Forest Green Rovers]] in July 2020 without playing a first-team game for Sheffield United. He played over 50 games for Forest Green, helping the club to win the League Two title in the 2021–22 campaign, and signed for Bradford City in July 2022. He spent the second half of the 2022–23 season on loan at [[Barrow A.F.C.|Barrow]] and was loaned out to [[Swindon Town F.C.|Swindon Town]] for the first half of the 2023–24 season. He signed for [[Stevenage F.C.|Stevenage]] in August 2024.

==Career==
===Early career===
Born in [[Huddersfield]], Young grew up supporting [[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield Town]].<ref name=Huddersfield>{{cite news |last1=Loveridge |first1=Ashley |title=Huddersfield fan Young takes the sting out of Bradford {{!}} Stroud Times |url=https://stroudtimes.com/huddersfield-fan-young-takes-the-sting-out-of-bradford/ |access-date=14 January 2024 |work=Stroud Times |date=31 October 2021}}</ref> He moved from Shelley Juniors to [[Guiseley A.F.C.|Guiseley]] in 2017.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.yorkshireeveningpost.co.uk/sport/rugby-union/guiseley-teenager-jake-young-snapped-sheffield-united-550870|title=Guiseley teenager Jake Young snapped up by Sheffield United|website=www.yorkshireeveningpost.co.uk|date=2 January 2019 }}</ref> He scored six goals in one [[FA Youth Cup]] match against [[Ossett United F.C.|Ossett United]] and was an unused [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] for the first-team in an [[FA Cup]] match.<ref>{{cite news |title=Jake Young: "Guiseley Is Everything For Me" |url=https://guiseleyafc.co.uk/jake-young-guiseley-is-everything-for-me/ |access-date=14 January 2024 |work=Guiseley AFC |date=16 January 2024}}</ref> He moved to [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]] after impressing manager [[Chris Wilder]] on trial in January 2019,<ref name="auto"/> but was released by the club before he signed for [[Forest Green Rovers F.C.|Forest Green Rovers]] in July 2020.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Charlesworth |first1=Ricky |title=Sheffield United youngster signs contract at League Two club following release |url=https://www.examinerlive.co.uk/sport/football/news/sheffield-united-youngster-departs-club-18606474 |access-date=14 January 2024 |work=Yorkshire Live |date=16 July 2020 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53431143|title=Forest Green: Sheffield United's teenage striker Jake Young signs on two-year deal|work=BBC Sport |date=16 July 2020}}</ref>

Reserves and Academy|West Bromwich Albion U21s]] on 6 October 2020.<ref name = "2020-21"/> His first league goal came eleven days later, in a 2–0 win over [[Stevenage F.C.|Stevenage]] at [[The New Lawn]], in which he was also named as [[Player of the match|man of the match]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Match Report: Forest Green Rovers 1-0 Stevenage |url=https://www.fgr.co.uk/news/match-report-forest-green-rovers-1-0-stevenage |access-date=14 January 2024 |work=fgr.co.uk |date=17 October 2020}}</ref> He scored eight goals in 33 appearances throughout the [[2020–21 Forest Green Rovers F.C. season|2020–21]] campaign.<ref name = "2020-21"/> [[Mark Cooper (footballer, born 1968)|Mark Cooper]], sacked as manager shortly before the season's end, said that Young possessed "[[Premier League]] ability", but needed to contribute more defensively.<ref name="preml"/> Young scored four goals in 29 games in the [[2021–22 Forest Green Rovers F.C. season|2021–22]] season as Rovers were promoted as champions of [[EFL League Two|League Two]] under the management of [[Rob Edwards (footballer, born 1982)|Rob Edwards]].<ref name="2021–22"/>
