'''Djenairo Gillian Noell Daniels''' (born 7 January 2002) is a professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]]. Born in the Netherlands, he plays for the [[Suriname national football team|Suriname national team]].

==Early life==
At age 11, he had a trial with the youth system of [[PSV Eindhoven]],<ref>{{cite news |title=PSV plukt talent weg bij Almere City FC |url=https://www.vi.nl/nieuws/psv-plukt-talent-weg-bij-almere-city-fc |work=[[Voetbal International]] |date=10 July 2018 |language=nl|trans-title=PSV plucks talent from Almere City FC}}</ref> but then joined the youth system of [[Almere City FC|Almere City]], where he played for the next six years.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://utrecht.nieuws.nl/sport/77186/fc-utrecht-neemt-spits-djenairo-daniels-over-van-psv/|title=FC Utrecht neemt spits Djenairo Daniels over van PSV|trans-title=FC Utrecht takes over striker Djenairo Daniels from PSV|language=nl|date=January 7, 2021|work=Utrecht Nieuws}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ed.nl/psv/psv-legt-talent-van-almere-city-vast-djenairo-daniels~ae0bf19a/|title=PSV legt talent van Almere City vast: Djenairo Daniels|language=nl|first=Rik|last=Elfrink|date=July 10, 2018|work=[[Eindhovens Dagblad]]|trans-title=PSV captures talent from Almere City: Djenairo Daniels}}</ref> In July 2018, he joined the youth system of [[PSV Eindhoven]] at the age of sixteen, signing a three-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.omroepflevoland.nl/sport/162054/jeugdvoetballer-daniels-16-naar-psv|title=Jeugdvoetballer Daniels (16) naar PSV|trans-title=Youth footballer Daniels (16) to PSV|date=July 10, 2018|language=nl|work=Omroep Flevoland}}</ref>

==Club career==
He made his senior debut for PSV's second team [[Jong PSV]] in the second tier [[Eerste Divisie]] on 29 August 2020 against [[Excelsior Rotterdam]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.voetbalprimeur.nl/nieuws/961464/19-jarige-jeugdinternational-vertrekt-op-verjaardag-van-psv-naar-fc-utrecht.html|title=19-jarige jeugdinternational vertrekt op verjaardag van PSV naar FC Utrecht|trans-title=19-year-old youth international leaves PSV for FC Utrecht on his birthday|language=nl|date=January 7, 2021|work=Voetbalprimeur}}</ref> He scored his first professional goal on 2 October 2020 against [[SC Telstar]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://psv.supporters.nl/nieuws/artikel/47855/Jong-PSV-wint-met-ruime-cijfers-van-Telstar|title=Jong PSV wint met ruime cijfers van Telstar|language=nl|trans-title=Young PSV beat Telstar with big numbers|date=October 2, 2020|work=PSV Supporters}}</ref> After not getting any opportunities with the first team, he was allowed to leave the club in January 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ed.nl/psv/psv-laat-belofte-djenairo-daniels-19-naar-fc-utrecht-vertrekken~a0dc04e7a/|title=PSV laat belofte Djenairo Daniels (19) naar FC Utrecht vertrekken|language=nl|trans-title=PSV lets promise Djenairo Daniels (19) leave for FC Utrecht|date=January 7, 2021|first=Rik|last=Elfrink|work=[[Eindhovens Dagblad]]}}</ref>

In January 2021, he signed a contract with [[FC Utrecht]] until 2023 with an option for a further season,<ref>{{cite ==International career==
Born in the Netherlands, Daniels is of Surinamese descent.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.natiosuriname.com/p/profvoetballers-van-surinaamse-afkomst.html|title=Profvoetballers van Surinaamse afkomst|website=Natio Suriname|trans-title=Professional football players of Surinamese descent|language=nl|access-date=22 November 2020|archive-date=24 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200924084846/https://www.natiosuriname.com/p/profvoetballers-van-surinaamse-afkomst.html|url-status=usurped}}</ref> He was named to the [[Netherlands national under-17 football team|Netherlands U17]] roster for the [[2019 UEFA European Under-17 Championship]] and [[2019 FIFA U-17 World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.voetbalzone.nl/doc.asp?uid=347986|title=Ajax levert veertig procent van volledige selectie Oranje Onder-17|trans-title=Ajax supplies forty percent of the entire selection Orange Under-17|language=nl|first=Dominic|last=Mostert|date=March 11, 2019|work=Voetbalzone}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.onsoranje.nl/nieuws/jeugd-mannen-onder-18/77059/selectie-onder-18-voor-wk-brazili%C3%AB|title=Selectie Onder 17 voor WK in Brazilië|language=nl|trans-title=Squad Under 17 for World Cup in Brazil|work=ONS Oranje}}</ref> He also was named to the [[Netherlands national under-18 football team|Netherlands U18]] in a four nations mini-tournament in 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.psv.nl/english-psv/news/article/which-psv-players-are-away-on-international-duty.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190920015600/https://www.psv.nl/english-psv/news/article/which-psv-players-are-away-on-international-duty.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=20 September 2019|title=Which PSV players are away on international duty?|work=[[PSV Eindhoven]]|date=September 2, 2019}}</ref>

In August 2025, Daniels began filing the required paperwork to play for [[Suriname national football team|Suriname]] at international level.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.voetbalzone.nl/nieuws/gesprekken-met-ryan-flamingo-gaven-avonturier-hoop-ik-dacht-zelfs-aan-stoppen/blte55eb2a40af9895f|title=Gesprekken met Ryan Flamingo gaven avonturier hoop: 'Ik dacht zelfs aan stoppen'|trans-title=Conversations with Ryan Flamingo gave adventurer hope: 'I even thought about quitting'|language=Dutch|first=Wessel|last=Antes|work=[[Voetbalzone]]|date=August 18, 2025}}</ref> On 30 September 2025, he was called up to the national team for the first time ahead of their [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification – CONCACAF third round|2026 FIFA World Cup qualification]] matches against [[Guatemala national football team|Guatemala]] and [[Panama national football team|Panama]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/ayrshire/kilmarnock-defender-aiming-world-cup-35990451|title=Kilmarnock defender aiming for World Cup bid after receiving maiden international call-up|first=Callum|last=Carson|work=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]]}}</ref> He made his debut for Suriname, during the 1–1 draw against Guatemala on 10 October 2025, as a second-half substitute, but he had to be substituted out himself due to injury.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.telegraaf.nl/sport/voetbal/wk-kwalificatie-virgil-misidjan-redt-punt-voor-suriname-tegen-guatemala-met-late-gelijkmaker/96764038.html|title=WK-kwalificatie: Virgil Misidjan redt punt voor Suriname tegen Guatemala met late gelijkmaker|trans-title=World Cup Qualifying: Virgil Misidjan saves a point for Suriname against Guatemala with a late equalizer|language=Dutch|date=11 October 2025|work=[[De Telegraaf]]|first=Jeroen|last=Kapteijns}}</ref>

'''Nikolas Agrafiotis''' ({{lang-sr-Cyrl|Николас Аграфиотис}}; born 25 April 2000) is a professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].

Born in the Netherlands, he has represented [[Serbia national under-16 football team|Serbia]] at youth level.

==Club career==
===Early years===
Agrafiotis played in the youth departments of [[FC Den Bosch]] and [[SBV Vitesse|Vitesse]]. From 2016 to 2020 he also played for the second team of the latter, [[Jong Vitesse]]. On 26 November 2016, he made his debut in the third-tier [[Tweede Divisie]] for Jong Vitesse, in the 3–0 away loss to [[VV Katwijk]].<ref>{{cite web |title=VV Katwijk – Vitesse (J) 3:0 (Tweede Divisie 2016/2017, 15. Round) |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/match-report/ma8266853/lineup/ |website=WorldFootball.net |publisher=HEIM:SPIEL |access-date=8 October 2024 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241008103601/https://www.worldfootball.net/report/tweede-divisie-2016-2017-vv-katwijk-vitesse-j/ |archive-date=8 October 2024}}</ref> Jong Vitesse suffered relegation to the [[Derde Divisie]] Sunday after the 2016–17 season, after which they reached promotion again a season later and returned to the Tweede Divisie.<ref>{{cite news |title=Jong Vitesse degradeert uit Tweede Divisie |url=https://www.gld.nl/nieuws/2133855/jong-vitesse-degradeert-uit-tweede-divisie |access-date=8 October 2024 |work=Omroep Gelderland |date=6 May 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241008103821/https://www.gld.nl/nieuws/2133855/jong-vitesse-degradeert-uit-tweede-divisie |archive-date=8 October 2024 |language=nl}}</ref>

===Dordrecht===
In June 2020, Agrafiotis signed as a free agent for [[FC Dordrecht]], where he signed a contract until mid-2022.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lammers |first1=Lex |title=Spits Agrafiotis van Vitesse naar FC Dordrecht |url=https://www.gelderlander.nl/vitesse/spits-agrafiotis-van-vitesse-naar-fc-dordrecht~a06f3986/ |access-date=30 November 2020 |work=De Gelderlander |date=29 June 2020 |language=nl}}</ref> He made his professional debut on 30 August 2020, in a 0–0 home draw against [[Go Ahead Eagles]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Houtappels |first1=Joost |title=Veldmate: 'Leek alsof we onder stroom stonden' |url=https://www.destentor.nl/ga-eagles/veldmate-leek-alsof-we-onder-stroom-stonden~a25baed5/ |access-date=30 November 2020 |work=de Stentor |date=30 August 2020 |language=nl |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221011182715/https://www.destentor.nl/ga-eagles/veldmate-leek-alsof-we-onder-stroom-stonden~a25baed5/ |archive-date=11 October 2022 |url-status=live}}</ref>

===Excelsior===
On 31 January 2022, Agrafiotis signed a one-and-a-half-year contract with [[SBV Excelsior|Excelsior]], with an option for an additional year.<ref>{{cite web |title=Excelsior legt Nikolas Agrafiotis voor anderhalf jaar vast |url=https://excelsiorrotterdam.nl/2022/01/excelsior-legt-nikolas-agrafiotis-voor-anderhalf-jaar-vast/ |website=Excelsior Rotterdam |language=nl |date=31 January 2022 |access-date=5 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205150854/https://excelsiorrotterdam.nl/2022/01/excelsior-legt-nikolas-agrafiotis-voor-anderhalf-jaar-vast/ |archive-date=5 February 2022 |url-status=live}}</ref> He made his debut for the club on 7 February in a 4–1 league loss to [[FC Eindhoven]], coming off the bench for [[Reuven Niemeijer]] in the 75th minute.<ref>{{cite web |title=Excelsior komt dramatische start niet meer te boven tegen Eindhoven |url=https://excelsiorrotterdam.nl/2022/02/excelsior-komt-dramatische-start-niet-meer-te-boven-tegen-eindhoven/ |website=Excelsior Rotterdam |access-date=30 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220208104117/https://excelsiorrotterdam.nl/2022/02/excelsior-komt-dramatische-start-niet-meer-te-boven-tegen-eindhoven/ |archive-date=8 February 2022 |language=nl |date=7 February 2022 |url-status=live}}</ref> Mostly appearing as a substitute, he would make his first start for the team on 29 April in a league draw against [[VVV-Venlo]], also providing an assist to the late equaliser by [[Marouan Azarkan]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Excelsior Rotterdam redt een punt tegen VVV-Venlo |url=https://excelsiorrotterdam.nl/2022/04/excelsior-rotterdam-redt-een-punt-tegen-vvv-venlo/ |website=Excelsior Rotterdam |access-date=30 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220430001418/https://excelsiorrotterdam.nl/2022/04/excelsior-rotterdam-redt-een-punt-tegen-vvv-venlo/ |archive-date=30 April 2022 |language=nl |date=29 April 2022 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Agrafiotis would prove decisive in the playoffs for promotion after Excelsior qualified by finishing sixth in the league table.<ref>{{cite news |title=Excelsior gelooft in promotie naar Eredivisie: 'Zijn beste counterploeg van de KKD' |url=https://www.nu.nl/voetbal/6202222/excelsior-gelooft-in-promotie-naar-eredivisie-zijn-beste-counterploeg-van-de-kkd.html |access-date=30 May 2022 |work=NU |date=22 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220525020144/https://www.nu.nl/voetbal/6202222/excelsior-gelooft-in-promotie-naar-eredivisie-zijn-beste-counterploeg-van-de-kkd.html |archive-date=25 May 2022 |language=nl}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club late in [[Overtime (sports)|extra time]] of the first round second leg against [[Roda JC Kerkrade]] to secure a 4–2 win on aggregate.<ref>{{cite news |title=Excelsior legt Roda na lange en soms verhitte voetbalavond over de knie |url=https://www.vi.nl/nieuws/excelsior-legt-roda-na-lange-en-soms-verhitte-voetbalavond-over-de-knie |access-date=30 May 2022 |work=Voetbal International |date=14 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220516031954/https://www.vi.nl/nieuws/excelsior-legt-roda-na-lange-en-soms-verhitte-voetbalavond-over-de-knie |archive-date=16 May 2022 |language=nl}}</ref> He scored again on 21 May in a 3–1 win over [[Heracles Almelo]], as they suffered relegation from the [[Eredivisie]] for the first time in two decades, and Excelsior advanced to the playoff final.<ref>{{cite news |title=Geen wonder van Almelo: Heracles verliest ook thuis van Excelsior en degradeert uit de Eredivisie |url=https://www.rtvoost.nl/nieuws/2102379/geen-wonder-van-almelo-heracles-verliest-ook-thuis-van-excelsior-en-degradeert-uit-de-eredivisie |access-date=30 May 2022 |work=RTV Oost |date=21 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220521233732/https://www.rtvoost.nl/nieuws/2102379/geen-wonder-van-almelo-heracles-verliest-ook-thuis-van-excelsior-en-degradeert-uit-de-eredivisie |archive-date=21 May 2022 |language=nl}}</ref> Excelsior would eventually win promotion to the [[Eredivisie]] after a penalty shoot-out against [[ADO Den Haag]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Knotsgek duel en rellen in Den Haag: Excelsior promoveert en vlucht van het veld |url=https://nos.nl/artikel/2430722-knotsgek-duel-en-rellen-in-den-haag-excelsior-promoveert-en-vlucht-van-het-veld |access-date=30 May 2022 |work=NOS |date=29 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220530220525/https://nos.nl/artikel/2430722-knotsgek-duel-en-rellen-in-den-haag-excelsior-promoveert-en-vlucht-van-het-veld |archive-date=30 May 2022 |language=nl}}</ref>

===Wehen Wiesbaden===
On 31 January 2024, Agrafiotis signed with [[SV Wehen Wiesbaden|Wehen Wiesbaden]] in German [[2. Bundesliga]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Wehen Wiesbaden|url=https://svww.de/news/artikel/svww-verpflichtet-nikolas-agrafiotis|title=SVWW VERPFLICHTET NIKOLAS AGRAFIOTIS|trans-title=SVWW SIGNS NIKOLAS AGRAFIOTIS|date=31 January 2024|access-date=31 January 2024|language=de|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240131090309/https://svww.de/news/artikel/svww-verpflichtet-nikolas-agrafiotis|archive-date=31 January 2024|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===St Mirren===
On 30 August 2026, Agrafiotis signed with [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]]. He scored his first goal for the club from the penalty spot in a home league match against Celtic, which St Mirren lost 2–1.

==International career==
Agrafiotis was born in the Netherlands to a Greek father and a Serbian mother. He is a youth international for Serbia.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Bomgaars |first1=Arco |url=https://www.ad.nl/regiosport-dordrecht/fc-dordrecht-aanvaller-nikolas-agrafiotis-snakt-naar-goals-ik-had-dit-seizoen-al-moeten-scoren~ab043f23/ |title=FC Dordrecht-aanvaller Nikolas Agrafiotis snakt naar goals: 'Ik had dit seizoen al moeten scoren' |work=de Stentor |date=18 September 2020 |language=nl |access-date=13 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201007031823/https://www.ad.nl/regiosport-dordrecht/fc-dordrecht-aanvaller-nikolas-agrafiotis-snakt-naar-goals-ik-had-dit-seizoen-al-moeten-scoren~ab043f23/ |archive-date=7 October 2020 |url-status=live}}</ref>

'''Jonathan Meier''' (born 11 November 1999) is a German professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[left-back]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].<ref>{{WorldFootball.net}}</ref>

==Career==
Meier made his professional debut for [[Dynamo Dresden]] in the [[3. Liga]] on 18 September 2020, starting in the away match against [[1. FC Kaiserslautern]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/match-report/ma9122751/lineup/ |title=Germany » 3. Liga 2020/2021 » 1. Round » 1. FC Kaiserslautern – Dynamo Dresden |website=WorldFootball.net |date=18 September 2020 |access-date=18 September 2020}}</ref>

On 14 August 2021, he joined [[FC Hansa Rostock|Hansa Rostock]] on loan.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fc-hansa.de/news/leihe-fuer-ein-jahr-f-c-hansa-rostock-verpflichtet-jonathan-meier-von-mainz-05.html|title=Leihe für ein Jahr: F.C. Hansa Rostock verpflichtet Jonathan Meier von Mainz 05|website=fc-hansa.de|date=14 August 2021|access-date=15 August 2021|language=de}}</ref>

On 11 June 2022, Meier agreed to return to Dynamo Dresden on a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Dynamo Dresden|url=https://www.dynamo-dresden.de/aktuelles/news/profis/willkommen-zurueck-sgd-verpflichtet-jonathan-meier/|title=WILLKOMMEN ZURÜCK! SGD VERPFLICHTET JONATHAN MEIER|date=11 June 2022|access-date=22 July 2022|language=de}}</ref>

On 12 June 2024, Meier signed a two-season contract with [[SSV Ulm 1846|SSV Ulm]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=SSV Ulm|url=https://www.ssvulm1846-fussball.de/profis/der-ssv-verpflichtet-jonathan-meier|title=DER SSV VERPFLICHTET JONATHAN MEIER|trans-title=SSV SIGNS JONATHAN MEIER|date=12 June 2024|access-date=4 July 2024|language=de}}</ref>

On 31 July 2026, Meier signed a two year deal with Kilmarnock in the Scottish Premiership, becoming the first German player to sign for the club.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Paton |first=Ewan |date=2026-07-31 |title=Jonathan Meier added to our ranks |url=https://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/news/jonathan-meier-added-to-our-ranks/ |access-date=2026-07-31 |website=Kilmarnock FC |language=en}}</ref>

'''Ryan James Finnigan''' (born 22 September 2003) is an English professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[central midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|Dundee}} club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].

==Club career==

=== Southampton ===
Having joined [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]]'s academy in May 2012,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.southamptonfc.com/en/teams/profile/ryan-finnigan | title=Ryan Finnigan |publisher=Southampton F.C. |access-date=5 September 2023}}</ref> Finnigan signed a professional contract with the club in December 2020.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.southamptonfc.com/news/2020-12-11/four-youngsters-sign-new-professional-deals-southampton-fc-academy-2020-21|title=Four youngsters sign professional deals|work=Southampton FC|date=11 December 2020|access-date=20 January 2021}}</ref> On 19 January 2021, Finnigan made his first professional appearance in Southampton's victory over [[Shrewsbury Town F.C.|Shrewsbury Town]] in the [[FA Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55574523|title=Southampton 2–0 Shrewsbury Town|date=19 January 2021|access-date=20 January 2021}}</ref>

==== Crewe Alexandra (loan) ====
On 18 January 2023, Finnigan joined [[EFL League Two|League Two]] side [[Crewe Alexandra F.C.|Crewe Alexandra]] for the remainder of the season,<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 January 2023 |title=Crewe Alexandra: Brighton keeper James Beadle and Southampton midfielder Ryan Finnigan join |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64325240 |access-date=18 January 2023 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> making his Crewe debut against [[Stockport County F.C.|Stockport County]] at [[Gresty Road]] on 31 January 2023.<ref name="BBC-31Jan2023">{{cite news |title=Crewe Alexandra 1-1 Stockport County |url=https://www.soccerbase.com/players/player.sd?player_id=136094 |access-date=15 February 2023 |work=BBC Sport |date=31 January 2023}}</ref> In his fifth appearance for ''the Railwaymen'', he scored his first professional goal, helping Crewe to a 2–0 home win against [[Hartlepool United F.C.|Hartlepool United]] on 14 February 2023.<ref name="BBC-14Feb2023">{{cite news |title=Crewe Alexandra 2-0 Hartlepool United 0 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64549646 |access-date=15 February 2023 |work=BBC Sport |date=14 February 2023}}</ref>

==== Shrewsbury Town (loan) ====
On 1 September 2023, Finnigan joined [[EFL League One|League One]] side [[Shrewsbury Town F.C.|Shrewsbury Town]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{Cite web |date=1 September 2023 |title=Ryan Finnigan makes Shrewsbury loan switch |url=https://www.southamptonfc.com/en/news/article/ryan-finnigan-makes-shrewsbury-loan-switch |access-date=1 September 2023 |website=Southampton FC}}</ref> He made his debut for the club on 5 September 2023 in a 3–0 defeat to [[Forest Green Rovers F.C.|Forest Green Rovers]] in the [[EFL Trophy]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Westbury |first=Ollie |date=5 September 2023 |title=EFL Trophy: Forest Green 3 Shrewsbury 0 – Report |url=https://www.shropshirestar.com/sport/football/shrewsbury-town-fc/2023/09/05/efl-trophy-forest-green-3-shrewsbury-0---report/ |access-date=21 September 2023 |website=Shropshire Star}}</ref> At the end of September, Finnigan suffered an ankle injury during training and was expected to be sidelined for several months.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Westbury |first=Ollie |date=1 October 2023 |title=Shrewsbury Town hit with Ryan Finnigan injury blow |url=https://www.shropshirestar.com/sport/football/shrewsbury-town-fc/2023/10/01/shrewsbury-town-hit-with-ryan-finnigan-injury-blow/ |access-date=5 October 2023 |website=Shropshire Star}}</ref>

=== Blackpool ===
On 31 January 2024, Finnigan was recalled from loan and joined League One side [[Blackpool F.C.|Blackpool]] on a permanent transfer for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{Cite web |date=31 January 2024 |title=Ryan Finnigan departs for permanent Blackpool move |url=https://www.southamptonfc.com/en/news/article/ryan-finnigan-departs-for-permanent-blackpool-move |access-date=31 January 2024 |website=Southampton FC}}</ref> He scored on his debut for the club, a 4–0 over Burton Albion in the first round of the EFL Cup on 13 August 2024.<ref>[https://www.skysports.com/football/burton-albion-vs-blackpool/510637 Burton Albion 0–4 Blackpool] – Sky Sports, 13 August 2024</ref>

==== Walsall (loan) ====
On 18 August 2025, Finnigan joined League Two side [[Walsall F.C.|Walsall]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 August 2025 |title=Ryan Finnigan Joins Walsall On Loan |url=https://www.blackpoolfc.co.uk/news/2025/august/18/ryan-finnigan-joins-walsall-on-loan/ |access-date=18 August 2025 |website=Blackpool FC}}</ref> He was named [[EFL League Two Player of the Month]] for November 2025, contributing three goals as ''the Saddlers'' continued their push for promotion.<ref name="Nov25 POTM"> {{cite web|url=https://www.efl.com/news/2025/december/12/sky-bet-league-two-manager-and-player-of-the-month-winners/|title=Sky Bet League Two Manager and Player of the Month winners|website=www.efl.com|date=12 December 2025|accessdate=14 December 2025}}</ref> He was recalled by Blackpool on 5 January 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2026 |title=Ryan Finnigan: Blackpool recall midfielder from Walsall loan |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c3940dg1k2xo |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 6 May 2026, Blackpool announced it had triggered an extension on the player's contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-06 |title=James Husband: Blackpool release former captain after seven years |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cg5pd79l176o |access-date=2026-05-12 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

=== Dundee ===
On 27 June 2026, Finnigan joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] on a three-year deal for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-06-27 |title=Ryan Finnigan Signs For The Dee |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/ryanfinnigan/ |access-date=2026-06-27 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Nicky Cleșcenco''' (born 23 July 2001) is a [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Midfielder#Winger|left winger]] for {{Scottish football updater|Kilmarno}} club [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]]. Born in Ireland, he plays for the [[Moldova national football team|Moldova national team]].<ref>{{WorldFootball.net}}</ref>

==Club career==
Cleșcenco played for [[Dacia Buiucani]] in his youth, before moving to Portugal in 2014 to play for the academies of [[Sporting CP]] and [[U.D. Leiria|União de Leiria]]. During the 2019–20 season, he made six senior appearances for União de Leiria in the [[Campeonato de Portugal (league)|Campeonato de Portugal]]. In February 2021, he joined the reserve team of Swiss club [[FC Sion|Sion]], playing in the [[Swiss Promotion League|Promotion League]].<ref name="FMF"/> On 17 February 2025 he signed for [[FC Zimbru Chișinău|Zimbru Chișinău]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://fmf.md/noutate/12379/nicky-clescenco-a-semnat-cu-zimbru-chisinau |title=Nicky Cleșcenco a semnat cu Zimbru Chișinău |website=fmf.md |publisher=[[Moldovan Football Federation]] |language=Romanian |date=17 February 2025}}</ref>

On 30 January 2026, Cleșcenco signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] on an eighteen-month contract.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/news/moldovan-international-winger-nicky-clescenco-signs-on-permanent-deal/|title=Moldovan International winger Nicky Cleşcenco signs on permanent deal|website=kilmarnockfc.co.uk|date=30 January 2026|accessdate=30 January 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
Cleșcenco made his international debut for [[Moldova national football team|Moldova]] on 3 June 2021, coming on as a substitute in the 87th minute for [[Dan Spătaru (footballer)|Dan Spătaru]] in a [[Exhibition game|friendly]] match against [[Turkey national football team|Turkey]]. The match in [[Paderborn]] finished as a 2–0 loss.<ref name="EUF">{{cite web |url=https://eu-football.info/_player.php?id=31503 |title=Nicky Cleșcenco |website=EU-Football.info |access-date=3 June 2021}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Cleșcenco was born in [[Dublin]], Ireland,<ref>{{Soccerway}}</ref> and is the son of former footballer and manager [[Serghei Cleșcenco]].<ref name="FMF"/>

'''Richard King''' (born 27 November 2001) is a Jamaican professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] and the [[Jamaica national football team|Jamaica national team]]. He previously played for [[Jamaica Premier League]] (JPL) club [[Cavalier F.C.|Cavalier]] and for [[Besta deild karla]] club [[ÍBV men's football|ÍBV]].

== Club career ==
King played for Cavalier FC in Jamaica.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.jamaicaobserver.com/sports/cavalier-defender-king-having-a-dream-season_232757?profile=1855 | title=Cavalier defender King having a dream season }}</ref>

In 2023, King spent one season on loan at [[ÍBV men's football|ÍBV]] in Iceland.

King return to Cavalier in 2024 and lead them to the JPL title.<ref>https://www.jamaicaobserver.com/2024/05/29/cavaliers-king-ready-fight-national-overseas-objectives/</ref>

===St Mirren===

In June 2025, King signed with [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] in the Scottish Premiership.<ref>https://jamaica-gleaner.com/article/sports/20250618/st-mirren-confirm-kings-move</ref><ref>https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/5880-jamaican-international-richard-king-joins-st-mirren</ref>

==International career ==
King made his senior international debut for Jamaica during a 3–0 loss against [[Peru national football team|Peru]] on 20 January 2020, and also feature in a WCQ match against [[Costa Rica national football team|Costa Rica]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://jamaica-gleaner.com/article/sports/20220120/king-beckford-make-international-starts-vs-peru | title=King, Beckford make international starts vs Peru | date=20 January 2022 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.jamaicaobserver.com/sports/boyz-exit-world-cup-race-with-a-whimper-after-going-down-to-costa-rica_243050 | title=Show's over! }}</ref>

On 28 May 2025, King scored his first goal for Jamaica, a penalty, during a 3–2 win against [[Trinidad and Tobago national football team|Trinidad and Tobago]] during the [[2025 Unity Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 May 2025 |title=Jamaica vs. Trinidad and Tobago 3–2 |url=https://uk.soccerway.com/matches/2025/05/27/world/friendlies/jamaica/trinidad-and-tobago/4641196/ |access-date=27 May 2025 |website=Soccerway}}</ref>

'''Ryan Astley''' (born 4 October 2001) is a Welsh professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for {{Scottish football updater|Dundee}} club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].<ref>{{soccerbase|116334}}</ref> He is a former Wales under-21 international.

==Early life==
Astley is from [[Llanfair Caereinion]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.countytimes.co.uk/news/20278472.powys-footballer-ryan-astley-seals-loan-move-accrington-stanley/|title=Powys football star seals move to English football league side|website=County Times |date=14 July 2022 }}</ref>

==Club career==
Astley began his career with [[Everton F.C.|Everton]], making his debut for their under-23 team at the age of 16 in 2018, before being offered a new contract in April 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/everton-offer-defender-new-contract-20362994|title=Everton offer defender new contract as season-ending injury confirmed|first=Sam|last=Carroll|date=12 April 2021|website=Liverpool Echo}}</ref> He was an unused substitute for their FA Cup match against [[Boreham Wood F.C.|Boreham Wood]] in March 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.countytimes.co.uk/news/19968897.powys-star-astley-bench-everton-seal-fa-cup-progress/|title=Powys football ace Ryan Astley makes bench for Everton in FA Cup|website=County Times |date=4 March 2022 }}</ref> Astley moved to [[Accrington Stanley F.C.|Accrington Stanley]] on loan from Everton in July 2022,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62157679|title=Accrington sign Everton defender Astley|work=BBC Sport |date=13 July 2022 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.accringtonstanley.co.uk/news/2022/july/signing-ryan-joins-on-loan/|title=SIGNING: Ryan joins on loan|website=www.accringtonstanley.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/everton-defender-delighted-completes-loan-24482841|title=Everton defender 'delighted' as he completes loan move|first=Paul|last=Wheelock|date=13 July 2022|website=Liverpool Echo}}</ref> and made his professional debut on 6 August 2022, appearing as a substitute.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.countytimes.co.uk/news/20606130.everton-wales-ace-astley-helps-accrington-stanley-victory-loan-debut/|title=Powys star makes English League debut as Accrington Stanley beat 10 man Shrewsbury|website=County Times |date=6 August 2022 }}</ref>

On 18 January 2024, Astley joined [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] on a two-and-a-half-year contract for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/astley-arrives/|title=Astley arrives at Dundee|website=dundeefc.co.uk|date=18 January 2024|accessdate=18 January 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/c80201kxkp7o|title=Dundee sign Astley from Everton for undisclosed fee|date=18 January 2024|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> He said that speaking with [[Owen Beck (footballer)|Owen Beck]], with whom he shared an agent, had helped him agree to the move.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/c9020w9gz7vo|title=Beck endorsement 'sealed' Astley transfer|date=18 January 2024|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> Astley made his debut for Dundee as a substitute in a league game away to [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=St Mirren strengthen top-six bid with Dundee win |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68136292 |access-date=8 February 2024 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 13 July 2024, Astley scored his first goal for Dundee in a 1–7 away victory over [[Bonnyrigg Rose F.C.|Bonnyrigg Rose]] in the [[Scottish League Cup]] group stage.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bonnyrigg Rose vs. Dundee - 13 July 2024 - Soccerway |url=https://uk.soccerway.com/matches/2024/07/13/scotland/league-cup/bonnyrigg-rose-athletic-fc/dundee-fc/4360410/ |access-date=13 July 2024 |website=uk.soccerway.com}}</ref>

On 9 August 2025, Astley scored his first league goal for Dundee, in a league draw away to [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rangers vs Dundee: Scottish Premiership stats & head-to-head |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cwypd9d0vk3t |access-date=9 August 2025 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 14 May 2026, Dundee confirmed that Astley had signed a contract extension with the club until 2029.<ref>{{Cite web |date=14 May 2026 |title=Ryan Astley: Here until 2029 |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/ryan-astley-here-until-2029/ |access-date=16 May 2026 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref>

==International career==
Astley is a Wales youth international.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://uk.soccerway.com/players/ryan-astley/482939/|title=Wales – R. Astley – Profile with news, career statistics and history – Soccerway|website=uk.soccerway.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.countytimes.co.uk/news/local/llanfair_caereinion/19535823.powys-everton-star-astley-earns-welsh-21s-call/|title=Wales look to Astley as Powys and Everton star called up for Bulgarian clash|website=County Times |date=25 August 2021 }}</ref> He has captained the under-21 team,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.countytimes.co.uk/news/local/llanfair_caereinion/20214322.powys-raised-everton-star-astley-leads-wales-u21s-triumph/|title=Llanfair Caereinion and Everton star leads out Wales for U21s international clash|website=County Times |date=16 June 2022 }}</ref> and has trained with the under-23 team.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.countytimes.co.uk/news/local/llanfair_caereinion/19997363.powys-everton-star-astley-earns-wales-u23-camp-call/|title=Powys star Astley earns Wales call ups for U23 European Championship qualifiers|website=County Times |date=16 March 2022 }}</ref>

'''Killian Phillips''' (born 30 March 2002) is an Irish [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as an [[attacking midfielder]] for [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]]. Born in United States, he represents the [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland national team]].

==Early life==
Phillips was born in [[San Diego]] to Irish parents on 30 March 2002 and moved to [[Kilbarrack]], [[Dublin]] as a 5-year-old.<ref name=the42>{{Cite web |last=Sneyd |first=David |title=The start of a journey in football: 'I feel like I'm always chasing, and being chased' |url=https://www.the42.ie/killian-phillips-crystal-palace-5775558-May2022/ |access-date=5 August 2022 |website=The42 |date=29 May 2022 |language=en}}</ref> He began playing football aged 5 with [[Kilbarrack United F.C.|Kilbarrack United]], then moved to Corduff at under-13 level, spending 4 seasons there and playing alongside fellow future senior [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland]] international [[Bosun Lawal]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/soccer/2025/0902/1531457-lawal-keeping-the-faith-and-eyeing-ireland-involvement/|title=Lawal keeping the faith and eyeing Ireland involvement|first=Ed|last=Leahy|date=2 September 2025|via=www.rte.ie}}</ref> followed by a stint at [[St. Kevin's Boys F.C.|St Kevin's Boys]] before returning to Kilbarrack at 16 after being rejected by [[Bohemian F.C.|Bohemians]] and [[Shelbourne F.C.|Shelbourne]] at under-17 level, then eventually earning a move to the academy of [[League of Ireland]] club [[Drogheda United F.C.|Drogheda United]] where he would play for their under-19 side.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/premier-league/im-starting-from-the-ground-up-again-mam-im-at-the-bottom-of-the-totem-pole-killian-phillips/41911851.html|title=‘I’m starting from the ground up again Mam, I’m at the bottom of the totem pole’ – Killian Phillips|date=15 August 2022|website=Irish Independent}}</ref><ref name=ind.ie>{{Cite web |title='He looked a box-to-box player with |url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/premier-league/he-looked-a-box-to-box-player-with-a-lot-of-strength-kilbarrack-youth-killian-phillips-catches-patrick-vieiras-eye-41269451.html ==Club career==
===Drogheda United===
Having been a non-playing substitute in some matches in 2020, Phillips made his debut for [[Drogheda United F.C.|Drogheda United]] in a 1–0 loss at home to [[Shamrock Rovers F.C.|Shamrock Rovers]] on 20 April 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.extratime.com/articles/27047/league-report-drogheda-united-0-1-shamrock-rovers/|title=League Report: Drogheda United 0 – 1 Shamrock Rovers|website=extratime.com}}</ref> The first senior goal of Phillips' career came on 8 May 2021, in a 7–0 win away to [[Waterford F.C.|Waterford]] at the [[Waterford Regional Sports Centre|RSC]] as the home side fielded their under-19 squad due to a [[COVID-19]] outbreak in the first team.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.extratime.com/matches/detail/42827/2/|title=League Report: Waterford 0 - 7 Drogheda United|website=ExtraTime.com}}</ref> On 24 October 2021, he scored the only goal of the game as Drogheda beat [[Derry City F.C.|Derry City]] at [[United Park]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/soccer/2021/1024/1255603-phillips-heads-drogheda-to-victory-over-derry/|title=Phillips heads Drogheda to victory over Derry|first=Barry|last=Landy|date=24 October 2021|via=www.rte.ie}}</ref> He made 31 appearances in all competitions during the 2021 season, scoring two goals.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ie.soccerway.com/players/killian-phillips/663530/|title=Republic of Ireland - K. Phillips - Profile with news, career statistics and history - Soccerway|website=ie.soccerway.com}}</ref>

===Crystal Palace===
At the end of the season, Phillips had a trial with [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] and made a permanent move to the [[Premier League]] club in January 2022,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Drogs ace Phillips signs Palace deal |url=https://www.independent.ie/regionals/louth/sport/soccer/drogs-ace-phillips-signs-palace-deal-41227986.html |access-date=5 August 2022 |website=independent |date=11 January 2022 |language=en}}</ref> and spent the rest of the [[2021–22 Crystal Palace F.C. season|2021–22 season]] with the club's under-23 team.<ref name=the42 /> In March 2022, he was selected for the [[Republic of Ireland national under-21 football team|Republic of Ireland under-21 squad]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Keep track of Palace's Academy internationals as Phillips earns U21s nod – News |url=https://www.cpfc.co.uk/news/academy/keep-track-of-crystal-palaces-academy-international-call-ups/2022-03-23/ |access-date=5 August 2022 |website=Crystal Palace F.C. |date=23 March 2022 |language=en-GB}}</ref> but was only involved as a non-playing substitute. He was part of the Crystal Palace first-team squad that travelled to Singapore and Australia before the [[2022–23 Crystal Palace F.C. season|2022–23 season]] and started in the friendly games against [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] and [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=AFP |title=Dubliner Killian Phillips starts for Crystal Palace in loss to Liverpool |url=https://www.the42.ie/liverpool-crystal-palace-killian-phillips-5818092-Jul2022/ |access-date=5 August 2022 |website=The42 |date=15 July 2022 |language=en}}</ref>
Phillips made his competitive senior debut for Crystal Palace on 23 August 2022, starting in a 2–0 win away to [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]] in the [[EFL Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Team news: Three debuts for Palace v Oxford – News |url=https://www.cpfc.co.uk/news/first-team/team-news-oxford-united-v-crystal-palace-in-league-cup-rodney-johnstone-and-phillips-debuts/2022-08-23/ |access-date=24 August 2022 |website=Crystal Palace F.C. |date=June 2022 |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url= https://uk.soccerway.com/matches/2022/08/23/england/league-cup/oxford-united-fc/crystal-palace-fc/3918237/|title=OXFORD UNITED VS CRYSTAL PALACE|website=Soccerway}}</ref>

====Loan to Shrewsbury Town====
On 29 December 2022, it was announced that Phillips would join [[Shrewsbury Town F.C.|Shrewsbury Town]] on loan until the end of the season, once the transfer window opened on 1 January 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Killian Phillips joins Salop on loan from Crystal Palace |url=https://www.shrewsburytown.com/news/2022/december/killian-phillips-joins-salop-on-loan-from-crystal-palace/ |access-date=2022-12-29 |website=www.shrewsburytown.com |language=en-gb}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Shrewsbury sign Palace midfielder Phillips on loan |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64119896 |access-date=2022-12-29}}</ref> Despite only featuring for half of the season, Phillips was awarded the Young Player of the Season for his efforts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gallery {{!}} Awards Night 2022/23 |url=https://www.shrewsburytown.com/news/2023/april/gallery--awards-night-202223/ |access-date=2023-05-23 |website=www.shrewsburytown.com |language=en-gb}}</ref> His performances for the ''Shrews'' were described as "immense" by the club's manager [[Steve Cotterill]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Westbury |first=Ollie |date=2023-04-22 |title='Immense' Killian Phillips has been a real loan star for Shrewsbury |url=https://www.shropshirestar.com/sport/football/shrewsbury-town-fc/2023/04/22/immense-killian-phillips-has-been-a-real-loan-star-for-shrewsbury/ |access-date=2023-05-23 |website=www.shropshirestar.com |language=en}}</ref>

====Loan to Wycombe Wanderers====
On 11 August 2023, Phillips signed a new contract with Crystal Palace and on the same day also joined [[EFL League One]] club [[Wycombe Wanderers F.C.|Wycombe Wanderers]] on a season long loan deal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cpfc.co.uk/news/announcement/killian-phillips-signs-new-contract-joins-wycombe-wanderers/|title=Killian Phillips signs new contract and joins Wycombe on loan - News|date=11 August 2023|website=Crystal Palace F.C.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/killian-phillips-crystal-palace-wycombe-wanderers-loan-6141173-Aug2023/|title=Ireland U21 Phillips agrees new Crystal Palace deal before League One loan|first=Niall|last=Kelly|date=11 August 2023|website=The 42}}</ref> Phillips scored his first league goal for the club in a 2–1 loss against local rivals [[Reading F.C.|Reading]] on 25 November 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67459982.amp|title=Wycombe Wanderers 1-2 Reading|date=25 November 2023|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

====Loan to Aberdeen====
After it was mutually agreed to cut short his loan at Wycombe Wanderers, Phillips joined Scottish club [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] on 28 January 2024 until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/crg933qgmdjo.amp|title=Aberdeen sign Killian Phillips on loan from Crystal Palace|date=28 January 2024|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 20 April 2024, he featured in the [[2023–24 Scottish Cup#Semi-finals|Scottish Cup Semi-final]] at [[Hampden Park]] which ended in heartbreak as he took his side's final penalty in the shootout which was saved by [[Joe Hart]], sending [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] through to the final.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aberdeenlive.news/sport/football/killian-phillips-opens-up-worst-9504513.amp|title=Killian Phillips opens up on 'worst feeling' at Aberdeen after cup heartbreak|first=P. A.|last=by Ronnie Esplin|date=23 August 2024|website=Aberdeen Live}}</ref>

====Loan to St Mirren====
On 21 August 2024, Phillips joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] on a season-long loan deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/5534-st-mirren-announce-signing-of-killian-phillips|title=St Mirren announce signing of Killian Phillips|website=www.stmirren.com|date=21 August 2024|accessdate=22 August 2024}}</ref> He scored 4 goals in 37 appearances in all competitions during his loan season with the club, before being voted the club's Player of the Year at the end of the season.<ref name="SMPOTY25">{{Cite web | title=St Mirren Player of the Year Awards 2024/25 | url=https://www.stmirren.com/commercial-news/5861-st-mirren-player-of-the-year-2024-25 | access-date=2025-08-25 | website=www.stmirren.com}}</ref>

===St Mirren===
On 22 May 2025 it was announced that Phillips had joined [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] on a permanent deal after the club activated their obligation to buy, following his loan spell, joining on a one-year contract with the option of a further season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/5864-2024-25-squad-update|title=2024/25 Squad Update|website=www.stmirren.com}}</ref> On 14 December 2025, Phillips played the full match in the [[2025 Scottish League Cup final]], as his side defeated [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] 3–1 at [[Hampden Park]] to win the first trophy of his career and the club's first in 12 years.<ref name="ScottishLC">{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/soccer/2025/12/14/irish-player-tracker-killian-phillips-and-roland-idowu-lift-scottish-league-cup-for-st-mirren/|title=Irish player tracker: Killian Phillips and Roland Idowu lift Scottish League Cup for St Mirren|first=Conor|last=McEvoy|date=14 December 2025|website=The Irish Times}}</ref>

==International career==
Phillips' first involvement at international level came in March 2022, when he captained a [[Republic of Ireland national under-21 football team|Republic of Ireland U20]] team in a 1–0 friendly match defeat against the Republic of Ireland Amateur side at [[Whitehall Stadium]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fai.ie/ireland/news/report-ireland-u20s-0-1-ireland-amateurs|title=REPORT | Ireland U20s 0-1 Ireland Amateurs | Football Association of Ireland|website=fai.ie}}</ref> His performance earned him a call up to the U21 side for their qualifying fixture away to [[Sweden national under-21 football team|Sweden U21]] the following week.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fai.ie/ireland/news/squad-update-burns-phillips-and-mcentee-join-u21s-squad|title=SQUAD UPDATE | Burns, Phillips and McEntee join U21s squad | Football Association of Ireland|website=fai.ie}}</ref> He made his debut for the U21 team in a 2–1 friendly win over [[Iceland national under-21 football team|Iceland U21]] at [[Turners Cross (stadium)|Turners Cross]] on 26 March 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fai.ie/ireland/match/55502/2023/999948672?tab=report|title=Republic of Ireland 2 – 1 Iceland | 2023 – Under-21 Mens Friendlies | 999948672 | Football Association of Ireland|website=fai.ie}}</ref> On 21 November 2023, he scored his first goal for his country in a 2–2 draw at home to [[Italy national under-21 football team|Italy U21]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.the42.ie/ireland-italy-u21-soccer-6228853-Nov2023/ | title=Heartbreak for Ireland as Italy claim dramatic late draw in Euro qualifier | date=21 November 2023 }}</ref>

On 14 May 2025, he received his first senior call up to the [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland national team]] for their friendly fixtures against [[Senegal national football team|Senegal]] and [[Luxembourg national football team|Luxembourg]] in June.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/international-soccer/heimir-hallgrimsson-calls-up-four-new-players-for-forthcoming-ireland-friendlies/a1103889987.html|title=Heimir Hallgrimsson calls up four new players for forthcoming Ireland friendlies|date=14 May 2025|website=www.independent.ie}}</ref> Phillips made his senior international debut on 6 June 2025, coming off the bench in a 1–1 draw with [[Senegal national football team|Senegal]] at the [[Aviva Stadium]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/international-soccer/heimir-hallgrimsson-highlights-positive-part-of-irelands-game-following-senegal-draw/a1590742303.html|title=Heimir Hallgrimsson highlights positive part of Ireland’s game following Senegal draw|date=6 June 2025|website=www.independent.ie}}</ref> He made his first start for the side 4 days later in a 0–0 draw away to [[Luxembourg national football team|Luxembourg]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/international-soccer/luxembourg-v-ireland-chances-at-a-premium-in-drab-end-of-season-encounter/a1907207554.html|title=Luxembourg v Ireland: Chances at a premium in drab end of season encounter|date=10 June 2025|website=Irish Independent}}</ref>

'''Jacob Anthony Chapman''' (born 22 October 2000) is an Australian professional [[association football|soccer]] player who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for {{Scottish football updater|StMirren}} club [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].

==Career==
Born in [[Wahroonga, New South Wales|Wahroonga]], Chapman spent his early career with [[Sydney United 58 FC|Sydney United 58]] and [[Marconi Stallions FC|Marconi Stallions]], before moving to England in 2018.<ref name="HTAFC"/> He signed for [[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield Town]] in January 2019 following a trial, and spent loan spells in non-league at [[Ossett United F.C.|Ossett United]] and [[Gateshead F.C.|Gateshead]].<ref name="HTAFC">{{Cite web|url=https://www.htafc.com/academy/huddersfield-town-b-team/goalkeeper/jacob-chapman/|title=Jacob Chapman – Goalkeeper – Huddersfield Town B Team – Huddersfield Town|website=www.htafc.com}}</ref> He moved on loan to [[Salford City F.C.|Salford City]] on 1 September 2022.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62759838|title=Salford sign Chapman, Galbraith and Bailey|work=BBC Sport }}</ref>

He made his debut for Huddersfield Town on 26 December 2023 in their 3–0 win against [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]], replacing the injured [[Chris Maxwell (footballer)|Chris Maxwell]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.examinerlive.co.uk/sport/football/news/jacob-chapman-over-moon-huddersfield-28353292|title=Jacob Chapman 'over the moon' with Huddersfield Town debut in Boxing Day win|date=27 December 2023|website=Yorkshire Live}}</ref>

On 21 March 2024, Chapman moved to [[Rochdale A.F.C.|Rochdale]] on loan until the end of the 2023–24 season.<ref>{{Cite news |date=21 March 2024 |title=Goalkeeper Chapman Joins |url=https://www.rochdaleafc.co.uk/news/2024/march/jacobchapmansigns/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240415022534/https://www.rochdaleafc.co.uk/news/2024/march/jacobchapmansigns/ |archive-date=15 April 2024 |access-date=17 July 2025 |language=en-gb |url-status=dead }}</ref> He signed on loan for [[Crawley Town F.C.|Crawley Town]] in January 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cwyr61e7d2po|title=Crawley Town sign Huddersfield keeper Jacob Chapman as striker Tola Showunmi departs|date=23 January 2026|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

===St Mirren===
On 1 July 2026, Chapman signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] on an initial two-year deal for an undisclosed fee.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/6461-goalkeeper-jacob-chapman-joins-on-two-year-deal|title=Goalkeeper Jacob Chapman joins on two-year deal|website=www.stmirren.com|date=1 July 2026|accessdate=1 July 2026}}</ref>

The SFA Performance Schools 10 years on], James Wilson, Shorthand Stories, June 2022 Rice signed for Rangers on 30 June 2022 after rejecting a professional contract with the ''Steelmen''.[https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2022/06/30/rice-leaves-to-join-rangers/ Bailey Rice leaves to join Rangers], Motherwell FC, 30 June 2022{{cite news|url=https://twitter.com/RFC_Youth/status/1542478052390838273?s=20&t=hjJCvUcunBbetmKQNxCj-Q|title=Rangers Academy are delighted to confirm that Under-17s player Bailey Rice will join us from Motherwell|work=Rangers FC|publisher=Twitter|date=30 June 2022}} He made his senior debut for Rangers in February 2023 in a [[Scottish Premiership]] match away to [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] as an 88th-minute substitute for [[Ryan Kent]],{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64607179 | title=Livingston 0–3 Rangers | work=BBC Sport | publisher=BBC | date=18 February 2023 | access-date=18 February 2023 }}{{ cite news | url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/football/23539984.inside-story-rices-rangers-debut-scotland-cap-within-24-hours/ | title=Inside story of Rice's Rangers debut & Scotland cap within 24 hours | publisher=The Herald | date=22 May 2023 | first=David | last=Irvine |url-access=subscription}} becoming the youngest [[post-war]] league player for the club, aged 16 years and 137 days, and the second youngest post-war player in all competitions, after [[Derek Ferguson]].{{ cite news | url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/who-bailey-rice-rangers-boss-31000535 | title=Who is Bailey Rice? Rangers boss Michael Beale declares starlet 'ready for the madhouse' | publisher=Daily Record | date=22 September 2023 | first=Ross | last=Pilcher }} In September of that year he signed a contract extension running to 2026.[https://www.rangers.co.uk/article/bailey-rice-signs-contract-extension/2ZqPBCU5UMv8OLyjhmM63g Bailey Rice Signs Contract Extension], Craig Vickers, Rangers FC, 12 September 2023 Rice made his [[UEFA Europa League]] debut on 28 November 2024, replacing [[Nedim Bajrami]] in the 80th minute of a 4–1 away win over [[OGC Nice]]. On 10 April 2025, he was selected to start in the competition's quarter-final first leg against [[Athletic Bilbao]], but had to be carried off on a stretcher with an hour played after suffering a head injury.{{ cite news | url=https://www.thenational.scot/sport/25081469.bailey-rice-stretchered-off-nasty-rangers-head-knock/ | title=Bailey Rice stretchered off after nasty Rangers head knock | publisher=The National | date=10 April 2025 | first=David | last=Irvine }} He made only 12 appearances overall during the campaign, with his progress compared unfavourably with that of former Motherwell youth teammate [[Lennon Miller]],[https://www.pressreader.com/uk/the-courier-advertiser-perth-and-perthshire-edition/20250313/282505779371173 Gemmill tells young duo to ‘make good decisions’], [[The Courier (Dundee)|The Courier]], 13 March 2025, via [[PressReader]] while Rice indicated his hope for more first-team opportunities in the season ahead.{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c0k3j7g0704o | title='I don't want to be squad player' - Rice on Rangers role | work=BBC Sport | date=10 May 2025 | access-date=24 July 2025 }} ==International career== Rice has represented [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] at youth levels, playing 14 matches for the [[Scotland national under-17 football team|under-17 team]].{{cite web|title=Bailey Rice Scottish FA player profile|url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/players/?pid=376766&lid=13|website=scottishfa.co.uk|accessdate=31 January 2023}} His debut for Rangers came less than 24 hours after playing for Scotland under-17s in Spain against [[Switzerland national under-17 football team|Switzerland]]. '''Imari Narain Che Hines-Samuels''' (born 5 February 2003) is an English [[association football|footballer]] who plays for {{Scottish football updater|Dundee}} club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] as a left-back.<ref name="sw">{{cite web |url=https://uk.soccerway.com/players/imari-narain-samuels/536028/ |title=Imari Samuels |publisher=Soccerway |access-date=18 May 2023}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Reading===
A youth product of [[Reading F.C.|Reading]], he signed scholarship terms with the club as a sixteen-year-old in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.readingfc.co.uk/players/u23/imari-samuels |website=ReadingFC |title=Imari Samuels |accessdate=18 May 2023}}</ref> He began training with the first team for the first time in August 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.getreading.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/striker-missing-teenager-steps-up-18788966 |website=Getreading.co.uk |first=Jonathan |last=Low |accessdate=18 May 2023 |date=19 August 2020 |title=Striker missing, teenager steps up and golden boots - seven things we spotted as Reading FC return for pre-season}}</ref> This came after he signed a one-and-a-half-year contract with Reading in January 2020, keeping him with the club until the summer of 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.getreading.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/who-imari-samuels-lowdown-teenage-18792686 |website=getreading.co.uk |accessdate=18 May 2023 |first1=Kristian |last1=Heneage |first2=Jonathan |last2=Low |title=Who is Imari Samuels? The lowdown on the teenage Reading FC defender training with the first team|date=20 August 2020 }}</ref> Samuels picked up an injury that required surgery in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |first=Jonathan |last=Low |url=https://www.getreading.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/reading-premier-league-transfer-brighton-24686291?int_source=amp_continue_reading&int_medium=amp&int_campaign=continue_reading_button#amp-readmore-target |date=5 August 2022 |website=Getreading.com |accessdate=18 May 2023 |title=Reading FC youngster breaks silence after sealing Premier League transfer to Brighton}}</ref>

===Brighton===
In August 2022, Samuels turned down Reading's offer of a new contract in order to join the academy of [[Premier League]] team [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]] on a two-year deal, with Reading receiving compensation from Brighton for his services.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.theargus.co.uk/sport/20602955.amp/ |date=5 August 2022 |first=Brian |last=Owen |website=The Argus |title=Brighton sign Imari Samuels from Reading |accessdate=18 May 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.getreading.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/reading-transfer-exit-premier-league-24677671 |website=getreading.co.uk |accessdate=18 May 2023 |title=Reading FC transfer exit confirmed as Imari Samuels makes Premier League move after Paul Ince verdict |first=Robert |last=Warlow |date=5 August 2022}}</ref>

On 18 May 2023 Samuels was included in a [[Premier League]] match day line-up for the first time, being named as substitute for Brighton away at [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://uk.soccerway.com/matches/2023/05/18/england/premier-league/newcastle-united-football-club/brighton--hove-albion-fc/3800225/ |website=Soccerway |date=18 May 2023 |accessdate=18 May 2023 |title=NEWCASTLE VS. BRIGHTON}}</ref> He made his Brighton debut in the 4-0 win over [[Crawley Town F.C.|Crawley Town]] in the [[EFL Cup]] in August 2024.<ref>{{cite web|date=14 January 2025|title= 'I'm ready to go' – Transfer decision made as Brighton ace makes permanent January exit|first=Derren |last=Howard|url= https://www.sussexexpress.co.uk/sport/football/brighton-and-hove-albion/im-ready-to-go-transfer-decision-made-as-brighton-ace-makes-permanent-january-exit-4942406|website=Sussex Express|accessdate=16 January 2025}}</ref>

=== Dundee ===
On 13 January 2025, Samuels joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] on a two-and-a-half year deal for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-01-13 |title=Samuels is a Dee |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/samuels-dee/ |access-date=2025-01-13 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> On 20 January, Samuels made his debut for the ''Dark Blues'' as a substitute against rivals [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] in the [[Scottish Cup]], and helped Dundee win their first [[Dundee derby]] since 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dundee end wait for derby win to knock Dundee United out of Cup |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cjdenj593znt |access-date=2025-01-22 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==International career==
Samuels has been selected at youth level by England at U15, [[England national under-16 football team|U16]] and [[England national under-17 football team|U17]] level.<ref>{{Cite web |first=Frankie |last=Elliott |url=https://www.sussexexpress.co.uk/sport/football/brighton-and-hove-albion/brighton-youngsters-picked-for-england-under-20-world-cup-squad-in-argentina-4138378 |website=Sussex Express |title=Brighton youngsters picked for England under-20 World Cup squad in Argentina |date=11 May 2023 |accessdate=18 May 2023}}</ref> In May 2023 he was selected as part of the [[2023 FIFA U-20 World Cup squads|England squad]] for the [[2023 FIFA U-20 World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Former Reading FC youngster off to the World Cup after England call-up |date=11 May 2023 |accessdate=18 May 2023 |website=Reading Chronicle |url=https://www.readingchronicle.co.uk/sport/23514732.former-reading-fc-youngster-off-world-cup-england-call-up/ |first=James |last=Earnshaw}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |first=Nizar |last=Kinsella |website=Evening Standard |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/england-u20-world-cup-chelsea-arsenal-tottenham-chukwuemeka-b1080278.html |title=England Under-20 World Cup squad: Chelsea, Tottenham and Arsenal stars called up |date=11 May 2023 |accessdate=18 May 2023}}</ref> His two appearances during the tournament both came in the group stage as a substitute against [[Uruguay national under-20 football team|Uruguay]] and starting in a goalless draw against [[Iraq national under-20 football team|Iraq]].<ref name="sw"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/match/_/gameId/668572 |title=Iraq 0-0 England |publisher=ESPN |access-date=12 June 2023}}</ref>

'''Johnly Levi Yfeko''' (born 23 June 2003) is an English professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[centre-back]] or [[left-back]] for Scottish Premiership club [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]]. He previously had spells with [[Exeter City F.C.]] and [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]], as well as the academies of both [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] and [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]]

==Career==
Yfeko started his career in the youth ranks of [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C|Tottenham Hotspur]] before being picked up by [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Willis |first=Cameron |date=2024-08-11 |title=MOTM Rangers loanee has ‘massive potential’ as stunning debut raises ‘option to buy’ fears |url=https://www.rangersnews.uk/news/motm-rangers-loanee-has-massive-potential-as-stunning-debut-raises-option-to-buy-fears/ |access-date=2025-09-07 |website=Rangers News |language=en-GB}}</ref> Yfeko signed for [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] and was a key defender for the Under-18s and 23s before being released in the summer of 2021. After being released he went on trial at [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]]'s Under-18s but was not signed.

===Rangers===

In January 2022, Yfeko signed for [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] on a short-term deal, however, he impressed significantly to earn an extension until the summer of 2024.<ref>{{ cite news | url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/johnly-yfeko-turns-rangers-heads-26673997  | title=Johnly Yfeko turns Rangers heads as January arrival pens long term Ibrox deal | first=Steven | last=Mair  | publisher=Daily Record | date=9 April 2022  }}</ref><ref>{{ Cite news|url=https://twitter.com/RFC_Youth/status/1512732053825064960?s=20&t=pPke9_6t9I1l4t1wugPoGw
|title=Johnly Yfeko signs contract extension|work=Rangers FC|publisher=Twitter, Inc|date=9 April 2022}}</ref>

He made appearances regularly playing for [[Rangers F.C. B Team and Academy|Rangers B]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hendry |first=Mark |date=2022-01-31 |title=Rangers new signing poses with jersey after Leicester move as Ramsey on verge |url=https://www.footballscotland.co.uk/spfl/scottish-premiership/rangers-new-signing-johnly-yfeko-22934876 |access-date=2024-01-20 |website=Football Scotland |language=en}}</ref>

=== Exeter City (loan) ===
On 23 July 2024, Yfeko joined Exeter City on a season-long loan, with an option to buy.<ref>{{Cite news|url= https://www.exetercityfc.co.uk/news/johnly-yfeko-grecian
|title= Johnly Yfeko Is A Grecian!|date= 23 July 2024|work= Exeter City F.C.}}</ref>

=== Exeter City ===
On 5 May 2025, Yfeko made his loan move to Exeter City permanent as the club triggered the option-to-buy option is his loan contract. The fee was undisclosed.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shahaney |first=Pranav |date=2025-05-05 |title=Rangers exit now official as defender joins English club |url=https://www.ibroxnews.com/2025/05/05/rangers-exit-now-official-as-defender-joins-english-club/ |access-date=2025-09-07 |website=Ibrox News |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Johnly Yfeko joins City on a permanent deal! {{!}} Exeter City F.C. |url=https://www.exetercityfc.co.uk/JohnlyPerm |access-date=2025-09-07 |website=www.exetercityfc.co.uk |language=en}}</ref>

===Kilmarnock===
On 31 July 2026, Yfeko returned to Scotland, joining [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] on a two-year deal for an undisclosed fee.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/news/defence-bolstered-with-johnly-yfeko-arrival/|title=Defence bolstered with Johnly Yfeko arrival|website=kilmarnockfc.co.uk|date=31 July 2026|accessdate=16 October 2026}}</ref>

'''Michael Schjønning-Larsen''' (born 2 February 2001) is a [[association football|football]]er who plays as a [[left-back]] for [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]]. Born in Denmark, he represents the [[Estonia national football team|Estonia national team]].<ref name="boldreturn">{{cite web|publisher=bold.dk|url=https://bold.dk/fodbold/nyheder/back-er-skiftet-til-estisk-topklub-vil-gerne-tilbage-til-dansk-fodbold/|title=Back er skiftet til estisk topklub: Vil gerne tilbage til dansk fodbold|date=24 February 2023}}</ref>

==Career==
On 16 December 2025, Schjǿnning-Larsen agreed to join [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] on an eighteen-month contract, joining from 1 January 2026.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/news/michael-schjonning-larsen-signs-for-kilmarnock/|title=Michael Schjønning-Larsen signs for Kilmarnock|website=kilmarnockfc.co.uk|date=16 December 2025|accessdate=28 December 2025}}</ref>

==International career==
Schjønning-Larsen made his debut for the [[Estonia national football team|Estonia national team]] on 8 June 2024 in a 4–1 [[2024 Baltic Cup|Baltic Cup]] victory against the [[Faroe Islands national football team|Faroe Islands]] at the [[Lilleküla Stadium]]. He started the game and played 78 minutes.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Soccerway|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2024/06/08/europe/baltic-cup/estonia/faroe-islands/4319904/|title=Estonia v Faroe Islands game report|date=8 June 2024}}</ref>

'''Louis Paul Jackson''' (born 18 September 2005) is a professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]]. 

== Club career ==
Born in [[Oldham]], but brought up in [[Trafford]], Jackson became a season-ticket holder at [[Manchester United]] at five years-old. He joined the Manchester United academy at ten years-old, and at the age of 15, he became the youngest player to ever feature for the club's under-23 team. He was part of the United youth side that won the [[FA Youth Cup]] in 2022. In October 2022, he signed his first professional contract with the club.<ref>{{cite web|date=11 October 2022|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/man-united-louis-jackson-contract-25229489|first=Richard|last=Fay|accessdate=29 September 2023|title= Manchester United youngster mentored by Darren Fletcher signs professional contract|website=Manchester Evening News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/player/_/id/349735/louis-jackson|title=Louis Jackson - Manchester United U21 Defender - ESPN (UK)|website=ESPN}}</ref> Jackson was first named on the bench for the senior team in the semi-finals of the [[2023–24 FA Cup|23–24 FA Cup]] against [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/live/football/68650698?page=16|title=FA Cup LIVE: Coventry vs Man Utd score, radio commentary & updates from Wembley semi-final|work=BBC Sport }}</ref> Although he was also named on the substitutes bench against [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]], [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]], and [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] in the [[Premier League]] later that season,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/match-report-from-man-utd-v-sheffield-united-in-the-premier-league-24-april-2024|title=Manchester United 4 Sheffield United 2|website=www.manutd.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/match-report-man-utd-vs-burnley-in-the-premier-league-27th-april-2024|title=Match report: United 1 Burnley 1|website=www.manutd.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/13126994/crystal-palace-4-0-man-utd-erik-ten-hags-side-humiliated-as-michael-olise-inspires-hosts-to-rout|title=Crystal Palace 4-0 Man Utd: Erik ten Hag's side humiliated as Michael Olise inspires hosts to rout|website=Sky Sports}}</ref> Jackson is yet to make his senior debut.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/manutd-youngster-fa-cup-squad-32635266|title=Ten Hag promotes unknown Man Utd youngster to first team for FA Cup semi-final|first=Samuel|last=Meade|date=April 20, 2024|website=The Mirror}}</ref>

In February 2025, he joined [[EFL League Two]] side [[Tranmere Rovers F.C.|Tranmere Rovers]] on loan for the rest of the 2024–25 season, but never made an appearance for the club.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/manchester-united-agree-unexpected-double-30928768.amp|website=Manchester Evening News|accessdate=4 February 2025|title= Manchester United agree unexpected double-transfer on deadline day|first=Steven|last=Railston|date=4 February 2025}}</ref>

In August 2025, he joined [[National League (division)|National League]] side [[Solihull Moors F.C.|Solihull Moors]] on loan for the rest of the 2025–26 season.

On 30 August 2026, Jackson moved from Manchester United to [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[St Mirren F.C.]] on a permanent deal.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Marshall |first=Adam |title=Jackson completes Scottish move {{!}} Manchester United |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/jackson-completes-scottish-move-to-st-mirren |access-date=2026-08-31 |website=www.manutd.com |language=en}}</ref>

== International career ==

Born in [[Oldham]], England, Jackson has represented both [[England national football team|England]] and [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] at youth level.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Coombs |first=Dan |date=2023-01-01 |title=Manchester United talents to watch in 2023: Louis Jackson |url=https://www.unitedinfocus.com/academy/manchester-united-talents-to-watch-in-2023-louis-jackson/#:~:text=Louis%20Jackson%20international%20status&text=Jackson%20was%20born%20in%20England,Scotland%20squads%20at%20under-17s |access-date=2024-12-13 |website=United In Focus |language=en-GB}}</ref> He was handed his international debut by [[Omer Riza]], the [[England national under-16 football team|England U16]] coach at the time, in an U16 friendly game against Northern Ireland that England won 6–0.<ref>{{Cite web |title=England U16 vs. Northern Ireland U16 - 3 June 2021 - Soccerway |url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2021/06/03/world/under-16-friendlies/england-u16/northern-ireland-u16/3511107/ |website=int.soccerway.com}}</ref> Despite that, he has since opted to represent Scotland at U17, U18, and U19 levels. Jackson currently plays for Scotland U19s. He scored his first international goal in a 3–1 win over Andorra U19 in the 2023–2024 [[UEFA European Under-19 Championship|UEFA Euro U19 Championship]] Qualifiers, on the 18 November 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Scotland - Andorra 3:1 |url=https://www.flashscore.com/match/042C4ste/#/match-summary/match-summary |website=www.flashscore.com}}</ref>

== Style of play ==
Jackson has been described as a "calm and composed" defender.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://thepeoplesperson.com/2024/04/20/louis-jackson-named-in-manchester-united-squad-for-fa-cup-semifinal-vs-coventry-279120/|title=Mason Mount and Sofyan Amrabat injury issues plunge Man United into crisis, Louis Jackson called up|first=Vatsal|last=Gupta|date=April 20, 2024}}</ref>
