'''Ashley Stephen Thomas Hay''' (born 10 July 2003) is an English professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for {{Scottish football updater|Dundee}} club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].

Hay is a product of the [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]] [[Football academy|academy]] and began his senior career in [[non-League football]] in 2020. He transferred to [[Brentford F.C. Reserves and Academy#Relaunch (2016%E2%80%93present)|Brentford B]] in 2023 and played his first professional senior football on [[Loan (sports)|loan]] at [[Cheltenham Town F.C.|Cheltenham Town]].

== Career ==

=== Non-League football ===
A [[Forward (association football)|forward]], Hay began his career with spells in the [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]] [[Football academy|academy]], the [[Hitchin Town F.C.|Hitchin Town]] youth system and with [[Letchworth Garden City Eagles F.C.|Letchworth Garden City Eagles]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 November 2022 |title=Heading South… Sports Take On Hitchin |url=https://mickleoverfc.com/heading-south-sports-take-on-hitchin/ |access-date=2 September 2023 |website=Mickleover Football Club |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=25 January 2019 |title=Weekly Bulletin From Roy |url=https://hitchintownfc.club/weekly-bulletin-from-roy-35/ |access-date=2 September 2023 |website=Hitchin Town FC |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name="SignsBaldock">{{Cite web |title=Confirmed Signings Part 10 |url=https://www.baldocktownfc.com/news/confirmed-signings-part-10-2562682.html |access-date=2 September 2023 |website=www.baldocktownfc.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Whitney" /> He began his senior career with [[Spartan South Midlands Football League|Spartan South Midlands League]] Premier Division club [[Baldock Town F.C.|Baldock Town]] in August 2020.<ref name="SignsBaldock" /> Hay scored 35 goals in 64 appearances,<ref name="AylesburyUnitedProfile">{{Cite web |title=Ashley Hay {{!}} Player Profile |url=https://www.aylesburyunitedarchive.com/player/ashley-hay |access-date=1 September 2023 |website=Aylesbury United Archive}}</ref> prior to moving up a step to transfer to [[Southern Football League|Southern League]] Premier Division Central club [[Biggleswade Town F.C.|Biggleswade Town]] in July 2022.<ref name="Whitney">{{Cite web |last=Whitney |first=Steve |title=O'Keefe Adds Three More to His Group |url=https://southern-football-league.co.uk/news/131824/OKeefe-Adds-Three-More-to-His-Group |access-date=2 September 2023}}</ref> Following a short spell in which he scored one goal in seven appearances,<ref name="AylesburyUnitedProfile" /> Hay transferred across the division to return to Hitchin Town in September 2022.<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1573659528540946434 |user=HitchinTownFC |title=✍️ {{!}} Ashley Hay breaking news!! We are delighted to welcome striker @ashleyhay_10 from @Biggleswade1874. Ashley goes straight into today's squad. 💛💚}}</ref> He scored 11 goals in 39 appearances during a [[2022–23 Southern Football League|2022–23]] season in which he was voted the club's Supporters' Player of the Year.<ref name="AylesburyUnitedProfile" /><ref name="SPOTY" /> Shortly after re-signing for the [[2023–24 Southern Football League|2023–24]] season,<ref name="SPOTY" /> Hay departed the club.<ref name="SignsBrentford" />

=== Brentford ===
On 31 August 2023, following a successful trial, Hay transferred to the [[Brentford F.C. Reserves and Academy#Relaunch (2016%E2%80%93present)|B team]] at [[Premier League]] club [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]].<ref name="SignsBrentford">{{Cite web |title=Ashley Hay signs for Brentford B |url=https://www.brentfordfc.com/en/news/article/brentford-b-team-ashley-hay-signs-for-brentford-b |access-date=1 September 2023 |website=www.brentfordfc.com |language=en-gb}}</ref> He signed a contract running until January 2024 and later signed an extension until the end of the 2023–24 season.<ref name="SignsBrentford" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=12 January 2024 |title=Weekly Bulletin – 12th January |url=https://hitchintownfc.club/weekly-bulletin-12th-january/ |access-date=19 January 2024 |website=Hitchin Town FC |language=en-GB}}</ref> Hay finished the 2023–24 season tied with [[Iwan Morgan]] as the B team's leading goalscorer, with 9 goals.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ashley Hay: Always Improving |url=https://www.brentfordfc.com/en/news/article/brentford-b-team-ashley-hay-interview- |access-date=9 July 2024 |website=www.brentfordfc.com |language=en-gb}}</ref> He also [[Captain (association football)|captained]] the team on occasion during the season.<ref name="Tabuteau">{{Cite web |last=Tabuteau |first=Sam |title=Ashley Hay looking to build on whirlwind first year at Brentford |url=https://hounslowherald.com/ashley-hay-looking-to-build-on-whirlwind-first-year-at-brentford-p25854-308.htm |access-date=3 November 2024 |website=hounslowherald.com}}</ref> Hay signed a new two-year contract, with the option of a further year, in June 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brentford academy confirm summer departures and extensions |url=https://www.brentfordfc.com/en/news/article/brentford-b-team-brentford-academy-departures-and-extensions-summer-2024 |access-date=1 June 2024 |website=www.brentfordfc.com |language=en-gb}}</ref>

Following a first team [[Friendly match|friendly]] appearance and 14 goals in 15 appearances for the B team during the first half of the 2024–25 season,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brentford 0 QPR 0: Minutes for first-team players in Jersey Road friendly |url=https://www.brentfordfc.com/en/news/article/first-team-brentford-0-queens-park-rangers-0-friendly |access-date=5 September 2024 |website=www.brentfordfc.com |language=en-gb}}</ref> Hay joined [[EFL League Two|League Two]] club [[Cheltenham Town F.C.|Cheltenham Town]] on [[Loan (sports)|loan]] for the remainder of [[2024–25 Cheltenham Town F.C. season|the season]] on 1 January 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ashley Hay joins Cheltenham Town on loan |url=https://www.brentfordfc.com/en/news/article/brentford-b-team-ashley-hay-cheltenham-town-loan-transfer |access-date=1 January 2025 |website=www.brentfordfc.com |language=en-gb}}</ref> He made 23 appearances and scored three goals during his spell.<ref name="2024-25" /> Following the expiry of the loan, Hay played in the remainder of Brentford B's season and was part of the [[2024–25 Professional U21 Development League#Professional Development League|2024–25 Professional Development League]]-winning squad.<ref name="LeavesBrentford">{{Cite web |title=Ashley Hay makes permanent switch to Dundee |url=https://www.brentfordfc.com/en/news/article/brentford-b-team-ashley-hay-makes-permanent-switch-dundee |access-date=4 July 2025 |website=Brentford FC |language=en-gb}}</ref> He transferred out of the club in July 2025.<ref name="LeavesBrentford" />

=== Dundee ===
On 4 July 2025, Hay transferred to [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] and signed a two-year contract,<ref>{{Cite web |date=4 July 2025 |title=Hay is a Dee! |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/hay-signs/ |access-date=4 July 2025 |website=Dundee Football Club – Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{Cite web |date=6 July 2025 |title=Dundee boss Steven Pressley gives transfer update as he hails Ashley Hay signing |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/5284152/dundee-steven-pressley-transfer-update-ashley-hay/ |access-date=1 August 2025 |website=The Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref> The move reunited him with head coach [[Steven Pressley]], formerly Head of Individual Development at Brentford.<ref name="LeavesBrentford" /> On 30 December 2025, Hay scored his first goal for the club in a home win over [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dundee 2-1 Kilmarnock: Dundee take a significant step towards Scottish Premiership safety |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c4g51rq5lmjt |access-date=30 December 2025 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
While a [[Non-League football|non-League]] footballer, Hay worked in [[McDonald's]] and undertook an [[apprenticeship]] as a [[plumber]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=14 August 2024 |title=Brentford news: Youngsters Ashley Hay and Benjamin Arthur on their football journeys |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/clygnznmem4o |access-date=15 August 2024 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> While a Brentford player, he [[Roommate|shared accommodation]] with teammate [[Benjamin Arthur (footballer)|Benjamin Arthur]].<ref name="Tabuteau" />

'''Eseosa Joshua Sule''' (born 1 April 2006) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].

==Club career==
===West Bromwich Albion===
Sule started his career with [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] before joining English side [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] in January 2023.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.expressandstar.com/sport/2025/07/08/west-brom-striker-focussed-as-he-heads-to-motherwell-on-loan/ |title=West Brom 14 goal striker issues focussed message after SPL loan move confirmed |website=Express & Star |date=8 July 2025 |access-date=9 July 2025}}</ref> On 13 May 2023, he signed his first professional contract with the club.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.wba.co.uk/news/eseosa-sule-signs-first-professional-deal-albion |title=Eseosa Sule signs first professional deal at Albion |publisher=West Bromwich Albion F.C. |date=13 May 2023 |access-date=9 July 2025}}</ref> On 13 August 2024, he made his professional debut for West Bromwich Albion in a 2–1 defeat to [[Fleetwood Town F.C.|Fleetwood Town]] in the [[EFL Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/match/_/gameId/710322/west-bromwich-albion-fleetwood-town |title=Fleetwood Town 2–1 West Bromwich Albion |website=ESPN |date=13 August 2024 |access-date=9 July 2025}}</ref> On 3 July 2025, he signed a new two-year contract with the club.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.wba.co.uk/news/seven-young-professionals-extend-albion-stays |title=Seven young professionals extend Albion stays |publisher=West Bromwich Albion F.C. |date=3 July 2025 |access-date=9 July 2025}}</ref>

On 7 July 2025, Sule joined [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2025/07/07/eseosa-sule-arrives-on-loan/ |title=Eseosa Sule arrives on loan |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |date=7 July 2025 |access-date=8 July 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c9qxe0g000yo |title=Motherwell sign Eseosa Sule on a season-long loan from West Brom |website=BBC Sport |date=7 July 2025 |access-date=8 July 2025}}</ref> He made his debut for the club on 12 July 2025, in a 2–2 draw with [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]] in the [[Scottish League Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/match/_/gameId/736181/motherwell-clyde |title=Clyde 2–2 Motherwell |website=ESPN |date=12 July 2025 |access-date=12 July 2025}}</ref> In August 2025, he returned to his parent club to recover from an injury sustained on loan, with the expectation of rejoining Motherwell once fit.<ref>{{cite web |title=Eseosa Sule injury update |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2025/08/06/eseosa-sule-injury-update/ |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |access-date=7 October 2025 |date=6 August 2025}}</ref> On 1 January 2026, he returned to West Bromwich Albion after his loan to Motherwell was ended early due to the thigh injury he sustained in August.<ref>{{cite web |title=Eseosa Sule returns to West Brom |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2026/01/01/eseosa-sule-returns-to-west-brom/ |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |access-date=1 January 2026 |date=1 January 2026}}</ref>

Sule made his league debut for West Bromwich Albion on 10 April 2026, featuring in a 0–0 draw with [[Millwall F.C.|Millwall]] in the [[EFL Championship|Championship]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c4gd520n6kpt |title=West Bromwich Albion 0–0 Millwall |website=BBC Sport |date=10 April 2026 |access-date=11 April 2026}}</ref>

===St Mirren===
On 14 July 2026, Sule signed with Scottish Premiership club [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] on a three-year contract for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.stmirren.com/news/eseosa-sule-signs |title=Eseosa Sule joins St Mirren on three-year deal |publisher=St Mirren F.C. |date=14 July 2026 |access-date=14 July 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-07-14 |title=St Mirren sign Eseosa Sule on permanent deal from West Brom |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cdx7xkwy2nyo |access-date=2026-07-14 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> He scored on his debut for the club on 21 July 2026, netting in a 4–3 win against [[East Kilbride F.C.|East Kilbride]] in the Scottish League Cup.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/clyv9v0g3ywt |title=St Mirren 4–3 East Kilbride |website=BBC Sport |date=21 July 2026 |access-date=21 July 2026}}</ref> He made his league debut on 1 August 2026, in a 2–0 win against [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c204ql8q4z4t |title=Falkirk 0–2 St Mirren |website=BBC Sport |date=1 August 2026 |access-date=1 August 2026}}</ref> He scored his first league goal on 17 October 2026, in a 3–1 defeat to [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cq62yj73kw4wt|title=Aberdeen 3–1 St Mirren|website=BBC Sport|date=17 October 2026|access-date=17 October 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
In November 2026, Sule received his first call-up to the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland U21]] side.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/en/news/scotland-under-21-squad-named-for-upcoming-friendlies|title=Scotland Under 21 Squad named for upcoming friendlies|publisher=Scottish FA|date=4 November 2026|access-date=4 November 2026}}</ref>

'''Samuel Antonio Ramos Linares''' (born 18 August 2000) is a Spanish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[central midfielder]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].

==Career==
Ramos was born in [[Santa Cruz de Tenerife]] and played in the [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]] academy. He played senior football for the [[UD Las Palmas C|third]] and [[UD Las Palmas Atlético|reserve teams]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=22 January 2024 |title=MFK Zemplín podpísal Ramosa |url=https://mfkzemplin.sk/mfk-zemplin-podpisal-ramosa/ |access-date=6 September 2025 |website=MFK Zemplín |language=sk}}</ref>

On 22 January 2024, it was announced that Ramos would be joining Slovak club [[MFK Zemplín Michalovce|Zemplín Michalovce]], signing a two-year contract.<ref name=":0" /> He made his professional debut for Zemplín Michalovce in a 2–1 loss against [[FK Železiarne Podbrezová|Železiarne Podbrezová]], coming on as a substitute for [[Martin Bednár]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=FK Železiarne Podbrezová - MFK Zemplín Michalovce {{!}} Detail zápasu |url=https://www.nikeliga.sk/zapas/2335-pod-mic |access-date=6 September 2025 |website=Niké liga}}</ref>He moved to St. Mirren in summer 2026.

'''Fraser Taylor''' (born 20 February 2003) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Midfielder (association football)|midfielder]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].

==Career==
===Early years and loans===
Fraser signed a professional contract with St Mirren after coming through the club's youth academy.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/4851-fraser-taylor-and-luke-kenny-agree-contract-extensions|title=Fraser Taylor and Luke Kenny agree contract extensions|website=www.stmirren.com}}</ref>
In July 2022, Taylor made his St Mirren debut coming off the bench in a 3–1 victory over [[Edinburgh City F.C.|Edinburgh City]] in the [[Scottish League Cup]] group stages.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stmirren.com/match-reports/4518-match-report-st-mirren-fc-edinburgh|title=Saints close out cup campaign with win|website=www.stmirren.com}}</ref>

In August 2023, Taylor signed a two-year contract extension until summer 2025.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/5058-fraser-taylor-and-kieran-offord-agree-new-contracts|title=Fraser Taylor and Kieran Offord agree new contracts|website=www.stmirren.com}}</ref> 

====Ballymena United (loan)====
In August 2023 Taylor joined [[NIFL Premiership]] side [[Ballymena United]] on a season long loan.<ref name="belfasttelegraph">{{Cite web|url=https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/sport/football/irish-league/ballymena-united-complete-loan-move-for-scottish-midfielder-after-impressing-in-st-mirren-friendly/a1747364507.html|title=Ballymena United complete loan move for Scottish midfielder after impressing in St Mirren friendly|date=2 August 2023|via=m.belfasttelegraph.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/in-your-area/renfrewshire/stephen-robinson-explains-loan-plan-30613161|title=Boss Robinson explains loan plan for St Mirren prospects Taylor and Offord|date=2 August 2023|website=Daily Record}}</ref>

Taylor won Ballymena's Player of the Year award, after helping the club avoid relegation.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newsletter.co.uk/sport/football/northern-ireland/former-ballymena-united-favourite-ticks-off-scottish-premiership-milestone-against-champions-celtic-5254791|title=Former Ballymena United favourite ticks off Scottish Premiership milestone against champions Celtic|date=3 August 2025|website=Belfast News Letter}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/sport/football/irish-league/scottish-youngsters-should-jump-at-irish-league-loan-chance-says-st-mirrens-fraser-taylor/a1585563232.html|title=Scottish youngsters should jump at Irish League loan chance, says St Mirren’s Fraser Taylor|date=31 May 2024|via=m.belfasttelegraph.co.uk}}</ref>

====Arbroath (loan)====
Taylor joined [[Scottish League One]] side [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] on a season long loan in September 2024.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/5582-fraser-taylor-heads-to-arbroath-on-loan|title=Fraser Taylor heads to Arbroath on loan|website=www.stmirren.com}}</ref> Taylor scored his first goal for Arbroath, scoring the winner in a 1–0 home victory over [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c4g7xlzj6ekt|title=Arbroath vs Stenhousemuir: Scottish League One|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

Following winning the Scottish League One title with Arbroath, Fraser won the PFA Scottish League One Player of the Year for the 2024–2025 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/fraser-taylor-claims-l1-prize|title=Fraser Taylor claims L1 prize {{pipe}} SPFL|website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref>

After returning from his loan spell with Arbroath, Taylor signed a one-year contract extension with St Mirren in May 2025.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/5839-here-to-stay-fraser-taylor-under-contract-for-2025-26|title=Here to Stay // Fraser Taylor under contract for 2025/26|website=www.stmirren.com}}</ref>

====Partick Thistle (loan)====
On 29 January 2026, Taylor joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/new-signing-fraser-taylor-29th-january-2026/|title=New Signing: Fraser Taylor – 29th January 2026|website=Partick Thistle FC}}</ref> Taylor made his Thistle debut the following day, coming off the bench in a 2–2 draw with [[St Johnstone]].<ref name="co.uk">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c5yxwlyw3gwt|title=St Johnstone vs Partick Thistle: Scottish Championship video stream & live text commentary - BBC Sport|website=bbc.co.uk|access-date=31 January 2026}}</ref>

===St Mirren breakthrough===

Upon returning from his Partick Thistle loan, Taylor signed a two-year contract extension with St. Mirren, committing himself to the club until 2028.<ref>{{cite news |title=St Mirren: Contract extension marks 'fresh start' for Fraser Taylor |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/clyx04937j6o |access-date=21 October 2026 |work=BBC Sport |date=30 June 2026}}</ref> Beginning to make regular appearances for his boyhood club in the [[2026–27 St Mirren F.C. season|2026–27 season]], he scored his debut goal for the club ina 1–0 victory over [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] on 3 September 2026.<ref>{{cite news |title=Kilmarnock 0-1 St Mirren: Killie remain without a point after loss to high-flying visitors |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/13579788/kilmarnock-0-1-st-mirren-killie-remain-without-a-point-after-loss-to-high-flying-visitors |access-date=21 October 2026 |work=Sky Sports |date=3 September 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Taylor grew up supporting [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]], the club he would begin his professional career with.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/24522183.st-mirren-starlet-taylor-dream-euro-delivery-boyhood-club/|title=Boyhood Buddie Fraser Taylor on 'amazing' St Mirren memories despite Euro exit|date=16 August 2024|website=The Herald}}</ref>
